sentences.zh: 元稹，字微之，河南人。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhen, style name Weizhi, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen, whose courtesy name was Weizhi, came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 後魏昭成皇帝，稹十代祖也。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaocheng of Later Wei was Zhen's tenth-generation ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaocheng of the Northern Wei was his tenth-generation forebear.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書、昌平公巖，六代祖也。

translations.literal: Yan, Minister of War and Duke of Changping, was his sixth-generation ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor was Yan, who had served as Minister of War and been enfeoffed as Duke of Changping.

sentences.zh: 曾祖延景，岐州參軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yanjing was a staff officer in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yanjing had held the post of military aide in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖悱，南頓丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fei was magistrate of Nandun.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fei had served as magistrate of Nandun.

sentences.zh: 父寬，比部郎中、舒王府長史，以稹貴，贈左僕射。

translations.literal: His father Kuan was a director in the Ministry of Justice and senior administrator of the Prince of Shu's household; because of Zhen's eminence, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kuan had been a director in the Ministry of Justice and senior administrator of the Prince of Shu's household; when Zhen rose to prominence, Kuan was posthumously honored as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 稹八歲喪父。

translations.literal: Zhen lost his father at the age of eight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was only eight when his father died.

sentences.zh: 其母鄭夫人，賢明婦人也；

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Zheng, was a wise and worthy woman;
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Zheng, was a woman of wisdom and virtue;

sentences.zh: 家貧，為稹自授書，教之書學。

translations.literal: The family was poor; she personally taught Zhen the classics and instructed him in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Though the household was poor, she taught him the classics herself and trained him in letters.

sentences.zh: 稹九歲能屬文。

translations.literal: At nine Zhen could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: By the age of nine he could already compose prose.

sentences.zh: 十五兩經擢第。

translations.literal: At fifteen he passed the examinations in both Classics.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he passed the civil service examinations in both of the Confucian Classics.

sentences.zh: 二十四調判入第四等，授秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: At twenty-four his provincial assessment placed him in the fourth grade, and he was appointed proofreader in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-four he qualified at the fourth grade in the provincial assessment and was made a proofreader in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 二十八應制舉才識兼茂、明於體用科，登第者十八人，稹為第一，元和元年四月也。

translations.literal: At twenty-eight he entered the special examination for men of outstanding talent and practical understanding; of the eighteen who passed, Zhen ranked first, in the fourth month of the first year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-eight he sat for the special "Outstanding Talent and Practical Understanding" examination; eighteen candidates passed, and Zhen took first place—in April of the first year of Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 制下，除右拾遺。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, he was appointed Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment edict followed, and he was named Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 稹性鋒銳，見事風生。

translations.literal: Zhen's nature was sharp; he seized on affairs as swiftly as wind arises.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was quick and incisive by nature, grasping affairs the moment they arose.

sentences.zh: 既居諫垣，不欲碌碌自滯，事無不言，即日上疏論諫職。

translations.literal: Once he held a remonstrance post, he did not wish to linger in mediocrity; nothing passed without his speaking out, and that very day he submitted a memorial on the duties of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Once installed in the remonstrance bureau, he refused to settle into routine obscurity; he spoke up on every matter and that very day submitted a memorial on the proper conduct of remonstrance officials.

sentences.zh: 又以前時王叔文、王伾以猥褻待詔，蒙幸太子，永貞之際，大撓朝政。

translations.literal: He also noted that earlier Wang Shuwen and Wang Pi, though base men awaiting summons at court, had won the crown prince's favor and during the Yongzhen era had greatly disrupted state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also recalled how Wang Shuwen and Wang Pi—men of coarse character who had lingered at court awaiting summons—had won the crown prince's favor and, during the Yongzhen regency, had thrown government into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 是以訓導太子宮官，宜選正人。

translations.literal: Therefore those who instruct and guide the crown prince's household officials ought to be upright men.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason he argued that those who instructed the crown prince's household should be men of upright character.

sentences.zh: 乃獻《教本書》曰：臣伏見陛下降明詔，修廢學，增胄子，選司成。

translations.literal: He therefore presented a "Book on the Foundations of Instruction," which read: This subject humbly sees that Your Majesty has issued a bright edict to restore abandoned schools, increase the crown prince's students, and select a director of studies.
translations.idiomatic: He accordingly submitted his "Book on the Foundations of Instruction," which began: This subject humbly observes that Your Majesty has issued a bright edict to restore abandoned schools, increase the crown prince's students, and select a director of studies.

sentences.zh: 大哉，堯之為君，伯夷典禮，夔教胄子之深旨也！

translations.literal: How great! When Yao was ruler, Boyi supervised rites and Kui taught the crown prince's students—the deep meaning of this!
translations.idiomatic: How great! When Yao was ruler, Boyi supervised the rites and Kui taught the crown prince's students—that is the deep meaning of this!

sentences.zh: 然而事有萬萬於此者，臣敢冒昧殊死而言之。

translations.literal: However, there are matters ten thousand times greater than this; this subject dares speak of them presumptuously, at the risk of death.
translations.idiomatic: Yet there are matters ten thousand times greater than this, and this subject dares speak of them presumptuously, at the risk of death.

sentences.zh: 臣聞諸賈生曰：「三代之君，仁且久者，教之然也。」

translations.literal: This subject has heard Jia Yi say: "The rulers of the Three Dynasties who were benevolent and long-lasting were so because of instruction."
translations.idiomatic: This subject has heard Jia Yi say: "The rulers of the Three Dynasties who were benevolent and long-lasting were so because of instruction."

sentences.zh: 誠哉是言！

translations.literal: Truly this saying!
translations.idiomatic: How true that saying is!

sentences.zh: 且夫周成王，人之中才也，近管、蔡則讒入，有周、召則義聞，豈可謂天聰明哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, King Cheng of Zhou was a man of middling talent; near Guan and Cai, slander entered; with the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao, righteousness was heard—how can one say he was heaven-endowed with brilliance?
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng of Zhou, moreover, was a man of middling talent: near Guan and Cai, slander entered; with the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao, righteousness was heard. How can one say he was heaven-endowed with brilliance?

sentences.zh: 然而克終於道者，得不謂教之然耶？

translations.literal: Yet because he was able to complete the Way to the end, must one not say it was because of instruction?
translations.idiomatic: Yet because he was able to complete the Way to the end, must one not say it was because of instruction?

sentences.zh: 俾伯禽、唐叔與之遊，《禮》、《樂》、《詩》、《書》為之習，目不得閱淫艷妖誘之色，耳不得聞優笑淩亂之音，口不得習操斷擊博之書，居不得近容順陰邪之黨，遊不得縱追禽逐獸之樂，玩不得有遐異僻絕之珍。

translations.literal: He was made to associate with Bo Qin and Uncle Tang; the Rites, Music, Poetry, and Documents were made his studies; his eyes were not allowed to view lewd, gaudy, and seductive colors; his ears were not allowed to hear the sounds of jesters' laughter and disorderly music; his mouth was not allowed to practice the arts of manipulation, gambling, and gaming; in residence he was not allowed to approach a party of flatterers and sinister men; in recreation he was not allowed to indulge in the pleasure of chasing birds and pursuing beasts; in playthings he was not allowed to possess rare and exotic treasures from distant lands.
translations.idiomatic: He was made to associate with Bo Qin and Uncle Tang; the Rites, Music, Poetry, and Documents were made his studies. His eyes were not allowed to view lewd and seductive sights; his ears were not allowed to hear jesters' laughter and disorderly music; his mouth was not allowed to practice manipulation, gambling, and gaming; in residence he was not allowed to approach flatterers and sinister men; in recreation he was not allowed to indulge in chasing birds and pursuing beasts; in playthings he was not allowed to possess rare exotic treasures from distant lands.

sentences.zh: 凡此數者，非謂備之於前而不為也，亦將不得見之矣。

translations.literal: Of all these matters, it is not that they are prepared before him yet he does not do them; rather, he will not even be allowed to see them.
translations.idiomatic: Of all these matters, it is not that they are set before him yet he refrains from them; rather, he will not even be allowed to see them.

sentences.zh: 及其長而為君也，血氣既定，遊習既成，雖有放心快己之事日陳於前，固不能奪已成之習、已定之心矣。

translations.literal: When he grew up and became ruler, his vital energies were already settled and his habits of association already formed; even if matters that indulge the heart and please the self were daily set before him, they could not wrest away habits already formed and a heart already settled.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up and became ruler, his vital energies were already settled and his habits of association already formed. Even if indulgences that pleased himself were daily set before him, they could not wrest away habits already formed and a heart already settled.

sentences.zh: 則彼忠直道德之言，固吾之所習聞也，陳之者有以諭焉；

translations.literal: Then those words of loyalty, uprightness, and moral virtue were what he was accustomed to hearing; when they were set forth, there was means to instruct him;
translations.idiomatic: Then words of loyalty, uprightness, and moral virtue were what he was accustomed to hearing; when they were set forth, there was means to instruct him;

sentences.zh: 彼庸佞違道之說，固吾之所積懼也，諂之者有以辨焉。

translations.literal: those base and fawning words that violate the Way were what he had long accumulated fear of; when flattery was offered, there was means to distinguish it.
translations.idiomatic: base and fawning words that violated the Way were what he had long accumulated fear of; when flattery was offered, there was means to distinguish it.

sentences.zh: 人之情，莫不欲耀其所能而黨其所近；

translations.literal: In human disposition, there is none who does not wish to display what he is capable of and take as his party those he is close to;
translations.idiomatic: In human nature, everyone wishes to display what he is capable of and take as his party those he is close to;

sentences.zh: 茍將得志，則必快其所蘊矣。

translations.literal: if he is about to achieve his aim, he will surely give free rein to what he harbors within.
translations.idiomatic: if he is about to achieve his aim, he will surely give free rein to what he harbors within.

sentences.zh: 物之性亦然。

translations.literal: The nature of things is likewise so.
translations.idiomatic: The nature of things is likewise so.

sentences.zh: 是以魚得水而遊，馬逸駕而走，鳥得風而翔，火得薪而熾。

translations.literal: Thus fish obtain water and swim; horses loose the reins and run; birds obtain wind and soar; fire obtains fuel and blazes.
translations.idiomatic: Thus fish obtain water and swim; horses loose the reins and run; birds obtain wind and soar; fire obtains fuel and blazes.

sentences.zh: 此皆物之快其所蘊也。

translations.literal: All these are things giving free rein to what they harbor within.
translations.idiomatic: All these are instances of things giving free rein to what they harbor within.

sentences.zh: 今夫成王所蘊道德也，所近聖賢也。

translations.literal: Now what King Cheng harbored within was moral virtue; those he was close to were sages and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: What King Cheng harbored within was moral virtue; those he was close to were sages and worthies.

sentences.zh: 是以舉其近，則周公左而召公右，伯禽魯而太公齊。

translations.literal: Thus when he raised up those close to him, the Duke of Zhou was at his left and the Duke of Shao at his right; Bo Qin was in Lu and Grand Duke Wang in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when he raised up those close to him, the Duke of Zhou was at his left and the Duke of Shao at his right; Bo Qin ruled Lu and Grand Duke Wang ruled Qi.

sentences.zh: 快其蘊，則興禮樂而朝諸侯，措刑罰而美教化。

translations.literal: Giving free rein to what he harbored within, he raised rites and music and received the feudal lords in audience, set aside punishments, and glorified instruction and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Giving free rein to what he harbored within, he raised rites and music and received the feudal lords in audience, set aside punishments, and glorified instruction and transformation.

sentences.zh: 教之至也，可不謂信然哉！

translations.literal: Instruction at its utmost—can one not call this truly so!
translations.idiomatic: Instruction at its utmost—can one not call this truly so!

sentences.zh: 及夫秦則不然。

translations.literal: But when it came to Qin, it was not so.
translations.idiomatic: But when it came to Qin, it was not so.

sentences.zh: 滅先王之學，曰將以愚天下；

translations.literal: It abolished the learning of former kings, saying it would thereby make all under Heaven stupid;
translations.idiomatic: It abolished the learning of former kings, saying it would thereby keep all under Heaven ignorant;

sentences.zh: 黜師保之位，曰將以明君臣。

translations.literal: it dismissed the posts of teacher and protector, saying it would thereby clarify ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: it dismissed the posts of teacher and protector, saying it would thereby clarify the roles of ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 胡亥之生也，《詩》、《書》不得聞，聖賢不得近。

translations.literal: When Huhai was born, he was not allowed to hear the Poetry and Documents, and sages and worthies were not allowed near him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huhai was born, he was not allowed to hear the Poetry and Documents, and sages and worthies were not allowed near him.

sentences.zh: 彼趙高者，詐宦之戮人也；

translations.literal: That Zhao Gao was a castrated man of the fraudulent eunuch class;
translations.idiomatic: That Zhao Gao was a castrated man of the fraudulent eunuch class;

sentences.zh: 而傅之以殘忍戕賊之術，且曰恣睢天下以為貴，莫見其面以為尊。

translations.literal: yet he was made his tutor in cruel and murderous arts, and it was said that to act wantonly over all under Heaven was esteemed, and that not seeing his face was honor.
translations.idiomatic: yet he was made his tutor in cruel and murderous arts, and it was said that to act wantonly over all under Heaven was esteemed, and that not seeing his face was honor.

sentences.zh: 是以天下之人人未盡愚，而胡亥固已不能分獸畜矣。

translations.literal: Thus though the people of all under Heaven were not yet entirely stupid, Huhai was already unable to distinguish beasts from livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Thus though the people of all under Heaven were not yet entirely ignorant, Huhai was already unable to distinguish beasts from livestock.

sentences.zh: 趙高之威懾天下，而胡亥固已自幽於深宮矣。

translations.literal: Zhao Gao's authority awed all under Heaven, and Huhai was already shut away in the deep palace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao's authority awed all under Heaven, and Huhai was already shut away in the deep palace.

sentences.zh: 彼李斯，秦之寵丞相也。

translations.literal: That Li Si was Qin's favored chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Si was Qin's favored chancellor.

sentences.zh: 因讒冤死，無所自明，而況於疏遠之臣庶乎！

translations.literal: Because of slander he died unjustly with no means to clear himself—how much more so for distant and lowly ministers and commoners!
translations.idiomatic: Because of slander he died unjustly with no means to clear himself—how much more so for distant and lowly ministers and commoners!

sentences.zh: 若然，則秦之亡有以致之也。

translations.literal: If it was so, then Qin's perishing had causes that brought it about.
translations.idiomatic: If it was so, then Qin's fall had causes that brought it about.

sentences.zh: 漢高承之以兵革，漢文守之以廉謹，卒不能蘇復大訓。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han took it over by arms, and Emperor Wen guarded it with integrity and caution, yet in the end could not revive the great instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han took it over by arms, and Emperor Wen guarded it with integrity and caution, yet in the end could not revive the great instruction.

sentences.zh: 是以景、武、昭、宣，天資甚美，才可以免禍亂；

translations.literal: Thus Jing, Wu, Zhao, and Xuan, with very fine natural endowments, were able by their talent to escape calamity and disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Emperors Jing, Wu, Zhao, and Xuan, with very fine natural endowments, were able by their talent to escape calamity and disorder;

sentences.zh: 哀、平之間，則不能虞篡弒矣。

translations.literal: between Ai and Ping, they could not guard against usurpation and regicide.
translations.idiomatic: but between Emperors Ai and Ping, they could not guard against usurpation and regicide.

sentences.zh: 然而惠帝廢易之際，猶賴羽翼以勝邪心。

translations.literal: Yet at the time when Emperor Hui was deposed and replaced, they still relied on supporting wings to overcome wicked hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Emperor Hui was deposed and replaced, they still relied on supporting ministers to overcome wicked hearts.

sentences.zh: 是後有國之君，議教化者，莫不以興廉舉孝、設學崇儒為意，曾不知教化之不行，自貴始。

translations.literal: After this, rulers who possessed the state, when discussing instruction and transformation, all took promoting integrity and recommending filial piety, establishing schools and honoring Confucianism as their intent—yet they never knew that instruction and transformation did not prevail because it began with the honored.
translations.idiomatic: After this, rulers who possessed the state, when discussing instruction and transformation, all took promoting integrity and recommending filial piety, establishing schools and honoring Confucianism as their intent—yet they never knew that instruction failed because it began with the honored rather than the humble.

sentences.zh: 略其貴者，教其賤者，無乃鄰於倒置乎？

translations.literal: Neglecting the honored and instructing the lowly—is this not close to turning things upside down?
translations.idiomatic: Neglecting the honored and instructing only the lowly—is this not close to turning things upside down?

sentences.zh: 洎我太宗文皇帝之在籓邸，以至於為太子也，選知道德者十八人與之遊習。

translations.literal: Down to when our Emperor Taizong was in the princely residence, and up to when he became crown prince, he selected eighteen men who understood moral virtue to associate and study with him.
translations.idiomatic: When our Emperor Taizong was in the princely residence, and up to when he became crown prince, he selected eighteen men who understood moral virtue to associate and study with him.

sentences.zh: 即位之後，雖遊宴飲食之間，若十八人者，實在其中。

translations.literal: After he ascended the throne, even amid feasting and dining, those eighteen men were truly among them.
translations.idiomatic: After he ascended the throne, even amid feasting and dining, those eighteen men were truly present.

sentences.zh: 上失無不言，下情無不達。

translations.literal: Of the ruler's faults, none went unspoken; of sentiments below, none went unreached.
translations.idiomatic: None of the ruler's faults went unspoken; none of the sentiments below went unreached.

sentences.zh: 不四三年而名高盛古，豈一日二日而致是乎？

translations.literal: In less than four or three years his fame rose above the ancients—could one or two days have brought this about?
translations.idiomatic: In less than three or four years his fame rose above the ancients—could one or two days have brought this about?

sentences.zh: 遊習之漸也！

translations.literal: It was the gradual effect of association and habit!
translations.idiomatic: It was the gradual effect of association and habit!

sentences.zh: 貞觀已還，師傅皆宰相兼領，其餘宮僚，亦甚重焉。

translations.literal: From the Zhenguan era onward, teachers and tutors were all concurrently held by chancellors, and the other palace officials were also greatly honored.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhenguan era onward, teachers and tutors were all concurrently held by chancellors, and the other palace officials were also greatly honored.

sentences.zh: 馬周以位高恨不得為司議郎，此其驗也。

translations.literal: Ma Zhou, because his rank was high, regretted that he could not be a director of deliberation—this is proof of it.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhou, because his rank was high, regretted that he could not serve as director of deliberation—this is proof of it.

sentences.zh: 文皇之後，漸疏賤之。

translations.literal: After Emperor Taizong, they were gradually treated with distance and contempt.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Taizong, they were gradually treated with distance and contempt.

sentences.zh: 用至母後臨朝，翦棄王室。

translations.literal: Their use reached the point where the empress dowager held court and the royal house was pruned and cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Matters reached the point where the empress dowager held court and the royal house was pruned and cast aside.

sentences.zh: 當中、睿二聖勤勞之際，雖有骨鯁敢言之士，既不得在調護保安之職，終不能吐扶衛之一辭。

translations.literal: At the time when the two sage emperors Zhongzong and Ruizong labored diligently, though there were men of firm bone and gills who dared speak, since they could not hold posts of tending, protecting, and securing, in the end they could not utter a single word of support and defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the two sage emperors Zhongzong and Ruizong labored diligently, though there were outspoken men of firm principle, since they could not hold posts of tending, protecting, and securing the heir, in the end they could not utter a single word of support and defense.

sentences.zh: 而令醫匠安金藏剖腹以明之，豈不大哀也耶？

translations.literal: Yet a physician-craftsman, An Jinzang, was made to cut open his belly to prove it—is this not great sorrow!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the physician An Jinzang was made to cut open his belly to prove his loyalty—is this not great sorrow!

sentences.zh: 兵興已來，茲弊尤甚。

translations.literal: Since military campaigns arose, this abuse has been especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Since military campaigns arose, this abuse has been especially severe.

sentences.zh: 師資保傅之官，非疾廢眊聵不任事者為之，即休戎罷帥不知書者處之。

translations.literal: The offices of teacher, protector, and tutor were filled either by men who were sick, disabled, dim-sighted, and deaf and unfit for duties, or by retired soldiers and dismissed generals who did not know books.
translations.idiomatic: The offices of teacher, protector, and tutor were filled either by men who were sick, disabled, dim-sighted, and deaf and unfit for duty, or by retired soldiers and dismissed generals who could not read.

sentences.zh: 至於友諭贊議之徒，疏冗散賤之甚者，縉紳恥由之。

translations.literal: As for companions, advisers, and commentators, they were men so remote, superfluous, scattered, and base that the gentry were ashamed to come by such posts.
translations.idiomatic: As for companions, advisers, and commentators, they were men so remote, superfluous, scattered, and base that the gentry were ashamed to hold such posts.

sentences.zh: 夫以匹士之愛其子者，猶求明哲慈惠之師以教之，直諒多聞之友以成之。

translations.literal: For a common scholar who loves his son, he still seeks a wise, clear, kind, and gracious teacher to instruct him and a straightforward, honest, and widely learned friend to complete him.
translations.idiomatic: A common scholar who loves his son still seeks a wise, clear, kind, and gracious teacher to instruct him and a straightforward, honest, and widely learned friend to complete his formation.

sentences.zh: 豈天下之元良，而可以疾廢眊聵不知書者為之師乎？

translations.literal: How can the heir apparent of all under Heaven have as his teacher one who is sick, disabled, dim-sighted, deaf, and does not know books?
translations.idiomatic: How can the heir apparent of all under Heaven have as his teacher one who is sick, disabled, dim-sighted, deaf, and illiterate?

sentences.zh: 疏冗散賤不適用者為之友乎？

translations.literal: Have as his friends men who are remote, superfluous, scattered, base, and unfit for use?
translations.idiomatic: Have as his friends men who are remote, superfluous, scattered, base, and unfit for use?

sentences.zh: 此何不及上古之甚也！

translations.literal: How is this not far inferior to high antiquity!
translations.idiomatic: How is this not far inferior to high antiquity!

sentences.zh: 近制，宮僚之外，往往以沈滯僻老之儒，充侍直、侍讀之選，而又疏棄斥逐之，越月逾時，不得召見，彼又安能傅成道德而保養其身躬哉？

translations.literal: Under recent regulations, apart from palace officials, sunken, stagnant, eccentric, and aged Confucians are often used to fill the selections for attendance duty and lecturing; yet they are also neglected, cast aside, and expelled—over months and beyond the proper time they are not summoned to audience. How can they tutor and complete moral virtue and nurture and preserve his person?
translations.idiomatic: Under recent regulations, apart from palace officials, sunken, stagnant, eccentric, and aged Confucians are often used to fill the selections for attendance duty and lecturing; yet they are also neglected, cast aside, and expelled—for months on end they are not summoned to audience. How can they tutor moral virtue and nurture and preserve his person?

sentences.zh: 臣以為積此弊者，豈不以皇天眷佑，祚我唐德，以舜繼堯，傳陛下十一聖矣，莫不生而神明，長而仁聖，以是為屑屑習儀者故不之省耳。

translations.literal: This subject believes that those who have accumulated this abuse surely do so because Heaven favors and protects, and the mandate rests on our Tang virtue; from Yao to Shun, down through Your Majesty's eleven sage emperors, none failed to be spiritually bright from birth and benevolent and sage in maturity—because of this they take it as mere petty ritual practice and do not examine it.
translations.idiomatic: This subject believes that those who have accumulated this abuse do so because Heaven favors and protects our Tang virtue; from Yao to Shun, down through Your Majesty's eleven sage emperors, none failed to be spiritually bright from birth and benevolent and sage in maturity—because of this they take it as mere petty ritual practice and do not examine it.

sentences.zh: 臣獨以為於列聖之謀則可也，計傳後嗣則不可。

translations.literal: This subject alone believes that for the plans of the successive sage emperors it may suffice, but when calculating the transmission to later generations it will not do.
translations.idiomatic: This subject alone believes that for the plans of the successive sage emperors it may suffice, but when calculating the transmission to later generations it will not do.

sentences.zh: 脫或萬代之後，若有周成之中才，而又生於深宮優笑之間，無周、召保助之教，則將不能知喜怒哀樂之所自矣，況稼穡艱難乎？

translations.literal: If perchance ten thousand generations hence there should be one of King Cheng's middling talent, yet born amid the deep palace and jesters' laughter, without the instruction of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao to protect and assist, then he will not be able to know whence joy, anger, sorrow, and delight come—how much less the hardships of planting and harvesting?
translations.idiomatic: If perchance ten thousand generations hence there should be one of King Cheng's middling talent, yet born amid the deep palace and jesters' laughter, without the instruction of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao to protect and assist, then he will not know whence joy, anger, sorrow, and delight come—how much less the hardships of planting and harvesting?

sentences.zh: 今陛下以上聖之資，肇臨海內，是天下之人傾耳註心之日。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, with the endowment of a supreme sage, has newly come to rule within the seas—this is the day when the people of all under Heaven incline their ears and fix their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty, with the endowment of a supreme sage, has newly come to rule the realm—this is the day when the people of all under Heaven incline their ears and fix their hearts.

sentences.zh: 特願陛下思成王訓導之功，念文皇遊習之漸，選重師保，慎擇宮僚，皆用博厚弘深之儒，而又明達機務者為之。

translations.literal: This subject especially wishes that Your Majesty reflect on King Cheng's achievement in instruction and guidance, recall Emperor Taizong's gradual effect of association and habit, select weighty teachers and protectors, carefully choose palace officials, and employ for them all broad, generous, vast, and profound Confucians who are also clear and penetrating in practical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: This subject especially wishes that Your Majesty reflect on King Cheng's achievement in instruction and guidance, recall Emperor Taizong's gradual effect of association and habit, select weighty teachers and protectors, carefully choose palace officials, and employ broad, generous, and profound Confucians who are also clear and penetrating in practical affairs.

sentences.zh: 更相進見，日就月將。

translations.literal: Let them attend one another in audience, advancing day by day and month by month.
translations.idiomatic: Let them attend in rotation, advancing day by day and month by month.

sentences.zh: 因令皇太子聚諸生，定齒胄講業之儀，行嚴師問道之禮。

translations.literal: Thereby command the crown prince to gather the students, fix the ceremonies of ordering by age and cap for lecturing on studies, and perform the rites of a stern teacher inquiring into the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby command the crown prince to gather the students, fix the ceremonies of ordering by age and cap for lecturing on studies, and perform the rites of a stern teacher inquiring into the Way.

sentences.zh: 至德要道以成之，徹膳記過以警之。

translations.literal: Use the utmost virtue and essential Way to complete him; withdraw meals and record faults to warn him.
translations.idiomatic: Use the utmost virtue and essential Way to complete him; withdraw meals and record faults to warn him.

sentences.zh: 血氣未定，則去禽色之娛以就學；

translations.literal: While vital energies are not yet settled, remove the diversions of birds and sensual pleasures to attend to study;
translations.idiomatic: While vital energies are not yet settled, remove the diversions of birds and sensual pleasures to attend to study;

sentences.zh: 聖質已備，則資遊習之善以弘德。

translations.literal: when sage substance is already complete, then draw on the goodness of association and habit to enlarge virtue.
translations.idiomatic: when sage substance is already complete, then draw on the goodness of association and habit to enlarge virtue.

sentences.zh: 此所謂「一人元良，萬方以貞」之化也。

translations.literal: This is what is called the transformation of "one man as the chief good, the myriad regions thereby upright."
translations.idiomatic: This is what is called the transformation of "one man as the chief good, the myriad regions thereby upright."

sentences.zh: 豈直修廢學，選司成，而足倫匹其盛哉？

translations.literal: How can merely restoring abandoned schools and selecting a director of studies suffice to match its greatness?
translations.idiomatic: How can merely restoring abandoned schools and selecting a director of studies suffice to match its greatness?

sentences.zh: 而又俾則百王，莫不幼同師，長同術，識君道之素定，知天倫之自然，然後選用賢良，樹為籓屏。

translations.literal: Moreover, make them models for the hundred kings, so that none fail to share teachers in youth and share methods in maturity, know that the ruler's Way is settled from the first, and know that heavenly relations are natural—then afterward select and employ the worthy and good and establish them as feudal screens.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, make them models for the hundred kings, so that none fail to share teachers in youth and share methods in maturity, know that the ruler's Way is settled from the first, and know that heavenly relations are natural—then afterward select and employ the worthy and good and establish them as feudal screens.

sentences.zh: 出則有晉、鄭、魯、衛之盛，入則有東牟、硃虛之強，蓋所謂宗子維城、犬牙盤石之勢也，又豈與夫魏、晉以降，囚賤其兄弟而自翦其本枝者，同年而語哉？

translations.literal: Going forth there would be the splendor of Jin, Zheng, Lu, and Wei; coming in there would be the strength of Dongmou and Zhuxu—this is what is called the momentum of clansmen as walls and interlocking teeth like bedrock. How can it be spoken of in the same year as Wei and Jin onward, who imprisoned and debased their brothers and themselves pruned their own branches?
translations.idiomatic: Going forth there would be the splendor of Jin, Zheng, Lu, and Wei; coming in there would be the strength of Dongmou and Zhuxu—this is what is called the momentum of clansmen as walls and interlocking teeth like bedrock. How can it be spoken of in the same breath as Wei and Jin onward, who imprisoned and debased their brothers and themselves pruned their own branches?

sentences.zh: 憲宗覽之甚悅。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong read it and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong read it with great satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 又論西北邊事，皆朝政之大者。

translations.literal: He also discussed northwestern frontier matters—all major concerns of court governance.
translations.idiomatic: He also addressed northwestern frontier affairs, each a matter of central importance to the court.

sentences.zh: 憲宗召對，問方略。

translations.literal: Xianzong summoned him for audience and asked his strategic views.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong summoned him for a private audience and questioned him on strategy.

sentences.zh: 為執政所忌，出為河南縣尉。

translations.literal: He was resented by those in power and was sent out as magistrate of Henan County.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers took offense, and he was transferred out to serve as magistrate of Henan County.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended, he was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: After observing mourning for his mother and completing the requisite period, he was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 四年，奉使東蜀，劾奏故劍南東川節度使嚴礪違制擅賦，又籍沒塗山甫等吏民八十八戶田宅一百一十一、奴婢二十七人、草千五百束、錢七千貫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was dispatched to eastern Shu and memorialized accusing the former military governor of Jiannan East, Yan Li, of violating regulations in levying unauthorized taxes, and of confiscating from officials and commoners including Tu Shanfu eighty-eight households' estates numbering one hundred and eleven, twenty-seven bondservants, fifteen hundred bundles of forage, and seven thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was sent on mission to eastern Shu and impeached the former military governor of eastern Sichuan, Yan Li, for unauthorized levies in violation of regulations. He further documented the confiscation of property from eighty-eight households of officials and commoners—including Tu Shanfu—totaling 111 parcels of land, 27 bondservants, 1,500 bundles of forage, and 7,000 strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 時礪已死，七州刺史皆責罰。

translations.literal: Yan Li had already died; the prefects of seven prefectures were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Li was already dead, but the governors of seven prefectures were all called to account and penalized.

sentences.zh: 稹雖舉職，而執政有與礪厚者惡之。

translations.literal: Though Zhen had performed his duties, someone among those in power who had been close to Yan Li bore him ill will.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhen had done his duty, certain powerful figures who had been on friendly terms with Yan Li turned against him.

sentences.zh: 使還，令分務東臺。

translations.literal: When he returned from his mission, he was ordered to divide duties at the eastern tribunal.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was assigned to share duties at the eastern office of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使韓臯封杖決湖州安吉令孫澥，四日內死。

translations.literal: Han Gao, surveillance commissioner of Zhexi, had Sun Xie, magistrate of Anji in Huzhou, beaten with the cudgel to death within four days.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gao, commissioner of Zhexi, had ordered Sun Xie, magistrate of Anji in Huzhou, beaten with the cudgel; Sun died within four days.

sentences.zh: 徐州監軍使孟升卒，節度使王紹傳送升喪柩還京，給券乘驛，仍於郵舍安喪柩。

translations.literal: When the army supervisor of Xuzhou, Meng Sheng, died, the military governor Wang Shao had Sheng's coffin escorted back to the capital, issued passes for relay transport, and even lodged the coffin at a postal station.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Sheng, the army supervisor at Xuzhou, died, the military governor Wang Shao had his coffin sent to the capital with relay passes and even housed the coffin overnight at a postal station—both grave breaches of protocol.

sentences.zh: 稹並劾奏以法。

translations.literal: Zhen impeached them both according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen impeached both men on legal grounds.

sentences.zh: 河南尹房式為不法事，稹欲追攝，擅令停務。

translations.literal: Fang Shi, intendant of Henan, had committed unlawful acts; Zhen wished to summon him for questioning, but Fang on his own authority ordered his office to cease operations.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Shi, intendant of the Henan metropolitan district, had engaged in unlawful conduct; when Zhen sought to summon him, Fang unilaterally suspended his office's operations.

sentences.zh: 既飛表聞奏，罰式一月俸，仍召稹還京。

translations.literal: Fang hurried a memorial to the throne; Shi was fined one month's salary, and Zhen was nevertheless recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fang rushed a memorial to court; Shi was fined one month's salary, and Zhen was recalled to the capital nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 宿敷水驛，內官劉士元後至，爭廳。

translations.literal: He lodged at Fushui Post; the inner-court eunuch Liu Shiyuan arrived later and they disputed over the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: While staying at Fushui Post, he encountered the eunuch Liu Shiyuan, who had arrived later and contested possession of the reception hall.

sentences.zh: 士元怒，排其戶，稹襪而走廳後。

translations.literal: Shiyuan in anger burst through the door; Zhen fled in his stocking feet to the rear of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan flew into a rage, forced the door open, and Zhen fled barefoot to the rear of the hall.

sentences.zh: 士元追之，後以棰擊稹傷面。

translations.literal: Shiyuan pursued him and afterward struck Zhen in the face with a club.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan pursued him and struck him across the face with a club.

sentences.zh: 執政以稹少年後輩，務作威福，貶為江陵府士曹參軍。

translations.literal: Those in power, regarding Zhen as a young junior who sought to wield authority for his own benefit, demoted him to army staff officer of Jiangling prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers, deeming the young upstart bent on throwing his weight around, demoted him to staff officer in the Jiangling prefectural army.

sentences.zh: 稹聰警絕人，年少有才名，與太原白居易友善。

translations.literal: Zhen's intelligence surpassed others; in youth he had a reputation for talent and was on friendly terms with Bai Juyi of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was exceptionally quick-witted; even in youth he enjoyed a reputation for talent, and he formed a close friendship with Bai Juyi of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 工為詩，善狀詠風態物色，當時言詩者，稱元、白焉。

translations.literal: He excelled at poetry and was skilled at depicting moods and scenes; those who spoke of poetry at the time paired Yuan and Bai.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at verse and had a gift for capturing mood and scenery; contemporaries who discussed poetry paired "Yuan and Bai."

sentences.zh: 自衣冠士子，至閭閻下俚，悉傳諷之，號為「元和體」。

translations.literal: From scholars in official dress down to commoners in the lanes, all recited and chanted his works, which were called the "Yuanhe style."
translations.idiomatic: From court gentlemen to common folk in the alleyways, everyone recited his poems; the style became known as the "Yuanhe manner."

sentences.zh: 既以俊爽不容於朝，流放荊蠻者僅十年。

translations.literal: Because his brilliance and candor were not tolerated at court, he was exiled to the southern barbarian lands for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: His brilliance and outspokenness had made him unwelcome at court, and he spent nearly ten years in exile in the Jingnan region.

sentences.zh: 俄而白居易亦貶江州司馬，稹量移通州司馬。

translations.literal: Before long Bai Juyi was also demoted to marshal of Jiangzhou; Zhen was transferred in grade to marshal of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Bai Juyi was demoted to marshal of Jiangzhou as well, while Zhen was transferred to the same post at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 雖通、江懸邈，而二人來往贈答。

translations.literal: Though Tong and Jiang were far apart, the two men exchanged visits and poetic gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Though Tongzhou and Jiangzhou lay far apart, the two men exchanged visits and poems across the distance.

sentences.zh: 凡所為詩，有自三十、五十韻乃至百韻者。

translations.literal: Of the poems they composed, some ran from thirty or fifty rhymes to as many as a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Their poems ranged in length from thirty or fifty rhymes to as many as a hundred.

sentences.zh: 江南人士，傳道諷誦，流聞闕下，裏巷相傳，為之紙貴。

translations.literal: Gentlemen south of the Yangtze passed them along and chanted them; they flowed to the capital, were copied from lane to lane, and drove up the price of paper.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars in the south copied and recited them; the poems traveled to the capital, spread through every neighborhood, and drove up the price of paper.

sentences.zh: 觀其流離放逐之意，靡不淒惋。

translations.literal: Observing the sense of wandering banishment in them, none failed to find them poignant and sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: Readers found in them the ache of exile and displacement—every poem touched with sorrow.

sentences.zh: 十四年，自虢州長史征還，為膳部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was summoned back from his post as senior administrator of Guozhou and made vice director of the Catering Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was recalled from senior administrator of Guozhou and appointed vice director in the Bureau of Foodstuffs.

sentences.zh: 宰相令狐楚一代文宗，雅知稹之辭學，謂稹曰：「嘗覽足下製作，所恨不多，遲之久矣。

translations.literal: The chief minister Linghu Chu, a literary authority of his generation, had long appreciated Zhen's literary learning and said to him: "I have read your compositions before; I regret there are not more of them, and I have waited too long.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chu, the chief minister and a leading literary figure of the age, had long admired Zhen's literary gifts. He told him, "I have read your work before and regretted that there was not more of it; I have waited far too long.

sentences.zh: 請出其所有，以豁予情。」

translations.literal: Please bring out everything you have, so as to satisfy my feelings."
translations.idiomatic: Bring out everything you have written and satisfy my wish at last."

sentences.zh: 稹因獻其文，自敘曰：稹初不好文，徒以仕無他歧，強由科試。

translations.literal: Zhen thereupon presented his writings, with a preface that read: Zhen at first did not love literature; he merely had no other path in office and was forced through the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen accordingly presented his collected writings, prefaced with an autobiographical note that read: At first I did not love literature; I merely had no other path in office and was forced through the civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 及有罪譴棄之後，自以為廢滯潦倒，不復為文字有聞於人矣。

translations.literal: After being condemned and cast aside for guilt, I considered myself discarded, stagnant, and down and out, and no longer expected my writings to become known among men.
translations.idiomatic: After being condemned and cast aside for guilt, I considered myself discarded, stagnant, and ruined, and no longer expected my writings to become known among men.

sentences.zh: 曾不知好事者抉擿芻蕪，塵瀆尊重。

translations.literal: I never knew that lovers of the matter would pick out the fodder and weeds and defile what is honored with dust.
translations.idiomatic: I never imagined that enthusiasts would pick out the fodder and weeds and defile what is honored.

sentences.zh: 竊承相公特於廊廟間道稹詩句，昨又面奉教約，令獻舊文。

translations.literal: I have privately heard that the Chief Minister especially spoke of Zhen's poetic lines in the halls of state; yesterday I again received face to face his instruction and command to present old writings.
translations.idiomatic: I have privately heard that the Chief Minister especially spoke of my poetic lines in the halls of state; yesterday I again received his face-to-face instruction to present my old writings.

sentences.zh: 戰汗悚踴，慚靦無地。

translations.literal: Trembling with sweat, startled and leaping, ashamed beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Trembling with sweat, startled and overwhelmed, I am ashamed beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 稹自御史府謫官，於今十餘年矣。

translations.literal: Zhen, since demotion from the Censorate, has now been more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Since my demotion from the Censorate, more than ten years have now passed.

sentences.zh: 閑誕無事，遂專力於詩章。

translations.literal: Leisurely and at ease with nothing to do, I then devoted my strength to poetic compositions.
translations.idiomatic: Leisurely and at ease with nothing to do, I then devoted myself to poetry.

sentences.zh: 日益月滋，有詩句千餘首。

translations.literal: Day by day and month by month they increased; there are more than a thousand poetic lines.
translations.idiomatic: Day by day and month by month they increased; I have more than a thousand poems.

sentences.zh: 其間感物寓意，可備矇瞽之風者有之。

translations.literal: Among them are some that respond to things and convey meaning, fit to supply the style of instruction for the blind.
translations.idiomatic: Among them are some that respond to things and convey meaning, fit to supply instruction for the unenlightened.

sentences.zh: 辭直氣粗，罪尤是懼，固不敢陳露於人。

translations.literal: The wording is blunt and the tone rough; guilt is what I especially fear, so I truly do not dare to display them before others.
translations.idiomatic: The wording is blunt and the tone rough; guilt is what I especially fear, so I truly do not dare display them before others.

sentences.zh: 唯杯酒光景間，屢為小碎篇章，以自吟暢。

translations.literal: Only amid the light of wine and cups have I often made small fragmentary compositions to chant and enjoy for myself.
translations.idiomatic: Only amid wine and cups have I often made small fragmentary pieces to chant for my own enjoyment.

sentences.zh: 然以為律體卑痹，格力不揚，茍無姿態，則陷流俗。

translations.literal: Yet I consider regulated verse base and cramped, its force and style not uplifted; if without manner and bearing, then it falls into vulgar fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I consider regulated verse base and cramped, its force and style not uplifted; without manner and bearing it falls into vulgar fashion.

sentences.zh: 常欲得思深語近，韻律調新，屬對無差，而風情宛然，而病未能也。

translations.literal: I constantly wished to attain thought deep and language near, rhyme and measure tuned anew, parallel couplets without flaw, and feeling and style gracefully present—but the ailment I have not yet been able to overcome.
translations.idiomatic: I constantly wished to attain deep thought and plain language, fresh rhyme and measure, flawless parallel couplets, and graceful feeling and style—but I have not yet overcome this failing.

sentences.zh: 江湖間多新進小生，不知天下文有宗主，妄相放效，而又從而失之，遂至於支離褊淺之辭，皆目為元和詩體。

translations.literal: Along the rivers and lakes there are many newly advanced young men who do not know that literature under Heaven has a master; they recklessly imitate one another, and moreover lose their way in doing so, until fragmentary and narrow shallow phrasing all is called the Yuanhe poetic style.
translations.idiomatic: Along the rivers and lakes there are many newly advanced young men who do not know that literature has a master; they recklessly imitate one another and lose their way, until fragmentary, narrow, shallow phrasing is all called the Yuanhe poetic style.

sentences.zh: 稹與同門生白居易友善。

translations.literal: Zhen was on friendly terms with his fellow student Bai Juyi.
translations.idiomatic: I was on friendly terms with my fellow student Bai Juyi.

sentences.zh: 居易雅能詩，就中愛驅駕文字，窮極聲韻，或為千言，或五百言律詩，以相投寄。

translations.literal: Juyi is elegantly skilled in poetry; among his works he especially loves driving and mastering words, exhausting sound and rhyme; sometimes thousand-character or five-hundred-character regulated poems he sends to exchange with me.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi is elegantly skilled in poetry; among his works he especially loves mastering words and exhausting sound and rhyme; sometimes he sends me thousand-character or five-hundred-character regulated poems in exchange.

sentences.zh: 小生自審不能過之，往往戲排舊韻，別創新辭，名為次韻相酬，蓋欲以難相排。

translations.literal: This humble student, examining myself, could not surpass him; I often playfully arranged old rhymes and separately created new wording, calling it matching rhymes in mutual response—intending to use difficulty to compete.
translations.idiomatic: Examining myself, I could not surpass him; I often playfully arranged old rhymes and created new wording, calling it matching rhymes in mutual response—intending to compete through difficulty.

sentences.zh: 自爾江湖間為詩者，復相放效，力或不足，則至於顛倒語言，重復首尾，韻同意等，不異前篇，亦目為元和詩體。

translations.literal: From then on, poets along the rivers and lakes again imitated one another; when strength was sometimes insufficient, it reached the point of inverted language, repeated beginnings and ends, rhymes and meaning the same, no different from the previous piece—this too was called the Yuanhe poetic style.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, poets along the rivers and lakes again imitated one another; when their strength was insufficient, it reached inverted language, repeated beginnings and ends, identical rhymes and meaning no different from the previous piece—this too was called the Yuanhe poetic style.

sentences.zh: 而司文者考變雅之由，往往歸咎於稹。

translations.literal: Yet those who oversee literature, examining the causes of the change in refined style, often lay blame on Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who oversee literature, examining the causes of the change in refined style, often lay blame on me.

sentences.zh: 嘗以為雕蟲小事，不足以自明。

translations.literal: I once considered it a trifling matter of carving insects, insufficient to clarify myself.
translations.idiomatic: I once considered it a trifling matter of literary ornament, insufficient to clarify myself.

sentences.zh: 始聞相公記憶，累旬已來，實慮糞土之墻，庇之以大廈，使不復破壞，永為板築者之誤。

translations.literal: When I first heard that the Chief Minister remembered me, for many days now I have truly feared that a wall of dung and earth would be sheltered by a great hall so that it would no longer be broken—forever becoming the error of those who lay boards and build.
translations.idiomatic: When I first heard that the Chief Minister remembered me, for many days I have truly feared that a wall of dung and earth would be sheltered by a great hall so it would no longer crumble—forever becoming the error of those who lay boards and build.

sentences.zh: 輒寫古體歌詩一百首，百韻至兩韻律詩一百首，為五卷，奉啟跪陳。

translations.literal: I have hastily copied one hundred old-style songs and poems and one hundred regulated poems from hundred rhymes down to two rhymes, making five scrolls, which I respectfully present kneeling.
translations.idiomatic: I have copied one hundred old-style songs and poems and one hundred regulated poems from hundred rhymes down to two rhymes, making five scrolls, which I respectfully present on my knees.

sentences.zh: 或希構廈之餘，一賜觀覽，知小生於章句中欒櫨榱桷之材，盡曾量度，則十餘年之邅回，不為無用矣。

translations.literal: Perhaps hoping that after the great hall is built you might once bestow a reading, knowing that this humble student's timber for rafters and ridgepoles within lines and stanzas has all been measured—then more than ten years of wandering will not have been without use.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps, after the great hall is built, you might once grant a reading and know that this humble student's rafter and ridgepole timber within lines and stanzas has all been measured—then more than ten years of wandering will not have been in vain.

sentences.zh: 楚深稱賞，以為今代之鮑、謝也。

translations.literal: Linghu Chu praised them deeply, holding him the Bao and Xie of the present age.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chu praised them extravagantly, declaring him the Bao Zhao and Xie Lingyun of their generation.

sentences.zh: 穆宗皇帝在東宮，有妃嬪左右嘗誦稹歌詩以為樂曲者，知稹所為，嘗稱其善，宮中呼為元才子。

translations.literal: While Emperor Muzong was crown prince, concubines and attendants at his side had sometimes recited Zhen's songs as tunes; knowing Zhen's work, they had praised it, and within the palace he was called the Yuan talent.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Muzong was still crown prince, ladies of his household had sometimes sung Zhen's poems as songs; they knew his work and praised it, and within the palace he was called "the Yuan talent."

sentences.zh: 荊南監軍崔潭峻甚禮接稹，不以掾吏遇之，常征其詩什諷誦之。

translations.literal: The Jingnan army supervisor Cui Tanjun treated Zhen with great courtesy, not regarding him as a mere clerk, and often requested his poems to recite.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Tanjun, army supervisor in Jingnan, treated Zhen with exceptional respect rather than as a lowly clerk, and often asked for his poems to recite.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，潭峻歸朝，出稹《連昌宮辭》等百餘篇奏御。

translations.literal: In the early Changqing era Tanjun returned to court and presented to the throne more than a hundred pieces including Zhen's "Ballad of the Lianchang Palace."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changqing reign Tanjun returned to the capital and presented to the throne more than a hundred of Zhen's works, including "Ballad of the Lianchang Palace."

sentences.zh: 穆宗大悅，問稹安在。

translations.literal: Muzong was greatly pleased and asked where Zhen was.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong was delighted and asked where Zhen was serving.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「今為南宮散郎。」

translations.literal: The reply was: "He is now a junior gentleman of the Southern Palace."
translations.idiomatic: The answer came: "He is presently a junior gentleman of the Southern Palace."

sentences.zh: 即日轉祠部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: That same day he was transferred to director of the Sacrifices Bureau with charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was transferred to director of the Sacrifices Bureau with charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以書命不由相府，甚鄙之。

translations.literal: The court, because written commands had not come through the chancellery, regarded this with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: The court looked down on the appointment because the edicts had not passed through the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 然辭誥所出，夐然與古為侔，遂盛傳於代，由是極承恩顧。

translations.literal: Yet the proclamations he drafted stood far apart from antiquity in their excellence and soon spread widely through the age; from this he received the utmost imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the edicts he drafted matched the ancients in grandeur and spread swiftly through the realm, and from this he won extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 嘗為《長慶宮辭》數十百篇，京師競相傳唱。

translations.literal: He once composed several dozen or hundred pieces of "Changqing Palace Lyrics," which the capital competed to sing.
translations.idiomatic: He composed dozens or hundreds of "Changqing Palace Lyrics," which the capital took up and sang in rivalry.

sentences.zh: 居無何，召入翰林，為中書舍人、承旨學士。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as drafting academician and chief academician.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as drafting academician and chief academician.

sentences.zh: 中人以潭峻之故，爭與稹交，而知樞密魏弘簡尤與稹相善，穆宗愈深知重。

translations.literal: Eunuchs, because of Tanjun, vied to befriend Zhen, and Wei Hongjian of the Bureau of Military Affairs was especially close to him; Muzong came to know and value him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Tanjun, eunuchs vied to befriend Zhen, and Wei Hongjian of the Bureau of Military Affairs was especially close to him; Muzong valued him all the more.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使裴度三上疏，言稹與弘簡為刎頸之交，謀亂朝政，言甚激訐。

translations.literal: The military governor of Hedong, Pei Du, submitted three memorials stating that Zhen and Hongjian were sworn friends plotting to disrupt court governance, with language fiercely accusatory.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du, military governor of Hedong, submitted three memorials claiming that Zhen and Hongjian were sworn friends plotting to disrupt court governance, in fiercely accusatory language.

sentences.zh: 穆宗顧中外人情，乃罷稹內職，授工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Muzong, considering sentiment inside and outside the court, removed Zhen from his inner post and appointed him vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong, weighing opinion within and outside the court, stripped Zhen of his inner-court post and made him vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 上恩顧未衰。

translations.literal: The emperor's favor for him had not yet waned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's favor had not yet waned.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年，拜平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changqing he was appointed chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changqing he was appointed chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 詔下之日，朝野無不輕笑之。

translations.literal: On the day the edict was issued, neither court nor populace could refrain from laughing lightly.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was promulgated, court and populace alike could scarcely suppress a smile.

sentences.zh: 時王廷湊、硃克融連兵圍牛元翼於深州，朝廷俱赦其罪，賜節鉞，令罷兵，俱不奉詔。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Tingcou and Zhu Keyi had joined forces to besiege Niu Yuanji at Shenzhou; the court had pardoned their crimes and bestowed military commissions, ordering them to withdraw, but both refused the edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Tingcou and Zhu Keyi had joined forces to besiege Niu Yuanji at Shenzhou; the court had pardoned their crimes and granted them military commissions, ordering them to withdraw, but both refused the edicts.

sentences.zh: 稹以天子非次拔擢，欲有所立以報上。

translations.literal: Zhen, because the Son of Heaven had raised him out of turn, wished to accomplish something to repay his sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, having been raised to office by an exceptional imperial favor, wished to accomplish something worthy in return.

sentences.zh: 有和王傅於方者，故司空頔之子，干進於稹。

translations.literal: There was a prince's tutor named Yu Fang, son of the former Minister of Works Yu Di, who pressed himself on Zhen for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: A prince's tutor named Yu Fang, son of the former Minister of Works Yu Di, pressed himself on Zhen seeking advancement.

sentences.zh: 言有奇士王昭、王友明二人，嘗客於燕、趙間，頗與賊黨通熟，可以反間而出元翼。

translations.literal: He spoke of two extraordinary men, Wang Zhao and Wang Youming, who had lodged in Yan and Zhao and were well acquainted with the rebel bands, and who could be used in a stratagem to extricate Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of two men of unusual ability, Wang Zhao and Wang Youming, who had sojourned in the Yan and Zhao region and were well acquainted with the rebel factions, and who might be turned through counter-intelligence to rescue Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 仍自以家財資其行，仍賂兵吏部令史為出告身二十通，以便宜給賜，稹皆然之。

translations.literal: He offered his family wealth to fund their mission and bribed clerks in the Ministry of War to issue twenty blank commissions for discretionary reward; Zhen approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: He offered his family wealth to fund their mission and bribed clerks in the Ministry of War to issue twenty blank commissions for discretionary reward; Zhen approved all of this.

sentences.zh: 有李賞者，知於方之謀，以稹與裴度有隙，乃告度云：「於方為稹所使，欲結客王昭等刺度。」

translations.literal: One Li Shang, knowing of Fang's plot and aware of the rift between Zhen and Pei Du, reported to Du: "Yu Fang is acting at Zhen's behest, seeking to recruit Wang Zhao and others to assassinate Du."
translations.idiomatic: A man named Li Shang, who knew of Fang's scheme and aware of the rift between Zhen and Pei Du, reported to Du: "Yu Fang is acting at Zhen's orders, recruiting Wang Zhao and others to assassinate you."

sentences.zh: 度隱而不發。

translations.literal: Du kept silent and did not expose it.
translations.idiomatic: Du kept silent and did not act on the report.

sentences.zh: 及神策軍中尉奏於方之事，乃詔三司使韓臯等訊鞫，而害裴事無驗，而前事盡露。

translations.literal: When the director of the Divine Stratagem Army memorialized on Fang's affair, an edict ordered the three judicial offices under Han Gao and others to investigate; the charge against Pei was unverified, but the earlier matters came fully to light.
translations.idiomatic: When the director of the Divine Stratagem Army reported on Fang's affair, the three judicial offices under Han Gao and others were ordered to investigate; the plot against Pei could not be verified, but the earlier schemes were fully exposed.

sentences.zh: 遂俱罷稹、度平章事，乃出稹為同州刺史，度守僕射。

translations.literal: Zhen and Du were both removed as chief councilors; Zhen was sent out as governor of Tongzhou and Du retained his post as vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Both Zhen and Du were removed as chief councilors; Zhen was sent out as governor of Tongzhou while Du remained vice director.

sentences.zh: 諫官上疏，言責度太重，稹太輕。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials submitted memorials saying the punishment of Du was too heavy and that of Zhen too light.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials submitted memorials arguing that Du's punishment was too severe and Zhen's too lenient.

sentences.zh: 上心憐稹，止削長春宮使。

translations.literal: The emperor, pitying Zhen, only stripped him of his commission as commissioner of the Everlasting Spring Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, taking pity on Zhen, only stripped him of his commission as commissioner of the Everlasting Spring Palace.

sentences.zh: 稹初罷相，三司獄未奏，京兆尹劉遵古遣坊所由潛邏稹居第，稹奏訴之。

translations.literal: When Zhen had first been removed as chief councilor, before the three offices had reported, the metropolitan intendant Liu Zungu sent ward officers to spy secretly on Zhen's residence; Zhen memorialized in protest.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Zhen lost the chancellorship, before the three offices had concluded their report, the metropolitan intendant Liu Zungu sent ward officers to spy on Zhen's residence; Zhen memorialized in protest.

sentences.zh: 上怒，罰遵古，遣中人撫諭稹。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered, punished Zungu, and sent a eunuch to console Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angered, punished Zungu, and dispatched a eunuch to console Zhen.

sentences.zh: 稹至同州，因表謝上，自敘曰：臣稹辜負聖明，辱累恩獎，便合自求死所，豈謂尚忝官榮？

translations.literal: When Zhen reached Tongzhou he submitted a memorial of thanks to the throne, with a self-account that read: This subject Zhen has failed the sage clarity, disgraced and burdened by favor and reward; he ought to seek his own place of death—how can he say he still undeservedly holds office and honor?
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Tongzhou he submitted a memorial of thanks to the throne, with a self-account that read: This subject Zhen has failed Your sage clarity, disgraced and burdened by favor and reward; I ought to seek my own place of death—how can I say I still undeservedly hold office and honor?

sentences.zh: 臣稹死罪。

translations.literal: This subject Zhen deserves death.
translations.idiomatic: This subject Zhen deserves death.

sentences.zh: 臣八歲喪父，家貧無業。

translations.literal: This subject lost his father at eight; the family was poor and without livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: This subject lost his father at eight; the family was poor and without livelihood.

sentences.zh: 母兄乞丐以供資養。

translations.literal: Mother and elder brother begged to supply sustenance.
translations.idiomatic: Mother and elder brother begged to supply sustenance.

sentences.zh: 衣不布體，食不充腸。

translations.literal: Clothes did not cover the body; food did not fill the belly.
translations.idiomatic: Clothes did not cover the body; food did not fill the belly.

sentences.zh: 幼學之年，不蒙師訓。

translations.literal: In the years of early study, I did not receive a teacher's instruction.
translations.idiomatic: In the years of early study, I did not receive a teacher's instruction.

sentences.zh: 因感鄰裏兒稚有父兄為開學校，涕咽發憤，願知《詩》、《書》。

translations.literal: Because I was moved that neighborhood children had fathers and elder brothers who opened schools, I wept and choked with indignation and wished to know the Poetry and Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Because I was moved that neighborhood children had fathers and elder brothers who opened schools, I wept and choked with indignation and wished to know the Poetry and Documents.

sentences.zh: 慈母哀臣，親為教授。

translations.literal: My kind mother pitied this subject and personally taught him.
translations.idiomatic: My kind mother pitied me and personally taught me.

sentences.zh: 年十有五，得明經出身，由是苦心為文，夙夜強學。

translations.literal: At fifteen I obtained entry by the classics examination; from this I labored at writing with bitter effort and studied strenuously morning and night.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen I obtained entry by the classics examination; from this I labored at writing with bitter effort and studied strenuously morning and night.

sentences.zh: 年二十四，登吏部乙科，授校書郎。

translations.literal: At twenty-four I passed the Ministry of Personnel second class and was appointed collator.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-four I passed the Ministry of Personnel second class and was appointed collator.

sentences.zh: 年二十八，蒙制舉首選，授左拾遺。

translations.literal: At twenty-eight I was honored with first selection in the special examination and was appointed left remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-eight I was honored with first selection in the special examination and was appointed left remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 始自為學，至於升朝，無朋友為臣吹噓，無親戚為臣援庇。

translations.literal: From first pursuing study to ascending court, there were no friends to puff up this subject, no kinsmen to shield and protect this subject.
translations.idiomatic: From first pursuing study to ascending court, there were no friends to puff me up, no kinsmen to shield and protect me.

sentences.zh: 莫非苦己，實不因人，獨立性成，遂無交結。

translations.literal: All was through bitter effort on myself; truly not through others. Independent character was formed, and thus there were no associations.
translations.idiomatic: All was through bitter effort on myself; truly not through others. Independent character was formed, and thus I had no associations.

sentences.zh: 任拾遺日，屢陳時政，蒙先皇帝召問於延英。

translations.literal: During my days as remonstrance official I repeatedly set forth current government affairs and was honored by the late emperor with summons and inquiry in Yanying.
translations.idiomatic: During my days as remonstrance official I repeatedly set forth current government affairs and was honored by the late emperor with summons and inquiry in Yanying.

sentences.zh: 旋為宰相所憎，出臣河南縣尉。

translations.literal: Soon I was hated by the chancellor and this subject was sent out as marshal of Henan County.
translations.idiomatic: Soon I was hated by the chancellor and was sent out as marshal of Henan County.

sentences.zh: 及為監察御史，又不規避，專心糾繩，復為宰相怒臣下庇親黨，因以他事貶臣江陵判司。

translations.literal: When I became investigating censor, again I did not evade or avoid but devoted my heart to impeachment and discipline. Again the chancellor was angry that this subject's subordinates sheltered kin and partisans, and on another matter demoted this subject to aide in Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When I became investigating censor, again I did not evade or avoid but devoted my heart to impeachment and discipline. Again the chancellor was angry that my subordinates sheltered kin and partisans, and on another matter demoted me to aide in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 廢棄十年，分死溝瀆。

translations.literal: Abandoned for ten years, I allotted myself to die in ditch and drain.
translations.idiomatic: Abandoned for ten years, I allotted myself to die in ditch and drain.

sentences.zh: 元和十四年，憲宗皇帝開釋有罪，始授臣膳部員外郎。

translations.literal: In Yuanhe 14, Emperor Xianzong opened release for the guilty and first appointed this subject vice director of the Board of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 14, Emperor Xianzong opened release for the guilty and first appointed me vice director of the Board of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 與臣同省署者，多是臣登朝時舉人；

translations.literal: Those in the same ministry office with this subject were mostly men this subject had recommended when ascending court;
translations.idiomatic: Those in the same ministry office with me were mostly men I had recommended when ascending court;

sentences.zh: 任卿相者，半是臣同諫院時拾遺、補闕。

translations.literal: those holding posts as ministers and chancellors were half remonstrance and supplementation officials from this subject's days in the remonstrance courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: those holding posts as ministers and chancellors were half remonstrance and supplementation officials from my days in the remonstrance courtyard.

sentences.zh: 愚臣既不料陛下天聽過卑，知臣薄藝，硃書授臣制誥，延英召臣賜緋。

translations.literal: This foolish subject had not expected that Your Majesty's heavenly hearing was excessively low, knowing this subject's slight arts—vermilion writing appointed this subject to draft edicts, and Yanying summoned this subject to bestow crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: This foolish subject had not expected that Your Majesty's heavenly hearing was excessively humble, knowing my slight arts—vermilion writing appointed me to draft edicts, and Yanying summoned me to bestow crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 宰相惡臣不出其門，由是百萬侵毀。

translations.literal: The chancellor hated that this subject did not come from his gate; thereby a hundred slanders invaded and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor hated that I did not come from his gate; thereby a hundred slanders invaded and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 陛下察臣無罪，寵獎逾深，召臣固授舍人，遣充承旨翰林學士，金章紫服，光飾陋軀，人生之榮，臣亦至矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty examined this subject and found no guilt; favor and reward exceeded the deep. This subject was summoned and firmly appointed palace aide, dispatched to serve as drafting Hanlin academician; golden seal and purple robes adorned my humble body—the glory of human life, this subject also reached its utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty examined me and found no guilt; favor and reward exceeded the deep. I was summoned and firmly appointed palace aide, dispatched to serve as drafting Hanlin academician; golden seal and purple robes adorned my humble body—the glory of human life, I also reached its utmost.

sentences.zh: 然臣益遭誹謗，日夜憂危。

translations.literal: Yet this subject increasingly suffered slander and day and night worried over peril.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I increasingly suffered slander and day and night worried over peril.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下聖鑒昭臨，彌加保任，竟排群議，擢授臺司。

translations.literal: Only Your Majesty's sage mirror brightly oversaw, increasingly added protection and trust, and in the end set aside the multitude of opinions and promoted me to the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Only Your Majesty's sage mirror brightly oversaw, increasingly added protection and trust, and in the end set aside the multitude of opinions and promoted me to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 臣忝有肺肝，豈並尋常宰相？

translations.literal: This subject undeservedly possessed heart and liver—how could he be ranked with ordinary chancellors?
translations.idiomatic: This subject undeservedly possessed heart and liver—how could I be ranked with ordinary chancellors?

sentences.zh: 況當行營退散之後，牛元翼未出之間，每聞陛下軫念之言，愚臣恨不身先士卒。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the campaign forces had withdrawn and dispersed, and Niu Yuanji had not yet emerged, each time I heard Your Majesty's words of anxious concern, this foolish subject regretted that he was not first among the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the campaign forces had withdrawn and dispersed, and Niu Yuanji had not yet emerged, each time I heard Your Majesty's words of anxious concern, this foolish subject regretted that I was not first among the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 所問於方計策，遣王友明等救解深州，蓋欲上副聖情，豈是別懷他意？

translations.literal: What was asked about in plans and stratagems—dispatching Wang Youming and others to rescue and relieve Shen Prefecture—was surely to match above the sage sentiment; how could it be harboring another intent?
translations.idiomatic: What was asked about in plans and stratagems—dispatching Wang Youming and others to rescue and relieve Shen Prefecture—was surely to match Your sage sentiment; how could it be harboring another intent?

sentences.zh: 不料奸人疑臣殺害裴度，妄有告論，塵瀆聖聰，愧羞天地。

translations.literal: I did not expect that wicked men suspected this subject of murdering Pei Du and falsely made accusations, dusting and defiling the sage hearing—shame before Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect that wicked men suspected me of murdering Pei Du and falsely made accusations, dusting and defiling Your sage hearing—shame before Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 臣本待辨明一了，便擬殺身謝責，豈料聖慈尚加，薄貶同州。

translations.literal: This subject originally waited to clarify the matter completely and then planned to kill his body to answer the blame—who expected that sage compassion still added favor, lightly demoting me to Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: This subject originally waited to clarify the matter completely and then planned to give my life to answer the blame—who expected that Your sage compassion still added favor, lightly demoting me to Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 雖違咫尺之間，不遠郊圻之境，伏料必是宸衷獨斷，乞臣此官。

translations.literal: Though separated by less than a foot's distance, not far from the suburban domain, I humbly reckon it must be the imperial heart's sole decision, granting this subject this office.
translations.idiomatic: Though separated by less than a foot's distance, not far from the suburban domain, I humbly reckon it must be Your imperial heart's sole decision, granting me this office.

sentences.zh: 若遣他人商量，乍可與臣遠處方鎮，豈肯遣臣俯近闕廷？

translations.literal: If others had been sent to deliberate, they might for a time send this subject to a distant frontier command—but would they be willing to send this subject bowing near the court gate?
translations.idiomatic: If others had been sent to deliberate, they might for a time send me to a distant frontier command—but would they be willing to send me bowing near the court gate?

sentences.zh: 所恨今月三日，尚蒙召對延英。

translations.literal: What I regret is that on the third day of this month I still received summons for audience in Yanying.
translations.idiomatic: What I regret is that on the third day of this month I still received summons for audience in Yanying.

sentences.zh: 此時不解泣血，仰辭天顏，乃至今日竄逐。

translations.literal: At that time I did not understand to weep blood and look up to decline the heavenly countenance, and thus reached today's banishment and expulsion.
translations.idiomatic: At that time I did not understand to weep blood and look up to decline Your countenance, and thus reached today's banishment and expulsion.

sentences.zh: 臣自離京國，目斷魂銷。

translations.literal: Since this subject left the capital, eyes are severed and soul is broken.
translations.idiomatic: Since I left the capital, my sight is severed and my soul is broken.

sentences.zh: 每至五更朝謁之時，實制淚不已。

translations.literal: Each time the fifth watch arrives for court audience, I truly restrain tears without end.
translations.idiomatic: Each time the fifth watch arrives for court audience, I truly restrain tears without end.

sentences.zh: 臣若餘生未死，他時萬一歸還，不敢更望得見天顏，但得再聞京城鐘鼓之音，臣雖黃土覆面，無恨九泉。

translations.literal: If this subject's remaining life is not yet ended and someday by chance I return, I dare not hope again to see the heavenly countenance—only to hear once more the capital's bells and drums; though yellow earth covers my face, I would have no regret in the nine springs.
translations.idiomatic: If my remaining life is not yet ended and someday by chance I return, I dare not hope again to see Your countenance—only to hear once more the capital's bells and drums; though yellow earth covers my face, I would have no regret in the grave.

sentences.zh: 臣無任自恨自慚，攀戀聖慈之至。

translations.literal: This subject cannot bear self-reproach and self-shame, clinging in longing to the utmost sage compassion.
translations.idiomatic: This subject cannot bear self-reproach and self-shame, clinging in longing to Your utmost sage compassion.

sentences.zh: 在郡二年，改授越州刺史、兼御史大夫、漸東觀察使。

translations.literal: After two years in the prefecture he was reassigned as governor of Yuezhou with concurrent appointment as grand censor and surveillance commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: After two years in the prefecture he was reassigned as governor of Yuezhou with concurrent appointment as grand censor and surveillance commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 會稽山水奇秀，稹所辟幕職，皆當時文士，而鏡湖、秦望之遊，月三四焉。

translations.literal: Kuaiji's mountains and waters were wondrously beautiful; the staff Zhen recruited were all literary men of the day, and excursions to Mirror Lake and Mount Qinwang came three or four times a month.
translations.idiomatic: The landscape of Kuaiji was wondrously beautiful; the staff he recruited were all leading literary men of the day, and he toured Mirror Lake and Mount Qinwang three or four times a month.

sentences.zh: 而諷詠詩什，動盈卷帙。

translations.literal: The poems he composed in response to occasions often filled whole scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The poems he composed on these outings often filled whole scrolls.

sentences.zh: 副使竇鞏，海內詩名，與稹酬唱最多，至今稱蘭亭絕唱。

translations.literal: His deputy Dou Gong, renowned throughout the realm for poetry, exchanged verses with Zhen more than any other; to this day their Lanting songs are called unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: His deputy Dou Gong, renowned throughout the realm for poetry, exchanged verses with Zhen more than any other; to this day their Lanting songs are called unmatched.

sentences.zh: 稹既放意娛遊，稍不修邊幅，以瀆貨聞於時。

translations.literal: Zhen gave himself over to pleasure and travel and paid little heed to personal decorum, gaining a reputation for corrupt enrichment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen gave himself over to pleasure and travel and paid little heed to personal decorum, gaining a reputation for corrupt enrichment.

sentences.zh: 凡在越八年。

translations.literal: In all he spent eight years in Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in Yue for eight years in all.

sentences.zh: 太和初，就加檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the early Taihe era he received an additional appointment as acting Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Taihe era he received an additional appointment as acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 三年九月，入為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year he entered the capital as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the third year he entered the capital as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 振舉紀綱，出郎官頗乖公議者七人。

translations.literal: He raised standards and regulations and removed seven bureau officials who had long fallen short of public consensus.
translations.idiomatic: He raised standards and regulations and removed seven bureau officials who had long fallen short of public consensus.

sentences.zh: 然以稹素無檢操，人情不厭服。

translations.literal: Yet because Zhen had never been restrained in conduct, popular sentiment did not willingly accept him.
