translations.idiomatic: Yet because Zhen had never been restrained in conduct, popular sentiment did not willingly accept him.

sentences.zh: 會宰相王播倉卒而卒，稹大為路歧，經營相位。

translations.literal: When the chief minister Wang Bo died suddenly, Zhen went to great lengths along the road, maneuvering for the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief minister Wang Bo died suddenly, Zhen went to great lengths along the road, maneuvering for the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，檢校戶部尚書，兼鄂州刺史、御史大夫、武昌軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he received an additional appointment as acting Minister of Revenue with concurrent posts as governor of Ezhou, grand censor, and military commissioner of the Wuchang army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he received an additional appointment as acting Minister of Revenue with concurrent posts as governor of Ezhou, grand censor, and military commissioner of the Wuchang army.

sentences.zh: 五年七月二十二日暴疾，一日而卒於鎮，時年五十三，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day of the seventh month of the fifth year he was seized by sudden illness and died at his post within a day, at the age of fifty-three; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second day of the seventh month of the fifth year he was seized by sudden illness and died at his post within a day, at the age of fifty-three; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 有子曰道護，時年三歲。

translations.literal: He had a son named Daohu, then three years old.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son named Daohu, then three years old.

sentences.zh: 稹仲兄司農少卿積，營護喪事。

translations.literal: Zhen's elder brother Ji, Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries, arranged the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's elder brother Ji, Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries, arranged the funeral.

sentences.zh: 所著詩賦、詔冊、銘誄、論議等雜文一百卷，號曰《元氏長慶集》。

translations.literal: His collected poems, fu, edicts, inscriptions, eulogies, discourses, and miscellaneous prose fill one hundred scrolls, entitled Collected Writings of Master Yuan of the Changqing Era.
translations.idiomatic: His collected poems, fu, edicts, inscriptions, eulogies, discourses, and miscellaneous prose fill one hundred scrolls, entitled Collected Writings of Master Yuan of the Changqing Era.

sentences.zh: 又著古今刑政書三百卷，號《類集》，並行於代。

translations.literal: He also compiled three hundred scrolls on penal administration ancient and modern, entitled Classified Compilations, and both works circulated in his age.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled three hundred scrolls on penal administration ancient and modern, entitled Classified Compilations, and both works circulated widely in his age.

sentences.zh: 稹長慶末因編刪其文稿，《自敘》曰：劉歆云：制不可削。

translations.literal: At the end of the Changqing era Zhen edited and abridged his collected writings; his "Self-Account" read: Liu Xin said: Institutions must not be cut away.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Changqing era he edited and abridged his collected writings; his "Self-Account" read: Liu Xin said: Institutions must not be cut away.

sentences.zh: 予以為有可得而削之者，貢謀猷，持嗜欲，君有之則譽歸於上，臣專之則譽歸於下。

translations.literal: I believe there are some that may be cut away: presenting plans and counsel, restraining appetites and desires—if the ruler possesses them, praise returns to the sovereign; if ministers monopolize them, praise returns to those below.
translations.idiomatic: I believe there are some that may be cut away: presenting plans and counsel, restraining appetites and desires—if the ruler possesses them, praise returns to the sovereign; if ministers monopolize them, praise returns to those below.

sentences.zh: 茍而存之，其攘也，非道也。

translations.literal: If they are kept, their usurpation is not the Way.
translations.idiomatic: If they are kept, their usurpation is not the Way.

sentences.zh: 經制度，明利害，區邪正，辨嫌惑，存之則事分著，去之則是非冺。

translations.literal: Passing through institutions, clarifying benefit and harm, distinguishing the wicked and upright, discerning suspicion and confusion—if kept, affairs are divided and clear; if removed, right and wrong are obscured.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through institutions, clarifying benefit and harm, distinguishing the wicked and upright, discerning suspicion and confusion—if kept, affairs are divided and clear; if removed, right and wrong are obscured.

sentences.zh: 茍而削之，其過也，非道也。

translations.literal: If they are cut away, the fault is not the Way.
translations.idiomatic: If they are cut away, the fault is not the Way.

sentences.zh: 元和初，章武皇帝新即位，臣下未有以言刮視聽者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, Emperor Muzong had newly ascended the throne, and among his subjects none yet spoke to cleanse his sight and hearing.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe, Emperor Muzong had newly ascended the throne, and among his subjects none yet spoke to cleanse his sight and hearing.

sentences.zh: 予時始以對詔在拾遺中供奉，由是獻《教本書》、《諫職》、《論事》等表十數通，仍為裴度、李正辭、韋熏訟所言當，而宰相曲道上語。

translations.literal: At that time I had just entered service among the remonstrance officials by imperial examination response, and thereby presented more than ten memorials including the Book on Foundations of Instruction, On the Duties of Remonstrance, and On Affairs; I also joined Pei Du, Li Zhengchen, and Wei Xun in litigation over what was said to be correct, while the chancellor twisted the way and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: At that time I had just entered service among the remonstrance officials by imperial examination response, and thereby presented more than ten memorials including the Book on Foundations of Instruction, On the Duties of Remonstrance, and On Affairs; I also joined Pei Du, Li Zhengchen, and Wei Xun in litigation over what was said to be correct, while the chancellor twisted the matter and reported upward.

sentences.zh: 上頗悟，召見問狀。

translations.literal: The sovereign was somewhat enlightened and summoned me to audience to inquire into the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign was somewhat enlightened and summoned me to audience to inquire into the matter.

sentences.zh: 宰相大惡之，不一月，出為河南尉。

translations.literal: The chancellor greatly hated this; within a month I was sent out as marshal of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor greatly hated this; within a month I was sent out as marshal of Henan.

sentences.zh: 後累歲，補御史，使東川。

translations.literal: After several years I was appointed censor and dispatched to Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: After several years I was appointed censor and dispatched to Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 謹以元和赦書，劾節度使嚴礪籍塗山甫等八十八家，過賦梓、遂之民數百萬。

translations.literal: In accordance with the Yuanhe amnesty edict, I impeached the military governor Yan Li for confiscating the property of Tu Shanfu and eighty-seven other households, over-taxing the people of Zi and Sui by several million.
translations.idiomatic: In accordance with the Yuanhe amnesty edict, I impeached the military governor Yan Li for confiscating the property of Tu Shanfu and eighty-seven other households, over-taxing the people of Zi and Sui by several million.

sentences.zh: 朝廷異之，奪七刺史料，悉以所籍歸於人。

translations.literal: The court was astonished, stripped him of seven grades of censorial authority, and returned all confiscated property to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The court was astonished, stripped him of seven grades of censorial authority, and returned all confiscated property to the people.

sentences.zh: 會潘孟陽代礪為節度使，貪過礪，且有所承迎，雖不敢盡廢詔，因命當得所籍者皆入資。

translations.literal: It happened that Pan Mengyang replaced Yan Li as military governor; he was greedier than Yan Li and moreover sought to curry favor. Though he did not dare wholly abolish the edict, he therefore ordered that all who should have received confiscated property must pay a fee to enter it.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Pan Mengyang replaced Yan Li as military governor; he was greedier than Yan Li and moreover sought to curry favor. Though he did not dare wholly abolish the edict, he therefore ordered that all who should have received confiscated property must pay a fee to obtain it.

sentences.zh: 資過其稱，榷薪盜賦無不為，仍為礪密狀不當得醜謚。

translations.literal: The fees exceeded their worth; monopolizing firewood and theft of taxes—nothing was left undone. He also submitted a secret memorial on Yan Li's behalf that he ought not receive an ugly posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: The fees exceeded their worth; he monopolized firewood and stole taxes—nothing was left undone. He also submitted a secret memorial on Yan Li's behalf that he ought not receive a disgraceful posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 予自東川還，朋礪者潛切齒矣。

translations.literal: When I returned from Dongchuan, Yan Li's partisans secretly ground their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: When I returned from Dongchuan, Yan Li's partisans secretly ground their teeth in hatred.

sentences.zh: 無何，分蒞東都臺。

translations.literal: Before long I was assigned to oversee the Eastern Capital Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Before long I was assigned to oversee the Eastern Capital Censorate.

sentences.zh: 天子久不在都，都下多不法者。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven had long been absent from the capital, and under the capital there were many lawless men.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven had long been absent from the capital, and in the capital there were many lawless men.

sentences.zh: 百司皆牢獄，有裁接吏械人逾歲而臺府不得而知之者，予因飛奏絕百司專禁錮。

translations.literal: Every office was a prison; there were receiving clerks who shackled men for more than a year while the censorate could not know of it. I therefore submitted an urgent memorial to forbid every office from exclusive imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: Every office was a prison; there were receiving clerks who shackled men for more than a year while the censorate could not know of it. I therefore submitted an urgent memorial to forbid every office from exclusive imprisonment.

sentences.zh: 河南尉判官，予劾之，忤宰相旨。

translations.literal: The Henan marshal's aide—I impeached him, offending the chancellor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: I impeached the Henan marshal's aide, offending the chancellor's intent.

sentences.zh: 監徐使死於軍，徐帥郵傳其柩，柩至洛，其下歐詬主郵吏，予命吏徙柩於外，不得復乘傳。

translations.literal: The supervisory commissioner of Xu died in the army; the Xu commander sent his coffin by post relay. When the coffin reached Luoyang, his subordinates beat and reviled the chief postal clerk. I ordered the clerks to move the coffin outside and forbade further use of post relay.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisory commissioner of Xu died in the army; the Xu commander sent his coffin by post relay. When the coffin reached Luoyang, his subordinates beat and reviled the chief postal clerk. I ordered the clerks to move the coffin outside and forbade further use of post relay.

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使封杖決安吉令至死；

translations.literal: The Zhexi observation commissioner sealed a staff and adjudged the magistrate of Anji to death;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhexi observation commissioner sealed a staff and adjudged the magistrate of Anji to death;

sentences.zh: 河南尹誣奏書生尹太階請死之；

translations.literal: the Henan governor falsely memorialized that the scholar Yin Taijie requested death;
translations.idiomatic: the Henan governor falsely memorialized that the scholar Yin Taijie requested death;

sentences.zh: 飛龍使誘趙寔家逃奴為養子；

translations.literal: the Feilong commissioner enticed a runaway slave of Zhao Shi's household to become an adopted son;
translations.idiomatic: the Feilong commissioner enticed a runaway slave of Zhao Shi's household to become an adopted son;

sentences.zh: 田季安盜娶洛陽衣冠女；

translations.literal: Tian Ji'an secretly married a genteel woman of Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Ji'an secretly married a genteel woman of Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 汴州沒入死商錢且千萬；

translations.literal: Bian Prefecture confiscated the money of a dead merchant, nearly ten million;
translations.idiomatic: Bian Prefecture confiscated the money of a dead merchant, nearly ten million;

sentences.zh: 滑州賦於民以千，授於人以八百；

translations.literal: Hua Prefecture levied a thousand from the people and handed over eight hundred to others;
translations.idiomatic: Hua Prefecture levied a thousand from the people and handed over only eight hundred;

sentences.zh: 朝廷饋東師，主計者誤命牛車四千三百乘飛芻越太行。

translations.literal: the court supplied the eastern army; the chief accountant mistakenly ordered four thousand three hundred ox carts to fly fodder over the Taihang Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: the court supplied the eastern army; the chief accountant mistakenly ordered four thousand three hundred ox carts to rush fodder over the Taihang Mountains.

sentences.zh: 類是數十事，或移或奏，皆主之。

translations.literal: Matters like these numbered in the dozens; whether by dispatch or memorial, I took charge of them all.
translations.idiomatic: Matters like these numbered in the dozens; whether by dispatch or memorial, I took charge of them all.

sentences.zh: 貞元已來，不慣用文法，內外寵臣皆喑嗚。

translations.literal: Since the Zhenyuan era, people were unaccustomed to using written law; favored ministers within and without all roared and clamored.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhenyuan era, people were unaccustomed to using written law; favored ministers within and without all roared and clamored.

sentences.zh: 會河南尹房式詐諼事發，奏攝之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Henan governor Fang Shi's fraud and false accusation came to light; I memorialized to take him into custody.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the Henan governor Fang Shi's fraud and false accusation came to light; I memorialized to take him into custody.

sentences.zh: 前所喑嗚者叫噪。

translations.literal: Those who had previously roared and clamored now shouted and made an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had previously roared and clamored now shouted and made an uproar.

sentences.zh: 宰相素以劾叛官事相銜，乘是黜予江陵掾。

translations.literal: The chancellor had long harbored resentment over my impeachment of a rebellious official; seizing this opportunity he dismissed me to aide in Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor had long harbored resentment over my impeachment of a rebellious official; seizing this opportunity he dismissed me to aide in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 後十年，始為膳部員外郎。

translations.literal: After ten years I was at last made vice director of the Board of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years I was at last made vice director of the Board of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 穆宗初，宰相更相用事，丞相段公一日獨得對，因請亟用兵部郎中薛存慶、考功員外郎牛僧孺，予亦在請中，上然之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Muzong's reign, chancellors alternated in wielding power. Chancellor Duan Wenchang one day alone obtained audience and thereupon requested the prompt use of Xue Cunqing, director of the Ministry of War, and Niu Sengru, vice director of the Ministry of Personnel examinations—I was also among those requested, and the sovereign approved.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Muzong's reign, chancellors alternated in wielding power. Chancellor Duan Wenchang one day alone obtained audience and thereupon requested the prompt appointment of Xue Cunqing, director of the Ministry of War, and Niu Sengru, vice director of the Ministry of Personnel examinations—I was also among those requested, and the sovereign approved.

sentences.zh: 不十數日次用為給、舍，他忿恨者日夜構飛語，予懼罪，比上書自明。

translations.literal: Within less than ten days I was next appointed drafting and palace aide; others who resented me day and night fabricated flying rumors. I feared punishment and repeatedly submitted memorials to clarify myself.
translations.idiomatic: Within less than ten days I was next appointed drafting and palace aide; others who resented me day and night fabricated flying rumors. I feared punishment and repeatedly submitted memorials to clarify myself.

sentences.zh: 上憐之，三召與語。

translations.literal: The sovereign pitied me and thrice summoned me to speak.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign pitied me and thrice summoned me to speak.

sentences.zh: 語及兵賦洎西北邊事，因命經紀之。

translations.literal: Our conversation reached military levies and northwestern border affairs, and he thereupon ordered me to manage them.
translations.idiomatic: Our conversation reached military levies and northwestern border affairs, and he thereupon ordered me to manage them.

sentences.zh: 是後書奏及進見，皆言天下事，外間不知，多臆度。

translations.literal: After this, in written memorials and audiences I spoke of affairs under Heaven; those outside did not know and mostly speculated.
translations.idiomatic: After this, in written memorials and audiences I spoke of affairs under Heaven; those outside did not know and mostly speculated.

sentences.zh: 陛下益憐其不漏禁中語，召入禁林，且欲亟用為宰相。

translations.literal: Your Majesty all the more pitied that I did not leak palace talk, summoned me into the forbidden grove, and wished to promptly use me as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty all the more valued that I did not leak palace talk, summoned me into the Hanlin Academy, and wished to promptly appoint me chancellor.

sentences.zh: 是時裴度在太原，亦有宰相望，巧者謀欲俱廢之，乃以予所無構於裴。

translations.literal: At that time Pei Du was in Taiyuan and also had prospects of chancellorship; the crafty plotted to abolish both together and therefore fabricated against Pei what I did not have.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Du was in Taiyuan and also had prospects of chancellorship; the crafty plotted to abolish both together and therefore fabricated against Pei charges that I had not made.

sentences.zh: 裴奏至，驗之皆失實。

translations.literal: Pei's memorial arrived; upon verification all was untrue.
translations.idiomatic: Pei's memorial arrived; upon verification all was untrue.

sentences.zh: 上以裴方握兵，不欲校曲直，出予為工部侍郎，而相裴之期亦衰矣。

translations.literal: The sovereign, because Pei was then holding troops, did not wish to judge right and wrong, and sent me out as vice minister of works; the prospect of Pei becoming chancellor also faded.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign, because Pei was then holding troops, did not wish to judge right and wrong, and sent me out as vice minister of works; the prospect of Pei becoming chancellor also faded.

sentences.zh: 不累月，上盡得所構者，雖不能暴揚之，遂果初意，卒用予與裴俱為宰相。

translations.literal: Within not many months the sovereign fully obtained those who had fabricated; though he could not publicly expose them, he then fulfilled his original intent and in the end used both me and Pei as chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Within not many months the sovereign fully obtained those who had fabricated; though he could not publicly expose them, he then fulfilled his original intent and in the end appointed both me and Pei as chancellors.

sentences.zh: 復有購狂民告予借客刺裴者，鞫之復無狀，而裴與予以故俱罷免。

translations.literal: Again there was one who bribed a mad commoner to report that I had borrowed a guest to assassinate Pei; upon interrogation again there was no substance, yet Pei and I were both dismissed for the old matter.
translations.idiomatic: Again someone bribed a mad commoner to report that I had borrowed a guest to assassinate Pei; upon interrogation again there was no substance, yet Pei and I were both dismissed for the old matter.

sentences.zh: 始元和十五年八月得見上，至是未二歲，僭忝恩寵，無是之速者；

translations.literal: From first seeing the sovereign in the eighth month of Yuanhe 15 to this time was not yet two years; presumptuously receiving favor and grace, none was so swift;
translations.idiomatic: From first seeing the sovereign in the eighth month of Yuanhe 15 to this time was not yet two years; presumptuously receiving favor and grace, none was so swift;

sentences.zh: 遭罹謗咎，亦無是之甚者。

translations.literal: suffering slander and blame, none was so severe.
translations.idiomatic: suffering slander and blame, none was so severe.

sentences.zh: 是以心腹腎腸，糜費於扶衛危亡之不暇，又惡暇經紀陛下之所付哉！

translations.literal: Thus heart, belly, kidneys, and bowels were wasted on supporting and defending in peril of destruction with no leisure—how could there be leisure to manage what Your Majesty entrusted!
translations.idiomatic: Thus heart and soul were consumed supporting and defending in peril of destruction with no leisure—how could there be leisure to manage what Your Majesty entrusted!

sentences.zh: 然而造次顛沛之中，前後列上兵賦邊防之狀，可得而存者一百一十五。

translations.literal: Yet amid haste and hardship, the military levy and border defense reports submitted before and after, of which copies can be preserved, number one hundred fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet amid haste and hardship, the military levy and border defense reports submitted before and after, of which copies can be preserved, number one hundred fifteen.

sentences.zh: 茍而削之，是傷先帝之器使也。

translations.literal: If they are cut away, this wounds the late emperor's employment of his vessel.
translations.idiomatic: If they are cut away, this wounds the late emperor's employment of his servant.

sentences.zh: 至於陳暢辨謗之章，去之則無以自明於朋友矣。

translations.literal: As for the chapters clarifying slander in full expression, if removed there would be no means to clarify myself before friends.
translations.idiomatic: As for the chapters clarifying slander in full expression, if removed there would be no means to clarify myself before friends.

sentences.zh: 其餘郡縣之奏請，賀慶之禮，因亦附於件目。

translations.literal: The rest—county and prefecture memorials and requests, congratulatory rites—are also appended to the list of items.
translations.idiomatic: The rest—county and prefecture memorials and requests, congratulatory rites—are also appended to the list of items.

sentences.zh: 始《教本書》，至於為人雜奏，二十有七軸，凡二百二十有七奏。

translations.literal: From the Book on Foundations of Instruction to miscellaneous memorials on behalf of others, there are twenty-seven scrolls, altogether two hundred twenty-seven memorials.
translations.idiomatic: From the Book on Foundations of Instruction to miscellaneous memorials on behalf of others, there are twenty-seven scrolls, altogether two hundred twenty-seven memorials.

sentences.zh: 終歿吾世，貽之子孫式，所以明經制之難行，而銷毀之易至也。

translations.literal: To the end of my life and death I bequeath them to descendants as a model, thereby making clear how hard institutions are to carry out and how easily destruction arrives.
translations.idiomatic: To the end of my life I bequeath them to descendants as a model, thereby making clear how hard institutions are to carry out and how easily destruction arrives.

sentences.zh: 其自敘如此，欲知其作者之意，備於此篇。

translations.literal: His self-account is as above; those who wish to know the author's intent will find it fully set forth in that piece.
translations.idiomatic: His self-account is as above; those who wish to know the author's intent will find it fully set forth in that piece.

sentences.zh: 稹文友與白居易最善。

translations.literal: Among Zhen's literary friends, Bai Juyi was closest.
translations.idiomatic: Of Zhen's literary friends, none was closer than Bai Juyi.

sentences.zh: 後進之士，最重龐嚴，言其文體類己，保薦之。

translations.literal: Junior scholars held Pang Yan in highest regard, saying his literary style resembled Zhen's own, and Zhen recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Younger writers esteemed Pang Yan most highly, saying his style resembled Zhen's, and Zhen recommended him.

sentences.zh: 龐嚴者，壽春人。

translations.literal: Pang Yan, Pang Yan, was a man of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Yan came from Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 父景昭。

translations.literal: His father was Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 嚴元和中登進士第，長慶元年應制舉賢良方正、能直言極諫科，策入三等，冠制科之首。

translations.literal: Yan passed the jinshi examination in the Yuanhe era; in the first year of Changqing he entered the special examination for worthy and upright men able to speak blunt remonstrance, his policy essay placing in the third grade and ranking first among those in the special examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yan passed the jinshi in the Yuanhe era; in the first year of Changqing he entered the special examination for worthy and upright men able to speak blunt remonstrance, placing third in grade and ranking first among the special-examination candidates.

sentences.zh: 是月，拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: That month he was appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he was appointed Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 聰敏絕人，文章峭麗。

translations.literal: His intelligence surpassed others, and his writing was sharp and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: He was exceptionally intelligent, and his prose was sharp and elegant.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士元稹、李紳頗知之。

translations.literal: Hanlin academicians Yuan Zhen and Li Shen knew him well.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin academicians Yuan Zhen and Li Shen knew him well.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year he was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as academician.

sentences.zh: 轉左補闕，再遷駕部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Supplementation Officer, then promoted again to director of the Carriages Bureau with charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Supplementation Officer, then promoted to director of the Carriages Bureau with charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 嚴與右拾遺蔣防俱為稹、紳保薦，至諫官內職。

translations.literal: Yan and the Right Reminder Jiang Fang were both recommended by Zhen and Shen to remonstrance posts and inner-court offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and the Right Reminder Jiang Fang were both recommended by Zhen and Shen for remonstrance posts and inner-court offices.

sentences.zh: 四年，昭湣即位，李紳為宰相李逢吉所排，貶端州司馬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Emperor Zhaomin ascended the throne; Li Shen was ousted by the chief minister Li Fengji and demoted to marshal of Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Emperor Zhaomin ascended the throne, Li Shen was ousted by the chief minister Li Fengji and demoted to marshal of Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 嚴坐累，出為江州刺史。

translations.literal: Yan was implicated and sent out as governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was implicated by association and sent out as governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 給事中於敖素與嚴善，制既下，敖封還，時人凜然相顧曰：「於給事犯宰相怒而為知己，不亦危乎！」

translations.literal: The Attendant-in-Ordinary Yu Ao had long been friendly with Yan; once the appointment edict was issued, Ao sealed it and returned it, and people at court looked at one another in alarm and said: "Attendant Yu has offended the chief minister's wrath for the sake of a friend—is he not in peril?"
translations.idiomatic: The Attendant-in-Ordinary Yu Ao had long been friendly with Yan; when the appointment edict was issued, Ao sealed it and returned it, and people at court looked at one another in alarm and said, "Attendant Yu has offended the chief minister's wrath for a friend's sake—is he not in peril?"

sentences.zh: 及覆制出，乃知敖駁制書貶嚴太輕，中外無不嗤誚，以為口實。

translations.literal: When the revised edict was issued, it turned out Ao had rejected the draft as punishing Yan too lightly; inside and outside the court none failed to mock and cite it as a byword.
translations.idiomatic: When the revised edict appeared, it turned out Ao had rejected the draft as punishing Yan too lightly; court and populace alike mocked the affair and made it a byword.

sentences.zh: 初李紳謫官，朝官皆賀逢吉，唯右拾遺吳思不賀。

translations.literal: When Li Shen was first demoted, court officials all congratulated Fengji; only the Right Reminder Wu Si did not congratulate him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shen was first demoted, court officials all congratulated Fengji; only the Right Reminder Wu Si refused to join them.

sentences.zh: 逢吉怒，改為殿中侍御史，充入蕃告哀使。

translations.literal: Fengji in anger transferred him to palace censor and appointed him envoy to announce mourning in a foreign land.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji in anger transferred him to palace censor and appointed him envoy to announce mourning in a foreign land.

sentences.zh: 嚴復入為庫部郎中。

translations.literal: Yan was recalled and made director of the Storehouses Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was recalled and made director of the Storehouses Bureau.

sentences.zh: 太和二年二月，上試制舉人，命嚴與左散騎常侍馮宿、太常少卿賈餗為試官，以裴休為甲等制科之首。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Taihe the emperor tested special-examination candidates and appointed Yan, together with the Left Regular Attendant Feng Su and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Jia Su, as examiners, with Pei Xiu ranking first in the top grade of the special examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Taihe the emperor tested special-examination candidates and appointed Yan, together with the Left Regular Attendant Feng Su and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Jia Su, as examiners, with Pei Xiu ranking first in the top grade of the special examination.

sentences.zh: 有應直言極諫舉人劉蕡，條對激切，凡數千言。

translations.literal: There was a candidate in the blunt remonstrance examination, Liu Fen, whose itemized responses were fiercely incisive, running to several thousand words in all.
translations.idiomatic: Among the candidates for blunt remonstrance was Liu Fen, whose itemized responses were fiercely incisive, running to several thousand words in all.

sentences.zh: 不中選，人鹹以為屈。

translations.literal: He was not selected, and people all regarded it as unjust.
translations.idiomatic: He was not selected, and people widely regarded it as unjust.

sentences.zh: 其所對策，大行於時，登科者有請以身名授蕡者。

translations.literal: His policy essay circulated greatly at the time, and among those who had passed the examination some asked to yield their fame to Fen.
translations.idiomatic: His policy essay circulated widely at the time, and some who had passed the examination offered to yield their fame to Fen.

sentences.zh: 嚴再遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: Yan was promoted again to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was promoted again to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 五年，權知京兆尹，以強幹不避權豪稱，然無士君子之檢操，貪勢嗜利。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he served as acting metropolitan intendant of Jingzhao, praised for being forceful and unafraid of powerful families, yet he lacked the restraint of a gentleman-scholar and was greedy for power and profit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he served as acting metropolitan intendant of Jingzhao, praised for being forceful and unafraid of powerful families, yet he lacked a gentleman-scholar's restraint and was greedy for power and profit.

sentences.zh: 因醉而卒。

translations.literal: He died of drunkenness.
translations.idiomatic: He died in a drunken stupor.

sentences.zh: 白居易，字樂天，太原人。

translations.literal: Bai Juyi, Bai Juyi, style name Letian, was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Juyi, whose courtesy name was Letian, came from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 北齊五兵尚書建之仍孫。

translations.literal: He was the great-grandson of Jian of the Northern Qi, who had been Minister of the Five Armies.
translations.idiomatic: He was the great-grandson of Jian, Minister of the Five Armies under the Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 建生士通，皇朝利州都督。

translations.literal: Jian begot Shitong, military governor of Lizhou in the present dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Jian begot Shitong, who served as military governor of Lizhou in the present dynasty.

sentences.zh: 士通生志善，尚衣奉御。

translations.literal: Shitong begot Zhishan, Attendant for Imperial Vestments.
translations.idiomatic: Shitong begot Zhishan, Attendant for Imperial Vestments.

sentences.zh: 志善生溫，檢校都官郎中。

translations.literal: Zhishan begot Wen, acting director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishan begot Wen, acting director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 溫生锽，歷酸棗、鞏二縣令。

translations.literal: Wen begot Huang, who served in turn as magistrate of Suozao and Gong counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wen begot Huang, who served in turn as magistrate of Suozao and Gong counties.

sentences.zh: 锽生季庚，建中初為彭城令。

translations.literal: Huang begot Jigeng, who in the early Jianzhong era was magistrate of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huang begot Jigeng, who in the early Jianzhong era was magistrate of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 時李正己據河南十餘州叛。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zhengji held more than ten prefectures south of the Yellow River in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Zhengji held more than ten prefectures south of the Yellow River in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 正己宗人洧為徐州刺史，季庚說洧以彭門歸國，因授朝散大夫、大理少卿、徐州別駕，賜緋魚袋，兼徐泗觀察判官。

translations.literal: Zhengji's clansman Wei was military governor of Xuzhou; Jigeng persuaded Wei to return Pengmen to the state, and for this he was granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, Xuzhou vice governor, a crimson fish bag, and concurrent appointment as administrative aide to the Xuzhou-Si surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengji's clansman Wei was military governor of Xuzhou; Jigeng persuaded Wei to return Pengmen to the state, and for this he was granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, Xuzhou vice governor, a crimson fish bag, and concurrent appointment as administrative aide to the Xuzhou-Si surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歷衢州、襄州別駕。

translations.literal: He served in turn as vice governor of Quzhou and Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as vice governor of Quzhou and Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 自锽至季庚，世敦儒業，皆以明經出身。

translations.literal: From Huang down to Jigeng, the family cultivated Confucian learning for generations, all entering office through the Classics examinations.
translations.idiomatic: From Huang down to Jigeng, the family cultivated Confucian learning for generations, all entering office through the Classics examinations.

sentences.zh: 季庚生居易。

translations.literal: Jigeng begot Juyi.
translations.idiomatic: Jigeng begot Juyi.

sentences.zh: 初，建立功於高齊，賜田於韓城，子孫家焉，遂移籍同州。

translations.literal: At first Jian had rendered meritorious service to the Northern Qi and was granted fields in Hancheng; the family settled there and later transferred their registry to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At first Jian had rendered meritorious service to the Northern Qi and was granted fields in Hancheng; the family settled there and later transferred their registry to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 至溫徙於下邽，今為下邽人焉。

translations.literal: When Wen moved to Xiaji, they became men of Xiaji; today they are registered as men of Xiaji.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen moved to Xiaji, the family settled there; today they are registered as men of Xiaji.

sentences.zh: 居易幼聰慧絕人，襟懷宏放。

translations.literal: Juyi in youth was exceptionally intelligent, with a broad and expansive spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi in youth was exceptionally intelligent, with a broad and expansive spirit.

sentences.zh: 年十五六時，袖文一編，投著作郎吳人顧況。

translations.literal: When he was fifteen or sixteen he tucked a literary manuscript under his sleeve and presented it to Gu Kuang, a native of Wu who was an editorial director.
translations.idiomatic: When he was fifteen or sixteen he tucked a literary manuscript under his sleeve and presented it to Gu Kuang, a native of Wu who was an editorial director.

sentences.zh: 況能文，而性浮薄，後進文章無可意者。

translations.literal: Kuang could write but was by nature frivolous; he found nothing satisfactory in the writings of junior scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang could write but was by nature frivolous; he found nothing satisfactory in the writings of junior scholars.

sentences.zh: 覽居易文，不覺迎門禮遇，曰：「吾謂斯文遂絕，復得吾子矣。」

translations.literal: Reading Juyi's essay, he could not help but go out to the gate to receive him with courtesy and said: "I thought this literary tradition had perished; I have found you again."
translations.idiomatic: Reading Juyi's essay, he could not help but go out to the gate to receive him with courtesy and said, "I thought this literary tradition had perished; I have found you again."

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年，始以進士就試，禮部侍郎高郢擢升甲科，吏部判入等，授秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan he first took the jinshi examination; Vice Director of Rites Gao Ying elevated him to the top grade, the Ministry of Personnel assessment placed him in grade, and he was appointed proofreader in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan he first took the jinshi examination; Vice Director of Rites Gao Ying elevated him to the top grade, the Ministry of Personnel assessment placed him in grade, and he was appointed proofreader in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 元和元年四月，憲宗策試制舉人，應才識兼茂、明於體用科，策入第四等，授盩厔縣慰、集賢校理。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yuanhe Emperor Xianzong tested special-examination candidates; Juyi entered the examination for outstanding talent and practical understanding, his policy placing in the fourth grade, and he was appointed magistrate of Zhouzhi and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Yuanhe Emperor Xianzong tested special-examination candidates; Juyi entered the examination for outstanding talent and practical understanding, his policy placing in the fourth grade, and he was appointed magistrate of Zhouzhi and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 居易文辭富艷，尤精於詩筆。

translations.literal: Juyi's literary compositions were rich and gorgeous, and he was especially skilled in poetic writing.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi's literary compositions were rich and gorgeous, and he was especially skilled in poetic writing.

sentences.zh: 自讎校至結綬畿甸，所著歌詩數十百篇，皆意存諷賦，箴時之病，補政之缺。

translations.literal: From proofreading through receiving his sash in the capital region, the songs and poems he composed numbered dozens or hundreds, all intending satirical expression, admonishing the ills of the age and repairing the gaps in governance.
translations.idiomatic: From proofreading through receiving his sash in the capital region, the songs and poems he composed numbered dozens or hundreds, all intending satirical expression, admonishing the ills of the age and repairing the gaps in governance.

sentences.zh: 而士君子多之，而往往流聞禁中。

translations.literal: Gentlemen and scholars mostly approved of them, and they often flowed into hearsay within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen and scholars mostly approved of them, and they often reached the ears of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 章武皇帝納諫思理，渴聞讜言，二年十一月，召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhangwu, wishing to receive remonstrance and ponder governance, was eager to hear blunt counsel; in the eleventh month of the second year he summoned Juyi into the Hanlin Academy as academician.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhangwu, wishing to receive remonstrance and ponder governance, was eager to hear blunt counsel; in the eleventh month of the second year he summoned Juyi into the Hanlin Academy as academician.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year he was appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year he was appointed Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 居易自以逢好文之主，非次拔擢，欲以生平所貯，仰酬恩造。

translations.literal: Juyi considered that he had encountered a sovereign who loved literature and had been raised out of turn; he wished to offer up what he had stored through his life to repay the grace of his elevation.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi considered that he had encountered a sovereign who loved literature and had been raised out of turn; he wished to offer up what he had stored through his life to repay the grace of his elevation.

sentences.zh: 拜命之日，獻疏言事曰：蒙恩授臣左拾遺，依前翰林學士，已與崔群同狀陳謝。

translations.literal: On the day he received his appointment, he submitted a memorial on affairs of state, which read: Receiving grace, Your Majesty appointed this subject Left Reminder, continuing as before as Hanlin academician; I have already submitted a joint memorial of thanks with Cui Qun.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he received his appointment, he submitted a memorial on affairs of state, which read: Receiving your grace, you appointed me Left Reminder while continuing me as Hanlin academician; I have already submitted a joint memorial of thanks with Cui Qun.

sentences.zh: 但言忝冒，未吐衷誠。

translations.literal: I spoke only of unworthy acceptance and did not express my inner sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: I spoke only of unworthy acceptance and did not express my inner sincerity.

sentences.zh: 今再瀆宸嚴，伏惟重賜詳覽。

translations.literal: Now again offending the imperial presence, I humbly beg that you again bestow careful reading.
translations.idiomatic: Now again intruding upon your imperial presence, I humbly beg your careful reading once more.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按《六典》，左右拾遺，掌供奉諷諫，凡發令舉事，有不便於時、不合於道者，小則上封，大則廷諍。

translations.literal: This subject respectfully consults the Administrative Compendium: the Left and Right Reminders oversee attendance and admonition; whenever orders are issued or affairs undertaken that are inconvenient to the times or not in accord with the Way, for small matters they submit sealed memorials, for great matters they remonstrate at court.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully consult the Administrative Compendium: the Left and Right Reminders oversee attendance and admonition; whenever orders or undertakings are inconvenient to the times or not in accord with the Way, for small matters they submit sealed memorials, for great matters they remonstrate at court.

sentences.zh: 其選甚重，其秩甚卑，所以然者，抑有由也。

translations.literal: Their selection is very weighty, their rank very low; the reason it is so indeed has a cause.
translations.idiomatic: Their selection is weighty, their rank low; there is indeed a reason for this.

sentences.zh: 大凡人之情，位高則惜其位，身貴則愛其身；

translations.literal: Generally speaking, in human feeling, when position is high one cherishes one's position, when the person is noble one loves one's person;
translations.idiomatic: Generally speaking, when position is high one cherishes one's position, when status is exalted one loves one's person;

sentences.zh: 惜位則偷合而不言，愛身則茍容而不諫，此必然之理也。

translations.literal: cherishing position then one steals agreement and does not speak; loving one's person then one is compliant and does not remonstrate—this is the inevitable principle.
translations.idiomatic: cherish position and one steals agreement without speaking; love one's person and one is compliant without remonstrating—this is inevitable.

sentences.zh: 故拾遺之置，所以卑其秩者，使位未足惜，身未足愛也。

translations.literal: Therefore in establishing the Reminders, the reason their rank is made low is to make position not yet worth cherishing and person not yet worth loving.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Reminders are given low rank so that position is not yet worth cherishing and person not yet worth loving.

sentences.zh: 所以重其選者，使下不忍負心，上不忍負恩也。

translations.literal: The reason their selection is made weighty is to make subordinates unable to bear betraying their hearts and superiors unable to bear betraying grace.
translations.idiomatic: Their selection is made weighty so that subordinates cannot bear to betray their hearts and superiors cannot bear to betray grace.

sentences.zh: 夫位不足惜，恩不忍負，然後能有闕必規，有違必諫。

translations.literal: When position is not worth cherishing and grace cannot be betrayed, only then can one where there are faults certainly admonish and where there are violations certainly remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: When position is not worth cherishing and grace cannot be betrayed, only then can one admonish wherever there are faults and remonstrate wherever there are violations.

sentences.zh: 朝廷得失無不察，天下利病無不言。

translations.literal: The court's gains and losses are all examined; the realm's benefits and harms are all spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: The court's gains and losses are all examined; the realm's benefits and harms are all spoken of.

sentences.zh: 此國朝置拾遺之本意也。

translations.literal: This is the original intent of our dynasty in establishing the Reminders.
translations.idiomatic: This is our dynasty's original intent in establishing the Reminders.

sentences.zh: 由是而言，豈小臣愚劣暗懦所宜居之哉？

translations.literal: Speaking from this, how could it be a post fit for a petty minister stupid, inferior, and timid?
translations.idiomatic: From this perspective, how could it be a post fit for a petty minister as stupid, inferior, and timid as I?

sentences.zh: 況臣本鄉校豎儒，府縣走吏，委心泥滓，絕望煙霄。

translations.literal: Moreover this subject was originally a village-school pedant and a runner-clerk in prefecture and county; my heart was cast into the mire, my hopes cut off from the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I was originally a village-school pedant and a runner-clerk in prefecture and county; my heart was cast into the mire, my hopes cut off from the clouds.

sentences.zh: 豈意聖慈，擢居近職，每宴飲無不先預，每慶賜無不先沾，中廄之馬代其勞，內廚之膳給其食。

translations.literal: Who would have thought of sagely kindness raising me to a nearby post: at every feast and drink I was invariably first to attend, at every celebratory bestowal invariably first to receive benefit; the imperial stable's horses bore my labor, the inner kitchen's meals supplied my food.
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought your sagely kindness would raise me to a nearby post: at every feast I was first to attend, at every celebratory bestowal first to benefit; the imperial stable's horses bore my labor, the inner kitchen's meals supplied my food.

sentences.zh: 朝慚夕惕，已逾半年，塵曠漸深，憂愧彌劇。

translations.literal: Morning ashamed, evening wary, already more than half a year; the dust of neglect grows deeper, worry and shame grow keener.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed morning and wary evening for more than half a year, the dust of neglect grows deeper and my worry and shame grow keener.

sentences.zh: 未申微效，又擢清班。

translations.literal: Before I had rendered the slightest service, I was again promoted to the pure ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Before I had rendered the slightest service, I was again promoted to the pure ranks.

sentences.zh: 臣所以授官已來僅經十日，食不知味，寢不遑安。

translations.literal: Therefore since receiving office it has been only ten days; in eating I do not know flavor, in sleeping I have no leisure for rest.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, in the ten days since receiving office, I have eaten without tasting and slept without rest.

sentences.zh: 唯思粉身以答殊寵，但未獲粉身之所耳。

translations.literal: I think only of grinding my body to repay extraordinary favor, yet have not yet obtained the place to grind my body.
translations.idiomatic: I think only of giving my body to repay extraordinary favor, yet have not yet found the occasion to do so.

sentences.zh: 今陛下肇臨皇極，初受鴻名，夙夜憂勤，以求致理。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has newly ascended the imperial pinnacle and first received the great name; day and night anxious and diligent, seeking to bring order.
translations.idiomatic: Now you have newly ascended the throne and first received the great name; day and night anxious and diligent, seeking to bring order.

sentences.zh: 每施一政、舉一事，無不合於道、便於時者。

translations.literal: Whenever you enact a policy or undertake an affair, none fails to accord with the Way and suit the times.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever you enact a policy or undertake an affair, none fails to accord with the Way and suit the times.

sentences.zh: 萬一事有不便於時者，陛下豈不欲聞之乎？

translations.literal: If by chance there is an affair inconvenient to the times, would Your Majesty not wish to hear of it?
translations.idiomatic: If by chance there is an affair inconvenient to the times, would you not wish to hear of it?

sentences.zh: 萬一政有不合於道者，陛下豈不欲知之乎？

translations.literal: If by chance there is a policy not in accord with the Way, would Your Majesty not wish to know of it?
translations.idiomatic: If by chance there is a policy not in accord with the Way, would you not wish to know of it?

sentences.zh: 倘陛下言動之際，詔令之間，小有闕遺，稍關損益，臣必密陳所見，潛獻所聞，但在聖心裁斷而已。

translations.literal: If in Your Majesty's words and actions, among edicts and orders, there are small omissions or slight matters bearing on benefit and harm, this subject will certainly secretly set forth what I have seen and quietly present what I have heard—only awaiting the sagely heart's judgment.
translations.idiomatic: If in your words and actions, among edicts and orders, there are small omissions or slight matters bearing on benefit and harm, I will secretly set forth what I have seen and quietly present what I have heard—only awaiting your judgment.

sentences.zh: 臣又職在禁中，不同外司，欲竭愚誠，合先陳露。

translations.literal: This subject's duties are moreover within the forbidden precincts, unlike outer offices; wishing to exhaust my foolish sincerity, I ought first to disclose it.
translations.idiomatic: My duties are moreover within the forbidden precincts, unlike outer offices; wishing to exhaust my sincerity, I ought first to disclose it.

sentences.zh: 伏希天鑒，深察赤誠。

translations.literal: I humbly hope for Heaven's discernment and deep perception of my red sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope for Heaven's discernment and deep perception of my sincerity.

sentences.zh: 居易與河南元稹相善，同年登制舉，交情隆厚。

translations.literal: Juyi was on friendly terms with Yuan Zhen of Henan; they had passed the special examination in the same year and their friendship was deep and thick.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi was on friendly terms with Yuan Zhen of Henan; they had passed the special examination in the same year and their friendship was deep and thick.

sentences.zh: 稹自監察御史謫為江陵府士曹掾，翰林學士李絳、崔群上前面論稹無罪，居易累疏切諫曰：

translations.literal: When Zhen was demoted from investigating censor to army staff officer of Jiangling prefecture, Hanlin academicians Li Jiang and Cui Qun spoke to the emperor's face arguing that Zhen was guiltless; Juyi submitted memorial after memorial in blunt remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen was demoted from investigating censor to army staff officer of Jiangling prefecture, Hanlin academicians Li Jiang and Cui Qun spoke to the emperor's face arguing that Zhen was guiltless; Juyi submitted memorial after memorial in blunt remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣內察事情，外聽眾議，元稹左降有不可者三。

translations.literal: This subject inwardly examined the matter and outwardly listened to public discussion; Yuan Zhen's demotion has three points that must not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Having examined the matter inwardly and listened to public discussion outwardly, I find three reasons Yuan Zhen's demotion must not stand.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: What are they?
translations.idiomatic: What are they?

sentences.zh: 元稹守官正直，人所共知。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhen in holding office is upright; all men know it.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knows that Yuan Zhen is upright in office.

sentences.zh: 自授御史已來，舉奏不避權勢，只如奏李佐公等事，多是朝廷親情。

translations.literal: Since receiving appointment as censor, in impeachments and memorials he has not avoided power and influence; matters such as memorializing against Li Zuogong and others mostly involved court intimates and kin.
translations.idiomatic: Since his appointment as censor, he has not shied from power and influence in his impeachments; cases such as his memorial against Li Zuogong and others mostly involved court intimates and kin.

sentences.zh: 人誰無私，因以挾恨，或假公議，將報私嫌，遂使誣謗之聲，上聞天聽。

translations.literal: Who among men is without private feeling? Accordingly they harbor resentment, or borrow public discussion to repay private grudges, so that slanderous voices reach the imperial ear.
translations.idiomatic: Who is without private feeling? Resentment has been harbored; public discussion has been borrowed to settle private grudges, and slander has reached Your Majesty's ears.

sentences.zh: 臣恐元稹左降已後，凡在位者，每欲舉職，必先以稹為誡，無人肯為陛下當官守法，無人肯為陛下嫉惡繩愆。

translations.literal: This subject fears that after Yuan Zhen's demotion, all who hold office, whenever they wish to perform their duties, will first take Zhen as a warning; no one will be willing to hold office and uphold the law for Your Majesty, no one willing to hate evil and restrain transgression for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that after Zhen's demotion, every official who wishes to perform his duties will first take him as a warning; no one will be willing to hold office and uphold the law for you, or to hate evil and restrain wrongdoing on your behalf.

sentences.zh: 內外權貴親黨，縱有大過大罪者，必相容隱而已，陛下從此無由得知。

translations.literal: Inside and outside, powerful nobles and their kin, even if they have great faults and great crimes, will only cover and conceal one another; Your Majesty from this will have no means of learning of it.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful nobles and their kin, inside and outside the court, will only cover for one another no matter how grave their faults; from this you will have no way to learn of them.

sentences.zh: 此其不可者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first point that must not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first reason it must not stand.

sentences.zh: 昨元稹所追勘房式之事，心雖徇公，事稍過當。

translations.literal: Yesterday, in the matter of Fang Shi that Yuan Zhen pursued and investigated, though his heart followed public duty, the affair was somewhat excessive.
translations.idiomatic: In yesterday's matter of Fang Shi, which Zhen pursued and investigated, his heart followed public duty, but the affair was somewhat excessive.

sentences.zh: 既從重罰，足以懲違，況經謝恩，旋又左降。

translations.literal: He has already received heavy punishment, sufficient to chastise transgression; moreover he had already thanked for imperial grace, yet was again demoted to a lower post.
translations.idiomatic: He has already received heavy punishment, enough to chastise the offense; moreover, he had already thanked you for imperial grace, yet was again demoted.

sentences.zh: 雖引前事以為責辭，然外議喧喧，皆以為稹與中使劉士元爭廳，因此獲罪。

translations.literal: Although earlier matters were cited as grounds for reproach, yet outside discussion is clamorous, all holding that Zhen quarreled with the palace envoy Liu Shiyuan over quarters and for this received punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Although earlier matters were cited as grounds for reproach, public talk is loud: all believe Zhen was punished because he quarreled with the palace envoy Liu Shiyuan over quarters.

sentences.zh: 至於爭廳事理，已具前狀奏陳。

translations.literal: As for the rights and wrongs of the quarrel over quarters, they have already been fully set forth in the previous memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The rights and wrongs of the quarrel over quarters have already been fully set forth in my previous memorial.

sentences.zh: 況聞士元蹋破驛門，奪將鞍馬，仍索弓箭，嚇辱朝官，承前已來，未有此事。

translations.literal: Moreover one hears that Shiyuan kicked through the relay station gate, seized a general's saddle and horse, and still demanded bow and arrows, terrifying and insulting court officials; from former times until now there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I have heard that Shiyuan kicked through the relay station gate, seized a general's saddle and horse, and still demanded bow and arrows, terrifying and insulting court officials; nothing like this has ever occurred before.

sentences.zh: 今中官有罪，未聞處置；

translations.literal: Now the palace official has guilt, yet no disposition has been heard of;
translations.idiomatic: Now the palace official is guilty, yet no punishment has been heard of;

sentences.zh: 御史無過，卻先貶官。

translations.literal: the censor is without fault, yet was first demoted.
translations.idiomatic: yet the censor, though without fault, was demoted first.

sentences.zh: 遠近聞知，實損聖德。

translations.literal: Near and far, on hearing of it, it truly damages sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far, all who hear of it know that it truly damages your sagely virtue.

sentences.zh: 臣恐從今已後，中官出使，縱暴益甚；

translations.literal: This subject fears that from now on, when palace officials go on missions, unrestrained violence will grow still worse;
translations.idiomatic: I fear that from now on, when palace officials go on missions, unrestrained violence will grow still worse;

sentences.zh: 朝官受辱，必不敢言。

translations.literal: court officials who suffer insult will certainly not dare to speak.
translations.idiomatic: court officials who suffer insult will certainly not dare to speak out.

sentences.zh: 縱有被淩辱毆打者，亦以元稹為戒，但吞聲而已。

translations.literal: Even if there are those who are insulted and beaten, they too will take Yuan Zhen as a warning and only swallow their voices.
translations.idiomatic: Even those who are insulted and beaten will take Zhen as a warning and only swallow their voices.

sentences.zh: 陛下從此無由得聞。

translations.literal: Your Majesty from this will have no means of hearing of it.
translations.idiomatic: From this you will have no way to hear of it.

sentences.zh: 此其不可二也。

translations.literal: This is the second point that must not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second reason it must not stand.

sentences.zh: 臣又訪聞元稹自去年已來，舉奏嚴礪在東川日枉法，沒入平人資產八十餘家；

translations.literal: This subject has also inquired and heard that since last year Yuan Zhen has memorialized that Yan Li, during his days in eastern Shu, violated the law and confiscated the property of more than eighty households of common people;
translations.idiomatic: I have also learned that since last year Zhen has memorialized that Yan Li, during his days in eastern Shu, violated the law and confiscated the property of more than eighty common households;

sentences.zh: 又奏王沼違法給券，令監軍押柩及家口入驛；

translations.literal: he also memorialized that Wang Zhao illegally issued passes, ordering the military supervisor to escort the coffin and household members into the relay station;
translations.idiomatic: he also memorialized that Wang Zhao illegally issued passes, ordering the military supervisor to escort the coffin and household members into the relay station;

sentences.zh: 又奏裴玢違敕征百姓草；

translations.literal: he also memorialized that Pei Bin violated an imperial order in levying fodder from the common people;
translations.idiomatic: he also memorialized that Pei Bin violated an imperial order in levying fodder from the common people;

sentences.zh: 又奏韓臯使軍將封杖打殺縣令。

translations.literal: he also memorialized that Han Gao had a military officer beat the county magistrate to death with a sealed staff.
translations.idiomatic: he also memorialized that Han Gao had a military officer beat the county magistrate to death with a sealed staff.

sentences.zh: 如此之事，前後甚多，屬朝廷法行，悉有懲罰。

translations.literal: Matters such as these, before and after, are very numerous; when the court's law was applied, all received punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Such matters are very numerous; when the court applied the law, all received punishment.

sentences.zh: 計天下方鎮，皆怒元稹守官。

translations.literal: Considering it, the military governors throughout the realm are all angry at Yuan Zhen for upholding office.
translations.idiomatic: I reckon that the military governors throughout the realm are all angry at Zhen for upholding his office.

sentences.zh: 今貶為江陵判司，即是送與方鎮，從此方便報怨，朝廷何由得知？

translations.literal: Now demoted to judicial adjutant at Jiangling, this is in effect delivering him to the military governors; from this they will conveniently repay their grudges—how is the court to learn of it?
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is demoted to judicial adjutant at Jiangling, he is in effect delivered to the military governors; from this they can conveniently settle their grudges—how is the court to learn of it?

sentences.zh: 臣伏聞德宗時有崔善貞者，告李锜必反，德宗不信，送與李锜，锜掘坑熾火，燒殺善貞。

translations.literal: This subject humbly has heard that in the time of Emperor Dezong there was one Cui Shanzhen who reported that Li Qi would certainly rebel; Dezong did not believe him and sent him to Li Qi, and Qi dug a pit, kindled a fire, and burned Shanzhen to death.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly recall that in Emperor Dezong's time Cui Shanzhen reported that Li Qi would certainly rebel; Dezong did not believe him and sent him to Li Qi, who dug a pit, kindled a fire, and burned Shanzhen to death.

sentences.zh: 曾未數年，李锜果反，至今天下為之痛心。

translations.literal: Before several years had passed, Li Qi did in fact rebel; to this day all under Heaven grieves over it.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years Li Qi did rebel; to this day the realm grieves over it.

sentences.zh: 臣恐元稹貶官，方鎮有過，無人敢言，陛下無由得知不法之事。

translations.literal: This subject fears that with Yuan Zhen demoted, when military governors have faults no one will dare to speak, and Your Majesty will have no means of learning of unlawful matters.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that with Zhen demoted, when military governors commit faults no one will dare speak, and you will have no way to learn of unlawful conduct.

sentences.zh: 此其不可者三也。

translations.literal: This is the third point that must not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third reason it must not stand.

sentences.zh: 若無此三不可，假如朝廷誤左降一御史，蓋是小事，臣安敢煩瀆聖聽，至於再三！

translations.literal: If there were not these three points that must not be allowed, supposing the court mistakenly demoted one censor to a lower post, it would merely be a small matter—how would this subject dare to trouble and offend the imperial ear, even to the point of repeating it again and again!
translations.idiomatic: Were it not for these three reasons, a mistaken demotion of one censor would be a small matter—how would I dare trouble your imperial ear again and again!

sentences.zh: 誠以所損者深，所關者大，以此思慮，敢不極言！

translations.literal: Truly because what is harmed is deep and what is involved is great, with this in mind, how would I not dare speak to the utmost!
translations.idiomatic: Truly, because the harm is deep and the stakes are great, with this in mind I cannot but speak to the utmost!

sentences.zh: 疏入不報。

translations.literal: The memorial entered and received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial entered and received no response.

sentences.zh: 又淄青節度使李師道進絹，為魏徵子孫贖宅。

translations.literal: Also the military governor of Ziqing, Li Shidao, presented silk to ransom the residence of Wei Zheng's descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Also the military governor of Ziqing, Li Shidao, presented silk to ransom the residence of Wei Zheng's descendants.

sentences.zh: 居易諫曰：「徵是陛下先朝宰相，太宗嘗賜殿材成其正室，尤與諸家第宅不同。

translations.literal: Juyi remonstrated, saying: "Wei was a chief minister of Your Majesty's former reign; Taizong once bestowed hall timber to complete his main hall, and it was especially unlike the mansions of other families.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi remonstrated, saying, "Wei was a chief minister of Your Majesty's former reign; Taizong once bestowed hall timber to complete his main hall, and it was especially unlike the mansions of other families.

sentences.zh: 子孫典貼，其錢不多，自可官中為之收贖，而令師道掠美，事實非宜。」

translations.literal: The descendants pawned it; the sum was not large and the court itself could redeem it, yet to let Shidao seize the credit is in truth not fitting."
translations.idiomatic: The descendants pawned it; the sum was not large and the court itself could redeem it, yet to let Shidao seize the credit is in truth not fitting."

sentences.zh: 憲宗深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply agreed.

sentences.zh: 上又欲加河東王鍔平章事，居易諫曰：「宰相是陛下輔臣，非賢良不可當此位。

translations.literal: The emperor also wished to add Wang E of Hedong as chief councilor; Juyi remonstrated, saying: "The chief councilor is Your Majesty's assisting minister; only the worthy and good should hold this post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also wished to add Wang E of Hedong as chief councilor; Juyi remonstrated, saying, "The chief councilor is Your Majesty's assisting minister; only the worthy and good should hold this post.

sentences.zh: 鍔誅剝民財，以市恩澤，不可使四方之人謂陛下得王鍔進奉，而與之宰相，深無益於聖朝。」

translations.literal: E strips the people's wealth to purchase favor; it must not be allowed that people in the four directions say Your Majesty received Wang E's tribute offerings and gave him the chancellorship—this is deeply without benefit to the holy court."
translations.idiomatic: E strips the people's wealth to purchase favor; it must not be allowed that people in the four directions say Your Majesty received Wang E's tribute offerings and gave him the chancellorship—this is deeply without benefit to the holy court."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: And so it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: And so it was stopped.

sentences.zh: 王承宗拒命，上令神策中尉吐突承璀為招討使，諫官上章者十七八。

translations.literal: Wang Chengzong defied orders; the emperor appointed the director of the Divine Stratagem Army, Tuoba Chenghuan, as campaign commissioner, and remonstrance officials submitted memorials numbering seventeen or eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengzong defied orders; the emperor appointed the director of the Divine Stratagem Army, Tuoba Chenghuan, as campaign commissioner, and remonstrance officials submitted memorials numbering seventeen or eighteen.

sentences.zh: 居易面論，辭情切至。

translations.literal: Juyi argued face to face, his words urgent and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi argued face to face, his words urgent and sincere.

sentences.zh: 既而又請罷河北用兵，凡數千百言，皆人之難言者，上多聽納。

translations.literal: Afterward he again requested withdrawal of troops in Hebei; in all several thousand words, all things difficult for others to speak, and the emperor mostly listened and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he again requested withdrawal of troops in Hebei; in all several thousand words, all things difficult for others to speak, and the emperor mostly listened and accepted.

sentences.zh: 唯諫承璀事切，上頗不悅，謂李絳曰：「白居易小子，是朕拔擢致名位，而無禮於朕，朕實難奈。」

translations.literal: Only on the matter of remonstrating against Chenghuan was the emperor somewhat displeased, and he said to Li Jiang: "Bai Juyi the youngster is one I raised and elevated to fame and position, yet he is without propriety toward me—I truly find it hard to bear."
translations.idiomatic: Only on the matter of remonstrating against Chenghuan was the emperor somewhat displeased, and he said to Li Jiang, "Bai Juyi the youngster is one I raised and elevated to fame and position, yet he is without propriety toward me—I truly find it hard to bear."

sentences.zh: 絳對曰：「居易所以不避死亡之誅，事無巨細必言者，蓋酬陛下特力拔擢耳，非輕言也。

translations.literal: Jiang replied: "The reason Juyi does not avoid the punishment of death and speaks on matters great and small is that he is repaying Your Majesty's special elevation of him by force—it is not light speech.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang replied, "The reason Juyi does not avoid the punishment of death and speaks on matters great and small is that he is repaying Your Majesty's special elevation of him by force—it is not light speech.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲開諫諍之路，不宜阻居易言。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty wishes to open the path of blunt remonstrance; you should not obstruct Juyi's words."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty wishes to open the path of blunt remonstrance; you should not obstruct Juyi's words."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your words are correct."

sentences.zh: 由是多見聽納。

translations.literal: From this Juyi was often heard and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: From this Juyi was often heard and accepted.

sentences.zh: 五年，當改官，上謂崔群曰：「居易官卑俸薄，拘於資地，不能超等，其官可聽自便奏來。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when his term for office change came due, the emperor said to Cui Qun: "Juyi's office is low and his salary thin; constrained by seniority he cannot be promoted beyond grade—his office may be reported as he himself wishes."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when his term for office change came due, the emperor said to Cui Qun, "Juyi's office is low and his salary thin; constrained by seniority he cannot be promoted beyond grade—his office may be reported as he himself wishes."

sentences.zh: 居易奏曰：「臣聞姜公輔為內職，求為京府判司，為奉親也。

translations.literal: Juyi memorialized, saying: "I have heard that Jiang Gongfu, holding an inner post, requested appointment as administrative aide in the capital prefecture for the sake of supporting his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi memorialized, saying, "I have heard that Jiang Gongfu, holding an inner post, requested appointment as administrative aide in the capital prefecture for the sake of supporting his parents.

sentences.zh: 臣有老母，家貧養薄，乞如公輔例。」

translations.literal: I have an aged mother; our household is poor and support is thin—I beg to follow Gongfu's example."
translations.idiomatic: I have an aged mother; our household is poor and support is thin—I beg to follow Gongfu's example."

sentences.zh: 於是，除京兆府戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed army staff officer in the metropolitan prefecture's revenue section.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was appointed army staff officer in the metropolitan prefecture's revenue section.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，丁母陳夫人之喪，退居下邽。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year he entered mourning for his mother Lady Chen and retired to Xiaji.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixth year he entered mourning for his mother Lady Chen and retired to Xiaji.

sentences.zh: 九年冬，入朝，授太子左贊善大夫。

translations.literal: In the winter of the ninth year he entered court and was appointed Left Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the ninth year he entered court and was appointed Left Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十年七月，盜殺宰相武元衡，居易首上疏論其冤，急請捕賊以雪國恥。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the tenth year bandits killed the chief minister Wu Yuanheng; Juyi was first to submit a memorial on his injustice and urgently requested capture of the assassins to wash away the national shame.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the tenth year bandits killed the chief minister Wu Yuanheng; Juyi was first to submit a memorial on his injustice and urgently requested capture of the assassins to wash away the national shame.

sentences.zh: 宰相以宮官非諫職，不當先諫官言事。

translations.literal: The chief ministers held that a palace official was not a remonstrance post and ought not speak before remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers held that a palace official was not a remonstrance post and ought not speak before remonstrance officials.

sentences.zh: 會有素惡居易者，掎摭居易，言浮華無行，其母因看花墮井而死，而居易作《賞花》及《新井》詩，甚傷名教，不宜置彼周行。

translations.literal: There happened to be one who had long disliked Juyi; he seized on Juyi and said he was frivolous and without conduct—that his mother had died from falling into a well while viewing flowers, yet Juyi composed "Viewing Flowers" and "The New Well," gravely injuring moral teaching, and was unfit to stand among the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: There happened to be one who had long disliked Juyi; he seized on Juyi and said he was frivolous and without conduct—that his mother had died from falling into a well while viewing flowers, yet Juyi composed "Viewing Flowers" and "The New Well," gravely injuring moral teaching, and was unfit to stand among the court ranks.

sentences.zh: 執政方惡其言事，奏貶為江表刺史。

translations.literal: Those in power at the time detested his remonstrances and memorialized that he be demoted to prefect south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power at the time detested his remonstrances and memorialized that he be demoted to prefect south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 詔出，中書舍人王涯上疏論之，言居易所犯狀跡，不宜治郡，追詔授江州司馬。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Drafting Academician Wang Ya submitted a memorial on the matter, saying that given the nature of Juyi's offenses he was unfit to govern a prefecture; the edict was recalled and he was appointed marshal of Jiangzhou instead.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, Drafting Academician Wang Ya submitted a memorial on the matter, saying that given the nature of Juyi's offenses he was unfit to govern a prefecture; the edict was recalled and he was appointed marshal of Jiangzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 居易儒學之外，尤通釋典，常以忘懷處順為事，都不以遷謫介意。

translations.literal: Beyond Confucian learning Juyi was especially versed in Buddhist scriptures and often took forgetting cares and accepting circumstances as his practice, not minding exile and demotion at all.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Confucian learning Juyi was especially versed in Buddhist scriptures and often took forgetting cares and accepting circumstances as his practice, not minding exile and demotion at all.

sentences.zh: 在湓城，立隱舍於廬山遺愛寺，嘗與人書言之曰：「予去年秋始遊廬山，到東西二林間香爐峰下，見雲木泉石，勝絕第一。

translations.literal: At Xuncheng he established a hermitage at the Jian'ai Temple on Mount Lu and once wrote to someone, saying: "Last autumn I first traveled Mount Lu; between the eastern and western forests at the foot of Incense Burner Peak I saw clouds, trees, springs, and rocks surpassing all else in excellence.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuncheng he established a hermitage at the Jian'ai Temple on Mount Lu and once wrote to someone, saying, "Last autumn I first traveled Mount Lu; between the eastern and western forests at the foot of Incense Burner Peak I saw clouds, trees, springs, and rocks surpassing all else in excellence.

sentences.zh: 愛不能舍，因立草堂。

translations.literal: I loved it and could not leave; therefore I built a thatched hall.
translations.idiomatic: I loved it and could not leave; therefore I built a thatched hall.

sentences.zh: 前有喬松十數株，修竹千餘竿，青羅為墻援，白石為橋道，流水周於舍下，飛泉落於檐間，紅榴白蓮，羅生池砌。」

translations.literal: Before it were more than ten tall pines, more than a thousand bamboo poles, green silk for a wall enclosure, white stone for a bridge path, flowing water circling below the lodge, flying springs falling between the eaves, red pomegranate and white lotus growing thick around the pool ledge."
translations.idiomatic: Before it were more than ten tall pines, more than a thousand bamboo poles, green silk for a wall enclosure, white stone for a bridge path, flowing water circling below the lodge, flying springs falling between the eaves, red pomegranate and white lotus growing thick around the pool ledge."

sentences.zh: 居易與湊、滿、朗、晦四禪師，追永、遠、宗、雷之跡，為人外之交。

translations.literal: Juyi with the four Chan masters Cou, Man, Lang, and Hui pursued the traces of Yong, Yuan, Zong, and Lei and formed friendships outside the world of men.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi with the four Chan masters Cou, Man, Lang, and Hui pursued the traces of Yong, Yuan, Zong, and Lei and formed friendships outside the world of men.

sentences.zh: 每相摧遊詠，躋危登險，極林泉之幽邃。

translations.literal: They often urged one another to travel and chant, climbing peril and ascending heights, reaching the utmost seclusion of forests and springs.
translations.idiomatic: They often urged one another to travel and chant, climbing peril and ascending heights, reaching the utmost seclusion of forests and springs.

sentences.zh: 至於翛然順適之際，幾欲忘其形骸。

translations.literal: When they arrived at a state of free and easy accord, they nearly forgot their own bodies.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived at a state of free and easy accord, they nearly forgot their own bodies.

sentences.zh: 或經時不歸，或逾月而返，郡守以朝貴遇之，不之責。

translations.literal: Sometimes they did not return for a whole season, or returned only after more than a month; the prefect treated them as court nobility and did not hold them accountable.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes they did not return for a whole season, or returned only after more than a month; the prefect treated them as court nobility and did not hold them accountable.

sentences.zh: 時元稹在通州，篇詠贈答往來，不以數千里為遠。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Zhen was in Tongzhou; poems exchanged in gift and response traveled back and forth, not considering several thousand li distant.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Zhen was in Tongzhou; poems exchanged in gift and response traveled back and forth, not considering several thousand li distant.

sentences.zh: 嘗與稹書，因論作文之大旨曰：夫文，尚矣，三才各有文。

translations.literal: He once wrote to Zhen, discussing the great principles of composition, saying: Writing is exalted indeed; the three powers each have their writing.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote to Zhen discussing the great principles of composition, saying: Writing is exalted indeed; heaven, earth, and humanity each have their own literature.

sentences.zh: 天之文三光首之；

translations.literal: Heaven's writing takes the three luminaries as foremost;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's literature is headed by the sun, moon, and stars;

sentences.zh: 地之文五材首之；

translations.literal: earth's writing takes the five materials as foremost;
translations.idiomatic: earth's literature is headed by the five elements;

sentences.zh: 人之文《六經》道之。

translations.literal: humanity's writing is guided by the Six Classics.
translations.idiomatic: human literature is guided by the Six Classics.

sentences.zh: 就《六經》言，《詩》又首之。

translations.literal: Speaking of the Six Classics, the Odes again come first.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Six Classics, the Odes come first.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 聖人感人心而天下和平。

translations.literal: The sage moves people's hearts and the realm is at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The sage moves people's hearts, and the realm is at peace.

sentences.zh: 感人心者，莫先乎情，莫始乎言，莫切乎聲，莫深乎義。

translations.literal: What moves people's hearts: nothing comes before feeling, nothing begins before words, nothing cuts closer than sound, nothing runs deeper than meaning.
translations.idiomatic: What moves the heart begins with feeling, starts with words, is sharpened by sound, and is grounded in meaning.

sentences.zh: 詩者，根情，苗言，華聲，實義。

translations.literal: Poetry takes feeling as root, words as shoot, sound as blossom, and meaning as fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Poetry has feeling for its root, words for its shoot, sound for its blossom, and meaning for its fruit.

sentences.zh: 上自賢聖，下至愚騃，微及豚魚，幽及鬼神。

translations.literal: From sages and worthies above to fools and dullards below, it reaches subtly to pigs and fish and darkly to ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: It ranges from sages and worthies down to fools and dullards, reaching subtly even to pigs and fish and darkly even to ghosts and spirits.

sentences.zh: 群分而氣同，形異而情一。

translations.literal: Classes are many but the breath is one; forms differ but feelings are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Though classes are many, the vital breath is one; though forms differ, feelings are the same.

sentences.zh: 未有聲入而不應、情交而不感者。

translations.literal: There has never been sound entering the ear without response, or feelings exchanged without mutual stirring.
translations.idiomatic: Never does sound enter the ear without response, nor feelings meet without mutual stirring.

sentences.zh: 聖人知其然，因其言，經之以六義；

translations.literal: The sage knew this to be so; taking their words, he threaded them with the six principles;
translations.idiomatic: Knowing this, the sage took people's words and threaded them with the six principles;

sentences.zh: 緣其聲，緯之以五音。

translations.literal: following their sounds, he wove them with the five tones.
translations.idiomatic: and following their sounds, wove them with the five tones.

sentences.zh: 音有韻，義有類。

translations.literal: Sounds have rhyme; meanings have categories.
