translations.idiomatic: Sound has rhyme; meaning has category.

sentences.zh: 韻協則言順，言順則聲易入；

translations.literal: When rhyme harmonizes, words flow; when words flow, sound enters easily;
translations.idiomatic: When rhyme harmonizes, words flow smoothly; when words flow, sound enters easily;

sentences.zh: 類舉則情見，情見則感易交。

translations.literal: when categories are set forth, feeling appears; when feeling appears, mutual stirring comes easily.
translations.idiomatic: when categories are set forth, feeling shows; when feeling shows, mutual stirring comes easily.

sentences.zh: 於是乎孕大含深，貫微洞密，上下通而二氣泰，憂樂合而百志熙。

translations.literal: Thus it bears the great and holds the deep, penetrates the subtle and threads the dense; above and below communicate and the two breaths are at peace, sorrow and joy unite and the hundred aims flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Thus it bears the great and holds the deep, penetrates the subtle and threads the dense; above and below communicate and the two breaths are at peace, sorrow and joy unite and the hundred aims flourish.

sentences.zh: 二帝三王所以直道而行、垂拱而理者，揭此以為大柄，決此以為大竇也。

translations.literal: The reason the Two Emperors and Three Kings could walk the straight path and govern with folded arms was that they raised this as the great handle and opened this as the great gateway.
translations.idiomatic: The Two Emperors and Three Kings could walk the straight path and govern with folded arms because they raised this as the great handle and opened this as the great gateway.

sentences.zh: 故聞「元首明，股肱良」之歌，則知虞道昌矣。

translations.literal: Thus upon hearing the song "The head is bright, the arms are good," one knows the way of Yu flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Thus hearing the song "The head is bright, the arms are good," one knows the way of Yu flourished.

sentences.zh: 聞五子洛汭之歌，則知夏政荒矣。

translations.literal: Upon hearing the song of the Five Sons at Luorui, one knows the government of Xia was in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the song of the Five Sons at Luorui, one knows the government of Xia was in disorder.

sentences.zh: 言者無罪，聞者作誡，言者聞者莫不兩盡其心焉。

translations.literal: The speaker is without guilt; the hearer takes warning—speaker and hearer alike fully give their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The speaker bears no guilt; the hearer takes warning—speaker and hearer alike give their full hearts.

sentences.zh: 洎周衰秦興，采詩官廢，上不以詩補察時政，下不以歌泄導人情。

translations.literal: By the time Zhou declined and Qin rose, the poetry-gathering office was abolished; above, poetry was not used to supplement and examine current government; below, songs were not used to vent and guide human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou declined and Qin rose, the poetry-gathering office was abolished; above, poetry no longer supplemented and examined government; below, songs no longer vented and guided human feeling.

sentences.zh: 用至於諂成之風動，救失之道缺。

translations.literal: Use came to the point where the wind of flattery and complacency stirred, and the way of remedying loss was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Flattery and complacency took hold, and the way of remedying loss was lost.

sentences.zh: 於時六義始剚矣。

translations.literal: At that time the six principles were first cut away.
translations.idiomatic: Then the six principles were first cut away.

sentences.zh: 《國風》變為《騷辭》，五言始於蘇、李。

translations.literal: The Airs of the States turned into Sao verse; five-character poetry began with Su and Li.
translations.idiomatic: The Airs of the States became Sao verse; five-character poetry began with Su Wu and Li Ling.

sentences.zh: 《詩》、《騷》皆不遇者，各系其志，發而為文。

translations.literal: Those of the Odes and Sao were all men who did not meet with favor; each attached to his own aim and, giving vent, produced writing.
translations.idiomatic: The authors of the Odes and Sao were all men who met with no favor; each clung to his own aim and, giving vent, produced writing.

sentences.zh: 故河梁之句，止於傷別；

translations.literal: Thus the lines at River Bridge stop at grieving parting;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the lines at River Bridge stop at grieving parting;

sentences.zh: 澤畔之吟，歸於怨思。

translations.literal: the chant beside the marsh returns to resentful brooding.
translations.idiomatic: the chant beside the marsh returns to resentful brooding.

sentences.zh: 仿徨抑郁，不暇及他耳。

translations.literal: Wandering, depressed, they had no leisure for anything else.
translations.idiomatic: Wandering and depressed, they had no leisure for anything else.

sentences.zh: 然去《詩》未遠，梗概尚存。

translations.literal: Yet they were not far from the Odes; the rough outline still remained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they were not far from the Odes; the rough outline still remained.

sentences.zh: 故興離別則引雙鳧一雁為喻，諷君子小人則引香草惡鳥為比。

translations.literal: Thus in treating parting they cited paired ducks and a single goose as metaphor; in satirizing gentleman and petty man they cited fragrant herbs and evil birds as comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in treating parting they cited paired ducks and a single goose as metaphor; in satirizing gentleman and petty man they cited fragrant herbs and evil birds as comparison.

sentences.zh: 雖義類不具，猶得風人之什二三焉。

translations.literal: Though the categories of meaning were not complete, they still preserved two or three out of ten of the Airs.
translations.idiomatic: Though the categories of meaning were not complete, they still preserved two or three out of ten of the Airs.

sentences.zh: 於時六義始缺矣。

translations.literal: At that time the six principles were first lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Then the six principles were first lacking.

sentences.zh: 晉、宋已還，得者蓋寡。

translations.literal: From Jin and Song onward, those who attained it were few indeed.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin and Song onward, those who attained it were few indeed.

sentences.zh: 以康樂之奧博，多溺於山水；

translations.literal: In Xie Lingyun's profundity and breadth, many drowned in landscape;
translations.idiomatic: In Xie Lingyun's profundity and breadth, many drowned in landscape;

sentences.zh: 以淵明之高古，偏放於田園。

translations.literal: in Tao Yuanming's lofty antiquity, many were set loose in fields and gardens.
translations.idiomatic: in Tao Yuanming's lofty antiquity, many were set loose in fields and gardens.

sentences.zh: 江、鮑之流，又狹於此。

translations.literal: The stream of Jiang and Bao was narrower still.
translations.idiomatic: The stream of Jiang Yan and Bao Zhao was narrower still.

sentences.zh: 如梁鴻《五噫》之例者，百無一二。

translations.literal: Cases like Liang Hong's "Five Sighs" were not one or two in a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Cases like Liang Hong's "Five Sighs" were not one or two in a hundred.

sentences.zh: 於時六義浸微矣！

translations.literal: At that time the six principles gradually faded!
translations.idiomatic: By then the six principles were gradually fading!

sentences.zh: 陵夷至於梁、陳間，率不過嘲風雪、弄花草而已。

translations.literal: Decline reached Liang and Chen, when as a rule it was no more than mocking wind and snow and toying with flowers and grasses.
translations.idiomatic: Decline reached Liang and Chen, when as a rule poetry was no more than mocking wind and snow and toying with flowers and grasses.

sentences.zh: 噫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 風雪花草之物，三百篇中豈舍之乎？

translations.literal: Are wind, flowers, snow, and grass absent from the three hundred pieces?
translations.idiomatic: Are wind, flowers, snow, and grass absent from the three hundred pieces?

sentences.zh: 顧所用何如耳。

translations.literal: It depends on how they are used.
translations.idiomatic: It depends on how they are used.

sentences.zh: 設如「北風其涼」，假風以刺威虐；

translations.literal: Suppose "The north wind is cold"—borrowing wind to satirize cruel oppression;
translations.idiomatic: Take "The north wind is cold"—wind is borrowed to satirize cruel oppression;

sentences.zh: 「雨雪霏霏」，因雪以湣征役；

translations.literal: "The snow falls thickly"—through snow to pity conscript labor;
translations.idiomatic: "The snow falls thickly"—through snow to pity conscript labor;

sentences.zh: 「棠棣之華」，感華以諷兄弟；

translations.literal: "The cherry-apple in flower"—moved by blossom to satirize brothers;
translations.idiomatic: "The cherry-apple in flower"—moved by blossom to satirize brothers;

sentences.zh: 「采采芣苡」，美草以樂有子也。

translations.literal: "Gathering plantain"—praising the herb to rejoice in having sons.
translations.idiomatic: "Gathering plantain"—praising the herb to rejoice in having sons.

sentences.zh: 皆興發於此而義歸於彼。

translations.literal: All rise from this and meaning returns to that.
translations.idiomatic: All rise from this and meaning returns to that.

sentences.zh: 反是者，可乎哉！

translations.literal: To do the opposite—can that be allowed!
translations.idiomatic: To do the opposite—can that be allowed!

sentences.zh: 然則「餘霞散成綺，澄江凈如練」，「歸花先委露，別葉乍辭風」之什，麗則麗矣，吾不知其所諷焉。

translations.literal: Then the pieces "Leftover glow scatters into brocade; the clear river is smooth as silk" and "Returning flowers first shed dew; parting leaves suddenly leave the wind"—lovely they are indeed, but I do not know what they satirize.
translations.idiomatic: Then pieces like "Leftover glow scatters into brocade; the clear river is smooth as silk" and "Returning flowers first shed dew; parting leaves suddenly leave the wind" are lovely indeed, but I do not know what they satirize.

sentences.zh: 故僕所謂嘲風雪、弄花草而已。

translations.literal: Thus what I call mocking wind and snow and toying with flowers and grasses.
translations.idiomatic: This is what I mean by mocking wind and snow and toying with flowers and grasses.

sentences.zh: 於時六義盡去矣。

translations.literal: At that time the six principles were entirely gone.
translations.idiomatic: By then the six principles were entirely gone.

sentences.zh: 唐興二百年，其間詩人不可勝數。

translations.literal: Tang has risen two hundred years; poets in that time are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Tang has risen for two hundred years; poets in that time are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 所可舉者，陳子昂有《感遇詩》二十首，鮑防《感興詩》十五篇。

translations.literal: Those who may be cited: Chen Zi'ang had twenty pieces of "Poems on Encountering Feeling"; Bao Fang had fifteen pieces of "Poems Stirred by Feeling."
translations.idiomatic: Those who may be cited: Chen Zi'ang had twenty "Poems on Encountering Feeling"; Bao Fang had fifteen "Poems Stirred by Feeling."

sentences.zh: 又詩之豪者，世稱李、杜。

translations.literal: Again, the mighty in poetry—the age calls them Li and Du.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the mighty in poetry—the age calls them Li and Du.

sentences.zh: 李之作，才矣！

translations.literal: Li's works—talented indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Li Bai's works—talented indeed!

sentences.zh: 奇矣！

translations.literal: Strange indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Strange indeed!

sentences.zh: 人不迨矣！

translations.literal: Men cannot reach him!
translations.idiomatic: Men cannot reach him!

sentences.zh: 索其風雅比興，十無一焉。

translations.literal: Search for elegance, Airs, comparison, and stirring— not one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Search for elegance, Airs, comparison, and stirring—not one in ten.

sentences.zh: 杜詩最多，可傳者千餘首。

translations.literal: Du's poems are most numerous; those that can be transmitted number more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fu's poems are most numerous; those that can be transmitted number more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 至於貫穿古今，覙縷格律，盡工盡善，又過於李焉。

translations.literal: As for penetrating past and present, threading through rules and forms, achieving utmost craft and utmost goodness—he surpasses Li.
translations.idiomatic: In penetrating past and present, threading through rules and forms, and achieving utmost craft and goodness, he surpasses Li Bai.

sentences.zh: 然撮其《新安》、《石壕》、《潼關吏》、《蘆子關》、《花門》之章，「硃門酒肉臭，路有凍死骨」之句，亦不過十三四。

translations.literal: Yet gather his chapters "Xin'an," "Shihao," "Tong Pass Officer," "Luzi Pass," and "Flower Gate," and the line "Vermilion gates reek of wine and meat; on the road lie bones of the frozen dead"—these too are no more than thirteen or fourteen out of a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Yet gather his chapters "Xin'an," "Shihao," "Tong Pass Officer," "Luzi Pass," and "Flower Gate," and the line "Vermilion gates reek of wine and meat; on the road lie bones of the frozen dead"—these too are no more than thirteen or fourteen out of a hundred.

sentences.zh: 杜尚如此，況不迨杜者乎？

translations.literal: If Du is still like this, how much more those who do not reach Du?
translations.idiomatic: If Du Fu is still like this, how much more those who do not reach Du Fu?

sentences.zh: 僕常痛詩道崩壞，忽忽憤發，或廢食輟寢，不量才力，欲扶起之。

translations.literal: I have often grieved that the way of poetry was collapsing; suddenly, in angry agitation, I would abandon eating or stop sleeping, not measuring talent and strength, wishing to raise it up again.
translations.idiomatic: I have often grieved that the way of poetry was collapsing; suddenly, in angry agitation, I would abandon eating or stop sleeping, not measuring my talent and strength, wishing to raise it up again.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 事有大謬者，又不可一二而言，然亦不能不粗陳於左右。

translations.literal: There are great errors in affairs that cannot be told one by one, yet I also cannot fail to set them out roughly before you.
translations.idiomatic: There are great errors in affairs that cannot be told one by one, yet I also cannot fail to set them out roughly before you.

sentences.zh: 僕始生六七月時，乳母抱弄於書屏下，有指「之」字、「無」字示僕者，僕口未能言，心已默識。

translations.literal: When I was six or seven months old, my wet nurse held me playing beneath a book screen; someone pointed out the characters "zhi" and "wu" to me; though my mouth could not yet speak, my heart had already silently recognized them.
translations.idiomatic: When I was six or seven months old, my wet nurse held me playing beneath a book screen; someone pointed out the characters "zhi" and "wu" to me; though my mouth could not yet speak, my heart had already silently recognized them.

sentences.zh: 後有問此二字者，雖百十其試，而指之不差。

translations.literal: Later, when asked about these two characters, though tested a hundred or ten times, I pointed without error.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when asked about these two characters, though tested a hundred or ten times, I pointed without error.

sentences.zh: 則知僕宿習之緣，已在文字中矣。

translations.literal: Then I knew that the bond of my former learning was already within writing.
translations.idiomatic: Then I knew that the bond of my former learning was already within writing.

sentences.zh: 及五六歲，便學為詩。

translations.literal: By five or six I was already learning to write poetry.
translations.idiomatic: By five or six I was already learning to write poetry.

sentences.zh: 九歲諳識聲韻。

translations.literal: At nine I was thoroughly versed in rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: At nine I was thoroughly versed in rhyme.

sentences.zh: 十五六，始知有進士，苦節讀書。

translations.literal: At fifteen or sixteen I first learned of the jinshi degree and studied books with bitter discipline.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen or sixteen I first learned of the jinshi degree and studied books with bitter discipline.

sentences.zh: 二十已來，書課賦，夜課書，間又課詩，不遑寢息矣。

translations.literal: From twenty onward, by day I studied fu, by night books; in between I also studied poetry, with no leisure for sleep and rest.
translations.idiomatic: From twenty onward, by day I studied fu, by night books; in between I also studied poetry, with no leisure for sleep and rest.

sentences.zh: 以至於口舌成瘡，手肘成胝。

translations.literal: It reached the point where my mouth and tongue formed sores and my hands and elbows formed calluses.
translations.idiomatic: It reached the point where my mouth and tongue formed sores and my hands and elbows formed calluses.

sentences.zh: 既壯而膚革不豐盈，未老而齒發早衰白；

translations.literal: Though grown, my skin and flesh were not full; though not yet old, my teeth and hair prematurely whitened early;
translations.idiomatic: Though grown, my skin and flesh were not full; though not yet old, my teeth and hair whitened early;

sentences.zh: 瞀然如飛蠅垂珠在眸子中者，動以萬數，蓋以苦學力文之所致！

translations.literal: dazed as though flies hanging beads in the pupils, numbering in the tens of thousands—this was caused by bitter study and forcing writing!
translations.idiomatic: dazed as though flies hanging beads in the pupils, numbering in the tens of thousands—this was caused by bitter study and forcing writing!

sentences.zh: 又自悲家貧多故，年二十七，方從鄉賦。

translations.literal: Again I grieved for myself that my family was poor and full of troubles; only at twenty-seven did I set out for the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Again I grieved that my family was poor and full of troubles; only at twenty-seven did I set out for the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 既第之後，雖專於科試，亦不廢詩。

translations.literal: After passing, though I specialized in the civil examinations, I did not abandon poetry.
translations.idiomatic: After passing, though I specialized in the civil examinations, I did not abandon poetry.

sentences.zh: 及授校書郎時，已盈三四百首。

translations.literal: By the time I was appointed collator, I already had three or four hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: By the time I was appointed collator, I already had three or four hundred pieces.

sentences.zh: 或出示交友如足下輩，見皆謂之工，其實未窺作者之域耳。

translations.literal: Sometimes I showed them to friends like you; all who saw them called them skilled, but in truth I had not yet glimpsed the domain of the true author.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes I showed them to friends like you; all who saw them called them skilled, but in truth I had not yet glimpsed the domain of the true author.

sentences.zh: 自登朝來，年齒漸長，閱事漸多。

translations.literal: Since entering court, my years gradually lengthened and affairs I witnessed gradually grew.
translations.idiomatic: Since entering court, my years gradually lengthened and affairs I witnessed gradually grew.

sentences.zh: 每與人言，多詢時務；

translations.literal: Whenever I spoke with others, I often inquired about current affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I spoke with others, I often inquired about current affairs;

sentences.zh: 每讀書史，多求理道。

translations.literal: whenever I read books and histories, I often sought the way and its principles.
translations.idiomatic: whenever I read books and histories, I often sought the way and its principles.

sentences.zh: 始知文章合為時而著，歌詩合為事而作。

translations.literal: I then knew that writing should be composed for the age, and songs and poems should be made for affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I then knew that writing should be composed for the age, and songs and poems should be made for affairs.

sentences.zh: 是時皇帝初即位，宰府有正人，屢降璽書，訪人急病。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had just taken the throne; the chief ministers had upright men; repeatedly imperial edicts were sent down, inquiring into people's urgent ills.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor had just taken the throne; the chief ministers had upright men; repeatedly imperial edicts were sent down, inquiring into people's urgent ills.

sentences.zh: 僕當此日，擢在翰林，身是諫官，月請諫紙。

translations.literal: On that day I was promoted to the Hanlin; my person was remonstrance official; monthly I requested remonstrance paper.
translations.idiomatic: On that day I was promoted to the Hanlin; my person was remonstrance official; monthly I requested remonstrance paper.

sentences.zh: 啟奏之間，有可以救濟人病，裨補時闕，而難於指言者，輒詠歌之，欲稍稍進聞於上。

translations.literal: Between memorials and reports, when there was something that could relieve people's ills, supplement and repair current lacks, yet was hard to speak of directly, I would chant and sing it, wishing gradually to advance it to the emperor's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Between memorials and reports, when there was something that could relieve people's ills, supplement and repair current lacks, yet was hard to speak of directly, I would chant and sing it, wishing gradually to advance it to the emperor's hearing.

sentences.zh: 上以廣宸聽，副憂勤；

translations.literal: Above, to broaden the imperial ear and assist anxious diligence;
translations.idiomatic: Above, to broaden the imperial ear and assist anxious diligence;

sentences.zh: 次以酬恩獎，塞言責；

translations.literal: next, to repay favor and reward and fulfill the duty of speech;
translations.idiomatic: next, to repay favor and reward and fulfill the duty of speech;

sentences.zh: 下以復吾平生之志。

translations.literal: below, to fulfill my lifelong aim.
translations.idiomatic: below, to fulfill my lifelong aim.

sentences.zh: 豈圖志未就而悔已生，言未聞而謗已成矣！

translations.literal: Who would have thought that before the aim was achieved regret was already born, before the words were heard slander was already formed!
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought that before the aim was achieved regret was already born, before the words were heard slander was already formed!

sentences.zh: 又請為左右終言之。

translations.literal: Again I ask to speak to the end before you.
translations.idiomatic: Again I ask to speak to the end before you.

sentences.zh: 凡聞僕《賀雨詩》，眾口籍籍，以為非宜矣；

translations.literal: Whenever people heard my "Poem on Congratulating the Rain," mouths were all abuzz, thinking it improper;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever people heard my "Poem on Congratulating the Rain," mouths were all abuzz, thinking it improper;

sentences.zh: 聞僕《哭孔戡詩》，眾面脈脈，盡不悅矣；

translations.literal: when they heard my "Poem on Mourning Kong Kan," faces were all stern, entirely displeased;
translations.idiomatic: when they heard my "Poem on Mourning Kong Kan," faces were all stern, entirely displeased;

sentences.zh: 聞《秦中吟》，則權豪貴近者，相目而變色矣；

translations.literal: when they heard "Chants of Qin," then powerful families and the noble and near exchanged glances and changed color;
translations.idiomatic: when they heard "Chants of Qin," then powerful families and the noble and near exchanged glances and changed color;

sentences.zh: 聞《登樂遊園》寄足下詩，則執政柄者扼腕矣；

translations.literal: when they heard the poem "Ascending Leyou Garden" sent to you, then those who held the reins of government clenched their wrists;
translations.idiomatic: when they heard the poem "Ascending Leyou Garden" sent to you, then those who held the reins of government clenched their wrists;

sentences.zh: 聞《宿紫閣村》詩，則握軍要者切齒矣！

translations.literal: when they heard the poem "Lodging at Zige Village," then those who grasped military power gnashed their teeth!
translations.idiomatic: when they heard the poem "Lodging at Zige Village," then those who grasped military power gnashed their teeth!

sentences.zh: 大率如此，不可遍舉。

translations.literal: Mostly it was like this; it cannot all be cited.
translations.idiomatic: Mostly it was like this; it cannot all be cited.

sentences.zh: 不相與者，號為沽譽，號為詆訐，號為訕謗。

translations.literal: Those not on good terms with me called it seeking reputation, called it slander, called it ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Those not on good terms with me called it seeking reputation, called it slander, called it ridicule.

sentences.zh: 茍相與者，則如牛僧孺之誡焉。

translations.literal: If on good terms, then like Niu Sengru's admonition.
translations.idiomatic: If on good terms, then like Niu Sengru's admonition.

sentences.zh: 乃至骨肉妻孥，皆以我為非也。

translations.literal: It reached the point that flesh and bone, wife and children—all regarded me as wrong.
translations.idiomatic: It reached the point that flesh and bone, wife and children—all regarded me as wrong.

sentences.zh: 其不我非者，舉世不過三兩人。

translations.literal: Those who did not regard me as wrong—in the whole realm were no more than two or three.
translations.idiomatic: Those who did not regard me as wrong—in the whole realm were no more than two or three.

sentences.zh: 有鄧魴者，見僕詩而喜，無何魴死。

translations.literal: There was Deng Fang, who saw my poems and rejoiced; before long Fang died.
translations.idiomatic: There was Deng Fang, who saw my poems and rejoiced; before long Fang died.

sentences.zh: 有唐衢者，見僕詩而泣，未幾而衢死。

translations.literal: There was Tang Qu, who saw my poems and wept; before long Qu died.
translations.idiomatic: There was Tang Qu, who saw my poems and wept; before long Qu died.

sentences.zh: 其餘即足下。

translations.literal: The rest is you.
translations.idiomatic: The rest is you.

sentences.zh: 足下又十年來困躓若此。

translations.literal: You too have been thwarted like this for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: You too have been thwarted like this for ten years.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 豈六義四始之風，天將破壞，不可支持耶？

translations.literal: Is the wind of the six principles and four beginnings of heaven about to be destroyed, beyond support?
translations.idiomatic: Is the wind of the six principles and four beginnings of heaven about to be destroyed, beyond support?

sentences.zh: 抑又不知天意不欲使下人病苦聞於上耶？

translations.literal: Or again, does one not know whether heaven's intent is unwilling to let the suffering of those below be heard above?
translations.idiomatic: Or again, does one not know whether heaven's intent is unwilling to let the suffering of those below be heard above?

sentences.zh: 不然，何有志於詩者，不利若此之甚也！

translations.literal: If not, why are those who aspire to poetry so greatly disadvantaged!
translations.idiomatic: If not, why are those who aspire to poetry so greatly disadvantaged!

sentences.zh: 然僕又自思關東一男子耳，除讀書屬文外，其他懵然無知，乃至書畫棋博，可以接群居之歡者，一無通曉，即其愚拙可知矣！

translations.literal: Yet I again reflect that I am but a man of east of the Pass; apart from reading books and composing writing, in other things I am blankly ignorant—even calligraphy, painting, chess, and gambling, which can join the pleasure of group living, I have not one that I understand; from this my foolish awkwardness can be known!
translations.idiomatic: Yet I again reflect that I am but a man of east of the Pass; apart from reading books and composing writing, in other things I am blankly ignorant—even calligraphy, painting, chess, and gambling, which can join the pleasure of group living, I have not one that I understand; from this my foolish awkwardness can be known!

sentences.zh: 初應進士時，中朝無緦麻之親，達官無半面之舊；

translations.literal: When I first answered the jinshi examination, in the central court I had no relative within the mourning-garment bond; among high officials I had no acquaintance of half a face;
translations.idiomatic: When I first answered the jinshi examination, in the central court I had no relative within the mourning-garment bond; among high officials I had no acquaintance of half a face;

sentences.zh: 策蹇步於利足之途，張空拳於戰文之場。

translations.literal: I urged lame steps on the path of swift feet and brandished empty fists on the battlefield of literary combat.
translations.idiomatic: I urged lame steps on the path of swift feet and brandished empty fists on the battlefield of literary combat.

sentences.zh: 十年之間，三登科第，名落眾耳，跡升清貫，出交賢俊，入侍冕旒。

translations.literal: Within ten years I thrice passed the examinations; my name fell on many ears, my track rose to the clear roster; going out I associated with worthy and eminent men, entering I attended the imperial crown.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten years I thrice passed the examinations; my name fell on many ears, my track rose to the clear roster; going out I associated with worthy and eminent men, entering I attended the imperial crown.

sentences.zh: 始得名於文章，終得罪於文章，亦其宜也。

translations.literal: At first I gained name through writing; in the end I offended through writing—it is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: At first I gained name through writing; in the end I offended through writing—it is fitting.

sentences.zh: 日者聞親友間說，禮、吏部舉選人，多以僕私試賦判為準的。

translations.literal: Recently I heard from among kin and friends that the Ministries of Rites and Personnel, in selecting candidates, often took my private examination fu and judgments as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I heard from among kin and friends that the Ministries of Rites and Personnel, in selecting candidates, often took my private examination fu and judgments as the standard.

sentences.zh: 其餘詩句，亦往往在人口中。

translations.literal: The rest of the poetic lines too are often on people's lips.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the poetic lines too are often on people's lips.

sentences.zh: 僕恧然自愧，不之信也。

translations.literal: I was ashamed and doubted it myself, not believing it.
translations.idiomatic: I was ashamed and doubted it myself, not believing it.

sentences.zh: 及再來長安，又聞有軍使高霞寓者，欲聘倡妓，妓大誇曰：「我誦得白學士《長恨歌》，豈同他哉？」

translations.literal: When I came again to Chang'an, I also heard that Military Commissioner Gao Xiayu wished to hire a singing girl; the girl greatly boasted, saying: "I can recite Academician Bai's 'Song of Everlasting Sorrow'—how can I be like the others?"
translations.idiomatic: When I came again to Chang'an, I also heard that Military Commissioner Gao Xiayu wished to hire a singing girl; the girl greatly boasted, saying: "I can recite Academician Bai's 'Song of Everlasting Sorrow'—how can I be like the others?"

sentences.zh: 由是增價。

translations.literal: and thereby raised her price.
translations.idiomatic: and thereby raised her price.

sentences.zh: 又足下書云：到通州日，見江館柱間有題僕詩者。

translations.literal: Again your letter says: On reaching Tongzhou, I saw on a pillar of the river lodge someone had inscribed my poem.
translations.idiomatic: Again your letter says: On reaching Tongzhou, I saw on a pillar of the river lodge someone had inscribed my poem.

sentences.zh: 何人哉？

translations.literal: Who was it?
translations.idiomatic: Who was it?

sentences.zh: 又昨過漢南日，適遇主人集眾娛樂，他賓諸妓見僕來，指而相顧曰：此是《秦中吟》、《長恨歌》主耳。

translations.literal: Again yesterday, passing Hannan, I happened to meet the host gathering the crowd for entertainment; other guests and singing girls, seeing me come, pointed and looked at one another, saying: This is the master of "Chants of Qin" and "Song of Everlasting Sorrow."
translations.idiomatic: Again yesterday, passing Hannan, I happened to meet the host gathering the crowd for entertainment; other guests and singing girls, seeing me come, pointed and looked at one another, saying: This is the master of "Chants of Qin" and "Song of Everlasting Sorrow."

sentences.zh: 自長安抵江西三四千里，凡鄉校、佛寺、逆旅、行舟之中，往往有題僕詩者；

translations.literal: From Chang'an to Jiangxi, three or four thousand li—everywhere in village schools, Buddhist temples, inns, and boats on the road, there are often inscriptions of my poems;
translations.idiomatic: From Chang'an to Jiangxi, three or four thousand li—everywhere in village schools, Buddhist temples, inns, and boats on the road, there are often inscriptions of my poems;

sentences.zh: 士庶、僧徒、孀婦、處女之口，每有詠僕詩者。

translations.literal: from the mouths of commoners and gentry, monks, widows, and maidens, there are often those who chant my poems.
translations.idiomatic: from the mouths of commoners and gentry, monks, widows, and maidens, there are often those who chant my poems.

sentences.zh: 此誠雕篆之戲，不足為多，然今時俗所重，正在此耳。

translations.literal: This is truly the sport of carving and inlay—not enough to count for much; yet what the present age values lies just in this.
translations.idiomatic: This is truly the sport of carving and inlay—not enough to count for much; yet what the present age values lies just in this.

sentences.zh: 雖前賢如淵、雲者，前輩如李、杜者，亦未能忘情於其間。

translations.literal: Though former worthies like Tao and Xie, and elders like Li and Du, also could not forget feeling in this.
translations.idiomatic: Though former worthies like Tao Yuanming and Xie Lingyun, and elders like Li Bai and Du Fu, also could not forget feeling in this.

sentences.zh: 古人云：「名者公器，不可多取。」

translations.literal: The ancients said: "Fame is a public vessel; one must not take too much of it."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "Fame is a public vessel; one must not take too much of it."

sentences.zh: 僕是何者，竊時之名已多。

translations.literal: What sort of man am I, that I have already stolen more than my share of fame of the age?
translations.idiomatic: What sort of man am I, that I have already stolen more than my share of fame of the age?

sentences.zh: 既竊時名，又欲竊時之富貴，使己為造物者，肯兼與之乎？

translations.literal: Having already stolen the age's name, I also wish to steal the age's wealth and honor—if I were the Creator, would He grant both together?
translations.idiomatic: Having already stolen the age's name, I also wish to steal the age's wealth and honor—if I were the Creator, would He grant both together?

sentences.zh: 今之屯窮，理固然也。

translations.literal: Today's hardship and obstruction—by principle it is surely so.
translations.idiomatic: Today's hardship and obstruction—by principle it is surely so.

sentences.zh: 況詩人多蹇，如陳子昂、杜甫，各授一拾遺，而屯剝至死。

translations.literal: Moreover poets mostly meet with obstruction; like Chen Zi'ang and Du Fu, each was granted a remonstrance post and yet met hardship and stripping unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover poets mostly meet with obstruction; like Chen Zi'ang and Du Fu, each was granted a remonstrance post and yet met hardship and stripping unto death.

sentences.zh: 孟浩然輩不及一命，窮悴終身。

translations.literal: Men like Meng Haoran did not reach even one appointment and ended their lives in poverty and emaciation.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Meng Haoran did not reach even one appointment and ended their lives in poverty and emaciation.

sentences.zh: 近日孟郊六十，終試協律；

translations.literal: Recently Meng Jiao at sixty finally passed the Harmonizing Office examination;
translations.idiomatic: Recently Meng Jiao at sixty finally passed the Harmonizing Office examination;

sentences.zh: 張籍五十，未離一太祝。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji at fifty had still not left the post of grand libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji at fifty had still not left the post of grand libationer.

sentences.zh: 彼何人哉！

translations.literal: What sort of men were they!
translations.idiomatic: What sort of men were they!

sentences.zh: 況僕之才又不迨彼。

translations.literal: Moreover my talent again does not reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover my talent again does not reach them.

sentences.zh: 今雖謫佐遠郡，而官品至第五，月俸四五萬，寒有衣，饑有食，給身之外，施及家人。

translations.literal: Though now demoted as assistant in a distant commandery, my official rank reaches the fifth grade, monthly salary four or five myriad; in cold I have clothes, in hunger food; beyond supplying my person, it extends to my family.
translations.idiomatic: Though now demoted as assistant in a distant commandery, my official rank reaches the fifth grade, monthly salary four or five myriad; in cold I have clothes, in hunger food; beyond supplying my person, it extends to my family.

sentences.zh: 亦可謂不負白氏子矣。

translations.literal: One may also say I have not failed the son of the Bai clan.
translations.idiomatic: One may also say I have not failed the son of the Bai clan.

sentences.zh: 微之，微之！

translations.literal: Zhen, Zhen!
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, Zhen!

sentences.zh: 勿念我哉！

translations.literal: Do not think of me!
translations.idiomatic: Do not think of me!

sentences.zh: 僕數月來，檢討囊帙中，得新舊詩，各以類分，分為卷目。

translations.literal: For several months I have examined satchels and folders, obtaining old and new poems, each sorted by category into fascicle titles.
translations.idiomatic: For several months I have examined satchels and folders, obtaining old and new poems, each sorted by category into fascicle titles.

sentences.zh: 自拾遺來，凡所遇所感，關於美刺興比者；

translations.literal: From remonstrance officer onward, all that I encountered and felt, relating to praise, satire, stirring, and comparison;
translations.idiomatic: From remonstrance officer onward, all that I encountered and felt, relating to praise, satire, stirring, and comparison;

sentences.zh: 又自武德至元和，因事立題，題為《新樂府》者，共一百五十首，謂之諷諭詩。

translations.literal: again from Wude to Yuanhe, setting titles according to affairs, titled "New Ballads"—altogether one hundred fifty pieces, called satirical-remonstrance poems.
translations.idiomatic: again from Wude to Yuanhe, setting titles according to affairs, titled "New Ballads"—altogether one hundred fifty pieces, called satirical-remonstrance poems.

sentences.zh: 又或退公，或臥病閑居，知足保和，吟玩性情者一百首，謂之閑適詩。

translations.literal: Again, whether leaving office or lying ill in leisure residence, content and preserving harmony, chanting and savoring one's nature—one hundred pieces, called leisurely-contentment poems.
translations.idiomatic: Again, whether leaving office or lying ill in leisure residence, content and preserving harmony, chanting and savoring one's nature—one hundred pieces, called leisurely-contentment poems.

sentences.zh: 又有事物牽於外，情理動於內，隨感遇而形於嘆詠者一百首，謂之感傷詩。

translations.literal: Again, when external things pull and inner principle stirs, following encounter and feeling and taking form in sighing chant—one hundred pieces, called poems of stirred feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Again, when external things pull and inner principle stirs, following encounter and feeling and taking form in sighing chant—one hundred pieces, called poems of stirred feeling.

sentences.zh: 又有五言、七言、長句、絕句，自百韻至兩韻者，四百餘首，謂之雜律詩。

translations.literal: Again, five-character, seven-character, long lines, and quatrains, from one hundred rhymes down to two rhymes—more than four hundred pieces, called miscellaneous regulated poems.
translations.idiomatic: Again, five-character, seven-character, long lines, and quatrains, from one hundred rhymes down to two rhymes—more than four hundred pieces, called miscellaneous regulated poems.

sentences.zh: 凡為十五卷，約八百首。

translations.literal: Altogether fifteen fascicles, about eight hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Altogether fifteen fascicles, about eight hundred pieces.

sentences.zh: 異時相見，當盡致於執事。

translations.literal: When we meet another time, I shall present them all to you.
translations.idiomatic: When we meet another time, I shall present them all to you.

sentences.zh: 微之，古人云：「窮則獨善其身，達則兼濟天下。」

translations.literal: Zhen, the ancients said: "In obstruction, cultivate the self alone; in attainment, benefit all under heaven together."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, the ancients said: "In obstruction, cultivate the self alone; in attainment, benefit all under heaven together."

sentences.zh: 僕雖不肖，常師此語。

translations.literal: Though I am unworthy, I constantly take this saying as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am unworthy, I constantly take this saying as teacher.

sentences.zh: 大丈夫所守者道，所待者時。

translations.literal: What a great man keeps is the Way; what he awaits is the time.
translations.idiomatic: What a great man keeps is the Way; what he awaits is the time.

sentences.zh: 時之來也，為雲龍，為風鵬，勃然突然，陳力以出；

translations.literal: When the time comes, he becomes cloud and dragon, wind and peng, suddenly bursting forth and offering his strength;
translations.idiomatic: When the time comes, he becomes cloud and dragon, wind and peng, suddenly bursting forth and offering his strength;

sentences.zh: 時之不來也，為霧豹，為冥鴻，寂兮寥兮，奉身而退。

translations.literal: when the time does not come, he becomes mist leopard, dark swan, silent and sparse, withdrawing his person.
translations.idiomatic: when the time does not come, he becomes mist leopard, dark swan, silent and sparse, withdrawing his person.

sentences.zh: 進退出處，何往而不自得哉！

translations.literal: Advancing, retreating, going out, staying—wherever he goes he is not without self-sufficiency!
translations.idiomatic: Advancing, retreating, going out, staying—wherever he goes he is not without self-sufficiency!

sentences.zh: 故僕志在兼濟，行在獨善，奉而始終之則為道，言而發明之則為詩。

translations.literal: Thus my aim lies in benefiting all together; my conduct lies in cultivating the self alone; keeping it from beginning to end is the Way; speaking and making it clear is poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Thus my aim lies in benefiting all together; my conduct lies in cultivating the self alone; keeping it from beginning to end is the Way; speaking and making it clear is poetry.

sentences.zh: 謂之諷諭詩，兼濟之志也；

translations.literal: Calling them satirical-remonstrance poems is the aim of benefiting all together;
translations.idiomatic: Calling them satirical-remonstrance poems is the aim of benefiting all together;

sentences.zh: 謂之閑適詩，獨善之義也。

translations.literal: calling them leisurely-contentment poems is the meaning of cultivating the self alone.
translations.idiomatic: calling them leisurely-contentment poems is the meaning of cultivating the self alone.

sentences.zh: 故覽僕詩者，知僕之道焉。

translations.literal: Thus those who read my poems know my Way.
translations.idiomatic: Thus those who read my poems know my Way.

sentences.zh: 其餘雜律詩，或誘於一時一物，發於一笑一吟，率然成章，非平生所尚者，但以親朋合散之際，取其釋恨佐歡，今銓次之間，未能刪去。

translations.literal: The rest of the miscellaneous regulated poems—sometimes tempted by one time or one thing, arising from one laugh or one chant, composed on the spur of the moment, not what I esteem in life—are only for the moment when kin and friends gather or part, taking them to release resentment and assist pleasure; in present selection and ordering I have not been able to delete them.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the miscellaneous regulated poems—sometimes tempted by one time or one thing, arising from one laugh or one chant, composed on the spur of the moment, not what I esteem in life—are only for the moment when kin and friends gather or part, taking them to release resentment and assist pleasure; in present selection and ordering I have not been able to delete them.

sentences.zh: 他時有為我編集斯文者，略之可也。

translations.literal: If another time someone compiles this writing for me, he may omit them.
translations.idiomatic: If another time someone compiles this writing for me, he may omit them.

sentences.zh: 微之，夫貴耳賤目，榮古陋今，人之大情也。

translations.literal: Zhen, to honor the ear and despise the eye, to glorify the old and despise the present—this is the great feeling of men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, to honor the ear and despise the eye, to glorify the old and despise the present—this is the great feeling of men.

sentences.zh: 僕不能遠征古舊，如近歲韋蘇州歌行，才麗之外，頗近興諷；

translations.literal: I cannot go far to cite antiquity; take in recent years Wei Suzhou's song-lines—beyond talent and beauty, they are quite near stirring satire;
translations.idiomatic: I cannot go far to cite antiquity; take in recent years Wei Yingwu's song-lines—beyond talent and beauty, they are quite near stirring satire;

sentences.zh: 其五言詩，又高雅閑淡，自成一家之體，今之秉筆者誰能及之？

translations.literal: his five-character poems again are lofty, elegant, leisurely, and plain, forming a style of their own—among those who wield the brush today, who can reach him?
translations.idiomatic: his five-character poems again are lofty, elegant, leisurely, and plain, forming a style of their own—among those who wield the brush today, who can reach him?

sentences.zh: 然當蘇州在時，人亦未甚愛重，必待身後，人始貴之。

translations.literal: Yet when Suzhou was alive, people also did not greatly love and esteem him; it had to wait until after his death before people began to value him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Suzhou was alive, people also did not greatly love and esteem him; it had to wait until after his death before people began to value him.

sentences.zh: 今僕之詩，人所愛者，悉不過雜律詩與《長恨歌》已下耳。

translations.literal: Today what people love in my poems is entirely no more than miscellaneous regulated poems and "Song of Everlasting Sorrow" and below.
translations.idiomatic: Today what people love in my poems is entirely no more than miscellaneous regulated poems and "Song of Everlasting Sorrow" and below.

sentences.zh: 時之所重，僕之所輕。

translations.literal: What the age values is what I lightly esteem.
translations.idiomatic: What the age values is what I lightly esteem.

sentences.zh: 至於諷諭者，意激而言質；

translations.literal: As for satirical-remonstrance poems, the intent is sharp and the words plain;
translations.idiomatic: As for satirical-remonstrance poems, the intent is sharp and the words plain;

sentences.zh: 閑適者，思淡而辭迂。

translations.literal: as for leisurely-contentment poems, the thought is bland and the diction circuitous.
translations.idiomatic: as for leisurely-contentment poems, the thought is bland and the diction circuitous.

sentences.zh: 以質合迂，宜人之不愛也。

translations.literal: Plain joined with circuitous—it is fitting that people do not love them.
translations.idiomatic: Plain joined with circuitous—it is fitting that people do not love them.

sentences.zh: 今所愛者，並世而生，獨足下耳。

translations.literal: Those who love them now, born in the same age—only you.
translations.idiomatic: Those who love them now, born in the same age—only you.

sentences.zh: 然百千年後，安知復無如足下者出，而知愛我詩哉？

translations.literal: Yet a hundred or a thousand years hence, who knows whether again someone like you will appear and know to love my poems?
translations.idiomatic: Yet a hundred or a thousand years hence, who knows whether again someone like you will appear and know to love my poems?

sentences.zh: 故自八九年來，與足下小通則以詩相戒，小窮則以詩相勉，索居則以詩相慰，同處則以詩相娛。

translations.literal: Thus from eight or nine years ago, with you when slightly in accord I admonish through poetry, when slightly in hardship I encourage through poetry, when living apart I console through poetry, when together I delight through poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Thus from eight or nine years ago, with you when slightly in accord I admonish through poetry, when slightly in hardship I encourage through poetry, when living apart I console through poetry, when together I delight through poetry.

sentences.zh: 知吾罪吾，率以詩也。

translations.literal: Knowing me or blaming me—in all cases it is through poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing me or blaming me—in all cases it is through poetry.

sentences.zh: 如今年春遊城南時，與足下馬上相戲，因各誦新艷小律，不雜他篇，自皇子陂歸昭國裏，叠吟遞唱，不絕聲者二十里餘。

translations.literal: Like this spring when touring south of the city, with you jesting on horseback, we each recited new and gorgeous short regulated pieces, not mixing other pieces; from Prince's Mound returning to Zhaoguo Ward, chanting and singing in turn, the sound unbroken for more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: Like this spring when touring south of the city, with you jesting on horseback, we each recited new and gorgeous short regulated pieces, not mixing other pieces; from Prince's Mound returning to Zhaoguo Ward, chanting and singing in turn, the sound unbroken for more than twenty li.

sentences.zh: 攀、李在傍，無所措口。

translations.literal: Pan and Li were at the side, with no place to put their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Pan and Li were at the side, with no place to put their mouths.

sentences.zh: 知我者以為詩仙，不知我者以為詩魔。

translations.literal: Those who knew me called me poetry immortal; those who did not know me called me poetry demon.
translations.idiomatic: Those who knew me called me poetry immortal; those who did not know me called me poetry demon.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 勞心靈，役聲氣，連朝接夕，不自知其苦，非魔而何？

translations.literal: Toiling the mind and spirit, enslaving breath and sound, connecting morning to evening, not knowing one's own suffering—is that not demon?
translations.idiomatic: Toiling the mind and spirit, enslaving breath and sound, connecting morning to evening, not knowing one's own suffering—is that not demon?

sentences.zh: 偶同人當美景，或花時宴罷，或月夜酒酣，一詠一吟，不覺老之將至。

translations.literal: By chance with companions amid fine scenery, or when the flower-season banquet ends, or when on a moonlit night the wine is deep, one chant and one recitation—before one knows it old age is near.
translations.idiomatic: By chance with companions amid fine scenery, or when the flower-season banquet ends, or when on a moonlit night the wine is deep, one chant and one recitation—before one knows it old age is near.

sentences.zh: 雖驂鸞鶴、遊蓬瀛者之適，無以加於此焉，又非仙而何？

translations.literal: Though the ease of riding paired cranes or roaming Penglai cannot be added to beyond this—again, is that not immortal?
translations.idiomatic: Though the ease of riding paired cranes or roaming Penglai cannot be added to beyond this—again, is that not immortal?

sentences.zh: 微之，微之！

translations.literal: Zhen, Zhen!
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, Zhen!

sentences.zh: 此吾所以與足下外形骸、脫蹤跡、傲軒鼎、輕人寰者，又以此也。

translations.literal: This is why I with you shed bodily form, cast off tracks, disdain regalia and tripods, and lightly esteem the human realm—again for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: This is why I with you shed bodily form, cast off tracks, disdain regalia and tripods, and lightly esteem the human realm—again for this reason.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，足下興有餘力，且欲與僕悉索還往中詩，取其尤長者，如張十八古樂府，李二十新歌行，盧、楊二秘書律詩，竇七、元八絕句，博搜精掇，編而次之，號為《元白往還集》。

translations.literal: At that time you still had surplus energy and also wished with me to search thoroughly all the poems exchanged back and forth, take the especially fine among them—like Zhang Eighteen's old ballads, Li Twenty's new song-lines, Secretaries Lu and Yang's regulated poems, Dou Seven and Yuan Eight's quatrains—search broadly, select finely, compile and arrange them, and title them "Collection of Yuan and Bai's Exchanges."
translations.idiomatic: At that time you still had surplus energy and also wished with me to search thoroughly all the poems exchanged back and forth, take the especially fine among them—like Zhang Eighteen's old ballads, Li Twenty's new song-lines, Secretaries Lu and Yang's regulated poems, Dou Seven and Yuan Eight's quatrains—search broadly, select finely, compile and arrange them, and title them "Collection of Yuan and Bai's Exchanges."

sentences.zh: 眾君子得擬議於此者，莫不踴躍欣喜，以為盛事。

translations.literal: The gentlemen who obtained a place to discuss this were all leaping with joy, taking it as a great event.
translations.idiomatic: The gentlemen who obtained a place to discuss this were all leaping with joy, taking it as a great event.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 言未終而足下左轉，不數月而僕又繼行，心期索然，何日成就？

translations.literal: Before the words were finished you were transferred left; within a few months I followed in going; the heart's expectation was desolate—what day would it be achieved?
translations.idiomatic: Before the words were finished you were transferred left; within a few months I followed in going; the heart's expectation was desolate—what day would it be achieved?

sentences.zh: 又可為之太息矣！

translations.literal: Again one may sigh deeply over this!
translations.idiomatic: Again one may sigh deeply over this!

sentences.zh: 僕常語足下，凡人為文，私於自是，不忍於割截，或失於繁多。

translations.literal: I have often told you: for any person composing writing, he is partial to his own work, unwilling to cut and trim, or errs in being too numerous.
translations.idiomatic: I have often told you: for any person composing writing, he is partial to his own work, unwilling to cut and trim, or errs in being too numerous.

sentences.zh: 其間妍媸，益又自惑。

translations.literal: Among them the beautiful and ugly—further he himself is confused.
translations.idiomatic: Among them the beautiful and ugly—further he himself is confused.

sentences.zh: 必待交友有公鑒無姑息者，討論而削奪之，然後繁簡當否，得其中矣。

translations.literal: One must wait for a friend who has fair judgment without indulgence, discuss and pare away, and only then whether prolix or concise is appropriate can reach the mean.
translations.idiomatic: One must wait for a friend who has fair judgment without indulgence, discuss and pare away, and only then whether prolix or concise is appropriate can reach the mean.

sentences.zh: 況僕與足下，為文尤患其多。

translations.literal: Moreover I with you, in writing especially fear its being too much.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I with you, in writing especially fear its being too much.

sentences.zh: 己尚病，況他人乎？

translations.literal: I myself still find it sickening—how much more others?
translations.idiomatic: I myself still find it sickening—how much more others?

sentences.zh: 今且各纂詩筆，粗為卷第，待與足下相見日，各出所有，終前志焉。

translations.literal: For now let each compile poetic drafts, roughly into fascicles; wait until the day we meet face to face, each bring out what he has, and fulfill the former aim.
translations.idiomatic: For now let each compile poetic drafts, roughly into fascicles; wait until the day we meet face to face, each bring out what he has, and fulfill the former aim.

sentences.zh: 又不知相遇是何年，相見是何地，溘然而至，則如之何？

translations.literal: Again I do not know in what year we will meet, in what place we will see each other; if suddenly it comes, then what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Again I do not know in what year we will meet, in what place we will see each other; if suddenly it comes, then what is to be done?

sentences.zh: 微之知我心哉！

translations.literal: Zhen knows my heart!
translations.idiomatic: Zhen knows my heart!

sentences.zh: 潯陽臘月，江風苦寒，歲暮鮮歡，夜長少睡。

translations.literal: Xunyang, twelfth month; river wind bitter cold; year's end with little joy; night long and little sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Xunyang, twelfth month; river wind bitter cold; year's end with little joy; night long and little sleep.

sentences.zh: 引筆鋪紙，悄然燈前，有念則書，言無銓次。

translations.literal: I draw the brush and spread paper, quietly before the lamp; when there is a thought I write; the words are without order of selection.
translations.idiomatic: I draw the brush and spread paper, quietly before the lamp; when there is a thought I write; the words are without order of selection.

sentences.zh: 勿以繁雜為倦，且以代一夕之話言也。

translations.literal: Do not weary at prolixity; let it stand in place of one evening's conversation.
translations.idiomatic: Do not weary at prolixity; let it stand in place of one evening's conversation.

sentences.zh: 居易自敘如此，文士以為信然。

translations.literal: Juyi's self-account is as above; literary men regarded it as trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi's self-account is as above; literary men regarded it as trustworthy.

sentences.zh: 十三年冬，量移忠州刺史。

translations.literal: In the winter of the thirteenth year he was transferred in grade to governor of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the thirteenth year he was transferred in grade to governor of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 自潯陽浮江上峽。

translations.literal: From Xunyang he floated upriver on the Yangtze into the gorges.
translations.idiomatic: From Xunyang he floated upriver on the Yangtze into the gorges.

sentences.zh: 十四年三月，元稹會居易於峽口，停舟夷陵三日。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourteenth year Yuan Zhen met Juyi at the gorge mouth and moored their boats at Yiling for three days.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourteenth year Yuan Zhen met Juyi at the gorge mouth and moored their boats at Yiling for three days.

sentences.zh: 時季弟行簡從行，三人於峽州西二十里黃牛峽口石洞中，置酒賦詩，戀戀不能訣。

translations.literal: At the time his younger brother Xingjian was traveling with him; the three men at a stone cave twenty li west of Yiling at the mouth of Yellow Ox Gorge set out wine and composed poems, reluctant to part and unable to take leave.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his younger brother Xingjian was traveling with him; the three men at a stone cave twenty li west of Yiling at the mouth of Yellow Ox Gorge set out wine and composed poems, reluctant to part and unable to take leave.

sentences.zh: 南賓郡當峽路之深險處也，花木多奇。

translations.literal: Nanbin prefecture lies at the deepest peril of the gorge route, and its flowers and trees are mostly extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Nanbin prefecture lies at the deepest peril of the gorge route, and its flowers and trees are mostly extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 居易在郡，為《木蓮荔枝圖》，寄朝中親友，各記其狀曰：「荔枝生巴、峽間，形圓如帷蓋。

translations.literal: While in the prefecture Juyi composed "Illustrations of Magnolia and Lychee" and sent them to kin and friends at court, each recording their forms, which read: "The lychee grows between Ba and the gorges; its form is round like a canopy.
translations.idiomatic: While in the prefecture Juyi composed "Illustrations of Magnolia and Lychee" and sent them to kin and friends at court, each recording their forms, which read, "The lychee grows between Ba and the gorges; its form is round like a canopy.

sentences.zh: 葉如桂，冬青；

translations.literal: Its leaves are like cassia, evergreen in winter;
translations.idiomatic: Its leaves are like cassia, evergreen in winter;

sentences.zh: 華如橘，春榮；

translations.literal: Its flowers are like the orange, blooming in spring;
translations.idiomatic: Its blossoms resemble the orange, opening in spring;

sentences.zh: 實如丹，夏熟。

translations.literal: Its fruit is like cinnabar, ripening in summer.
translations.idiomatic: Its fruit is like cinnabar, ripening in summer.

sentences.zh: 朵如蒲萄，核如枇杷，殼如紅繒，膜如紫綃，瓤肉瑩白如雪，漿液甘酸如醴酪。

translations.literal: Its clusters are like grapes, its pit like loquat, its shell like red silk gauze, its membrane like purple gauze, its flesh lustrous white as snow, its juice sweet and sour like fermented milk.
translations.idiomatic: Clusters hang like grapes; the pit resembles a loquat; the shell is red silk gauze, the membrane purple gauze; the flesh gleams white as snow; the juice is sweet-sour as cultured curds.

sentences.zh: 大略如此，其實過之。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking it is thus, and in reality it surpasses this description.
translations.idiomatic: That is the general picture—and the fruit itself surpasses it.

sentences.zh: 若離本枝，一日而色變，二日而香變，三日而味變，四五日外，色香味盡去矣。」

translations.literal: If separated from its branch, in one day its color changes, in two days its fragrance changes, in three days its flavor changes, and beyond four or five days its color, fragrance, and flavor are all gone."
translations.idiomatic: If separated from its branch, in one day its color changes, in two days its fragrance changes, in three days its flavor changes, and beyond four or five days its color, fragrance, and flavor are all gone."

sentences.zh: 「木蓮大者高四五丈，巴民呼為黃心樹，經冬不雕。

translations.literal: "The magnolia large ones reach four or five zhang in height; the people of Ba call it the yellow-heart tree, and it does not wither through winter.
translations.idiomatic: "The magnolia grows as tall as four or five zhang; Ba people call it the yellow-heart tree and it never sheds in winter.

sentences.zh: 身如青楊，有白文。

translations.literal: Its trunk is like green poplar, with white markings.
translations.idiomatic: Its trunk is like green poplar, with white markings.

sentences.zh: 葉如桂，厚大無脊。

translations.literal: Its leaves are like cassia, thick and large without a midrib.
translations.idiomatic: Its leaves are like cassia, thick and large without a midrib.

sentences.zh: 花如蓮，香色艷膩皆同，房獨蕊有異。

translations.literal: Its flowers are like the lotus; fragrance, color, and lush beauty are all the same, only the calyx and solitary pistil differ.
translations.idiomatic: Its flowers are like the lotus; fragrance, color, and lush beauty are all the same, only the calyx and solitary pistil differ.

sentences.zh: 四月初始開，自開迨謝，僅二十日。

translations.literal: It first opens in the fourth month; from opening until fading is only twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: It first opens in the fourth month; from opening until fading is only twenty days.

sentences.zh: 元和十四年夏，命道士毋丘元志寫之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourteenth year of Yuanhe he ordered the Daoist priest Wuqiu Yuanzhi to paint them.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourteenth year of Yuanhe he ordered the Daoist priest Wuqiu Yuanzhi to paint them.

sentences.zh: 惜其遐僻，因以三絕賦之。」

translations.literal: Pitying their remote seclusion, he therefore composed a fu in three parts on them."
translations.idiomatic: Pitying their remote seclusion, he therefore composed a fu in three parts on them."

sentences.zh: 有「天教拋擲在深山」之句，鹹傳於都下，好事者喧然模寫。

translations.literal: There was the line "Heaven decreed them cast away deep in the mountains," which all transmitted in the capital, and enthusiasts clamored to copy it.
translations.idiomatic: Among its lines was "Heaven cast them off deep in the mountains," which swept through the capital until enthusiasts clamored to copy it.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，召還京師，拜司門員外郎。

translations.literal: That winter he was summoned back to the capital and appointed vice director of the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was summoned back to the capital and appointed vice director of the Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉主客郎中、知制誥，加朝散大夫，始著緋。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to director of the Guests Bureau with charge of drafting edicts, granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and for the first time wore crimson.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to director of the Guests Bureau with charge of drafting edicts, granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and for the first time wore crimson.

sentences.zh: 時元稹亦征還為尚書郎、知制誥，同在綸閣。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Zhen was also summoned back as director in a ministry with charge of drafting edicts, and both were together in the drafting pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Zhen was also summoned back as director in a ministry with charge of drafting edicts, and both were together in the drafting pavilion.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年三月，受詔與中書舍人王起覆，試禮部侍郎錢徽下及第人鄭朗等一十四人。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Changqing he received an edict together with Drafting Academician Wang Qi to review the fourteen men including Zheng Lang whom Vice Director of Rites Qian Hui had passed in the lower examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Changqing he received an edict together with Drafting Academician Wang Qi to review the fourteen men including Zheng Lang whom Vice Director of Rites Qian Hui had passed in the lower examination.

sentences.zh: 十月，轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was transferred to drafting academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was transferred to drafting academician.

sentences.zh: 十一月，穆宗親試制舉人，又與賈餗、陳岵為考策官。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Emperor Muzong personally tested special-examination candidates, and Juyi again served with Jia Su and Chen Hu as policy examiners.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Emperor Muzong personally tested special-examination candidates, and Juyi again served with Jia Su and Chen Hu as policy examiners.

sentences.zh: 凡朝廷文字之職，無不首居其選，然多為排擯，不得用其才。

translations.literal: Of all court posts for written composition, none failed to place him first in selection, yet he was often ostracized and could not employ his talents.
translations.idiomatic: Of all court posts for written composition, none failed to place him first in selection, yet he was often ostracized and could not employ his talents.

sentences.zh: 時天子荒縱不法，執政非其人，制御乖方，河朔復亂。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was dissolute and lawless, those in power were not the right men, regulation and control were misaligned, and Hebei again fell into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Son of Heaven was dissolute and lawless, those in power were not the right men, regulation and control were misaligned, and Hebei again fell into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 居易累上疏論其事，天子不能用，乃求外任。

translations.literal: Juyi submitted memorial after memorial discussing these matters; the Son of Heaven could not employ them, and Juyi then sought an outer appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi submitted memorial after memorial discussing these matters; the Son of Heaven could not employ them, and Juyi then sought an outer appointment.

sentences.zh: 七月，除杭州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was appointed governor of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was appointed governor of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄而元稹罷相，自馮翊轉浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: Before long Yuan Zhen was removed as chief councilor and transferred from Fengyi to surveillance commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuan Zhen was removed as chief councilor and transferred from Fengyi to surveillance commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 交契素深，杭、越鄰境，篇詠往來，不間旬浹。

translations.literal: Their bond of friendship had always been deep; Hang and Yue were neighboring jurisdictions, and poems exchanged in gift and response came without a break of ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Their bond of friendship had always been deep; Hang and Yue were neighboring jurisdictions, and poems exchanged in gift and response came without a break of ten days.

sentences.zh: 嘗會於境上，數日而別。

translations.literal: They once met on the border and parted after several days.
translations.idiomatic: They once met on the border and parted after several days.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，除太子左庶子，分司東都。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was appointed Left Mentor to the Heir Apparent with duty at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was appointed Left Mentor to the Heir Apparent with duty at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 寶歷中，復出為蘇州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Baoli era he was again sent out as governor of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baoli era he was again sent out as governor of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，征拜秘書監，賜金紫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, Juyi was summoned as Director of the Palace Library and granted the gold-purple seal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, Juyi was summoned as Director of the Palace Library and granted the gold-purple seal.

sentences.zh: 九月上誕節，召居易與僧惟澄、道土趙常盈對御講論於麟德殿。

translations.literal: On the imperial birthday in the ninth month he summoned Juyi together with the monk Weicheng and the Daoist Zhao Changying to lecture before the throne in the Qinde Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the imperial birthday in the ninth month he summoned Juyi together with the monk Weicheng and the Daoist Zhao Changying to lecture before the throne in the Qinde Hall.

sentences.zh: 居易論難鋒起，辭辨泉註，上疑宿構，深嗟挹之。

translations.literal: Juyi's disputations rose like spears and his eloquence poured like a spring; the emperor suspected he had prepared them beforehand and deeply sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi's rebuttals flashed like spears and his eloquence poured forth; the emperor suspected prepared answers and marveled at his mastery.

sentences.zh: 太和二年正月，轉刑部侍郎，封晉陽縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Taihe he was transferred to vice minister of Punishments, enfeoffed as Baron of Jinyang with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Taihe he was transferred to vice minister of Punishments, enfeoffed as Baron of Jinyang with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 三年，稱病東歸，求為分司官，尋除太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the third year he claimed illness and returned east, requesting a duty-at-large post, and soon was appointed Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he claimed illness and returned east, requesting a duty-at-large post, and soon was appointed Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 居易初對策高第，擢入翰林，蒙英主特達顧遇，頗欲奮厲效報，茍致身於訏謨之地，則兼濟生靈，蓄意未果，望風為當路者所擠，流徙江湖。

translations.literal: When Juyi first answered policy at the top grade and was elevated into the Hanlin Academy, he received the special favor of an enlightened sovereign and wished earnestly to repay it; if he could reach a place of state counsel, he would benefit the people as well—but his intent was not realized; seeing the wind, those in power ostracized him and he was cast to the rivers and lakes.
translations.idiomatic: When Juyi first topped the policy examination and entered the Hanlin, an enlightened sovereign singled him out for favor and he burned to repay it—hoping to reach the council chamber and benefit the people at once. His intent never ripened; those in power read the wind and crowded him out until he drifted on rivers and lakes.

sentences.zh: 四五年間，幾淪蠻瘴。

translations.literal: Within four or five years he nearly succumbed to miasma in the southern wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Within four or five years he nearly succumbed to miasma in the southern wilds.

sentences.zh: 自是宦情衰落，無意於出處，唯以逍遙自得，吟詠情性為事。

translations.literal: From this his official ambition declined and he had no mind for advancement or withdrawal, taking only free roaming and self-contentment and chanting to express his nature as his affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From this his official ambition declined and he had no mind for advancement or withdrawal, taking only free roaming and self-contentment and chanting to express his nature as his affairs.

sentences.zh: 太和已後，李宗閔、李德裕朋黨事起，是非排陷，朝升暮黜，天子亦無如之何。

translations.literal: After Taihe, the factional affairs of Li Zongmin and Li Deyu arose; right and wrong were used to entrap one another, and men were elevated at dawn and demoted at dusk—the Son of Heaven likewise could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: After Taihe, the factional affairs of Li Zongmin and Li Deyu arose; right and wrong were used to entrap one another, and men were elevated at dawn and demoted at dusk—the Son of Heaven likewise could do nothing about it.

sentences.zh: 楊穎士、楊虞卿與宗閔善，居易妻，穎士從父妹也。

translations.literal: Yang Yingshi and Yang Yuqing were friendly with Zongmin; Juyi's wife was Yingshi's cousin on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yingshi and Yang Yuqing were friendly with Zongmin; Juyi's wife was Yingshi's cousin on the father's side.

sentences.zh: 居易愈不自安，懼以黨人見斥，乃求致身散地，冀於遠害。

translations.literal: Juyi grew all the more ill at ease, fearing rejection as a faction member, and sought to place himself in a scattered post, hoping to escape harm from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Juyi grew all the more ill at ease, fearing rejection as a faction member, and sought to place himself in a scattered post, hoping to escape harm from afar.

sentences.zh: 凡所居官，未嘗終秩，率以病免，固求分務，識者多之。

translations.literal: In every office he held he never completed a full term, generally leaving on grounds of illness, firmly requesting duty-at-large posts—those who understood approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: In every office he held he never completed a full term, generally leaving on grounds of illness, firmly requesting duty-at-large posts—those who understood approved of this.

sentences.zh: 五年，除河南尹。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed metropolitan intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed metropolitan intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 七年，復授太子賓客分司。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was again appointed Mentor to the Heir Apparent with duty at large.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was again appointed Mentor to the Heir Apparent with duty at large.

sentences.zh: 初，居易罷杭州，歸洛陽。

translations.literal: At first, when Juyi left Hangzhou, he returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Juyi left Hangzhou, he returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 於履道里得故散騎常侍楊憑宅，竹木池館，有林泉之致。

translations.literal: At Lüdao Lane he obtained the former residence of the Regular Attendant Yang Ping, with bamboo, trees, ponds, and lodges possessing the charm of forests and springs.
translations.idiomatic: At Lüdao Lane he obtained the former residence of the Regular Attendant Yang Ping, with bamboo, trees, ponds, and lodges possessing the charm of forests and springs.

sentences.zh: 家妓樊素、蠻子者，能歌善舞。

translations.literal: His household entertainers Fansu and Manzi could sing and dance well.
translations.idiomatic: His household entertainers Fansu and Manzi could sing and dance well.

sentences.zh: 居易既以尹正罷歸，每獨酌賦詠於舟中，因為《池上篇》曰：東都風土水木之勝在東南偏，東南之勝在履道里，裏之勝在西北隅，西闬北垣第一第，即白氏叟樂天退老之地。

translations.literal: Juyi, having left office as capital intendant and returned home, would often drink alone and compose verses in his boat; he therefore wrote his "Essay on the Pool," which read: The excellence of the Eastern Capital's terrain, waters, and trees lies in the southeastern quarter; the excellence of the southeast lies in Lüdao Ward; the excellence within the ward lies in the northwest corner—the first residence at the western gate and northern wall, the place where the old gentleman of the Bai clan, Juyi, retired in old age.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office as capital intendant and returning home, he would often drink alone and compose verses in his boat; he therefore wrote his "Essay on the Pool," which read: In the Eastern Capital, the finest scenery of land and water lay in the southeast; the choicest part of the southeast was Lüdao Ward; and the choicest spot in the ward was the northwest corner—the first mansion on the western lane and northern wall, where the Bai clansman Juyi lived out his retirement.

sentences.zh: 地方十七畝，屋室三之一，水五之一，竹九之一，而島樹橋道間之。

translations.literal: The grounds covered seventeen mu; buildings occupied one third, water one fifth, bamboo one ninth, and islands, trees, bridges, and paths were interspersed among them.
translations.idiomatic: The estate covered seventeen mu: a third in buildings, a fifth in water, a ninth in bamboo, with islands, trees, bridges, and paths distributed throughout.

sentences.zh: 初樂天既為主，喜且曰：「雖有池臺，無粟不能守也」，乃作池東粟廩。

translations.literal: At first, once Juyi had become master of the place, he said with delight: "Though there are pools and terraces, without grain one cannot sustain them," and so built a grain storehouse east of the pool.
translations.idiomatic: When Juyi first took possession, he said happily, "Though one has pools and terraces, without grain one cannot keep them up," and built a granary east of the pool.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「雖有子弟，無書不能訓也。」

translations.literal: He said again: "Though there are sons and younger kin, without books one cannot instruct them."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Though one has sons and kin, without books one cannot teach them."

sentences.zh: 乃作池北書庫。

translations.literal: And so he built a book repository north of the pool.
translations.idiomatic: and built a library north of the pool.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「雖有賓朋，無琴酒不能娛也」，乃作池西琴亭，加石樽焉。

translations.literal: He said again: "Though there are guests and friends, without zither and wine one cannot enjoy oneself," and so built a zither pavilion west of the pool, adding stone wine jars.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Though one has guests and friends, without zither and wine one cannot entertain," and built a zither pavilion west of the pool, with stone wine vessels added.

sentences.zh: 樂天罷杭州刺史，得天竺石一、華亭鶴二以歸。

translations.literal: When Juyi left the post of prefect of Hangzhou, he obtained one stone from Tianzhu and two cranes from Huating and brought them home.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving his post as prefect of Hangzhou, Juyi brought home one stone from Tianzhu and two cranes from Huating.

sentences.zh: 始作西平橋，開環池路。

translations.literal: He then built the West Flat Bridge and opened the circuit road around the pool.
translations.idiomatic: He then built West Flat Bridge and opened a circuit road around the pool.

sentences.zh: 罷蘇州刺史時，得太湖石五、白蓮、折腰菱、青板舫以歸，又作中高橋，通三島逕。

translations.literal: When he left the post of prefect of Suzhou, he obtained five Lake Tai stones, white lotuses, waist-bent water chestnuts, and a blue-planked boat and brought them home; he also built the Middle High Bridge, linking a path to the three islands.
translations.idiomatic: When he left the prefecture of Suzhou, he returned with five Taihu stones, white lotuses, bent-neck water chestnuts, and a blue-planked boat, and built Middle High Bridge to connect a path to the three islands.

sentences.zh: 罷刑部侍郎時，有粟千斛，書一車，洎臧獲之習管磬弦歌者指百以歸。

translations.literal: When he left the post of vice minister of justice, he had a thousand hu of grain, a cartload of books, and roughly a hundred servants trained in pipes, chimes, zithers, and song who returned with him.
translations.idiomatic: When he stepped down as vice minister of justice, he had a thousand hu of grain, a cartload of books, and about a hundred household servants skilled in pipes, chimes, strings, and song.

sentences.zh: 先是潁川陳孝仙與釀酒法，味甚佳；

translations.literal: Earlier, Chen Xiaoxian of Yingchuan had given him a brewing method; the flavor was excellent;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chen Xiaoxian of Yingchuan had taught him a brewing method of excellent flavor;

sentences.zh: 博陵崔晦叔與琴，韻甚清；

translations.literal: Cui Huishu of Boling had given him a zither; its tone was very clear;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huishu of Boling had given him a zither of very clear tone;

sentences.zh: 蜀客姜發授《秋思》，聲甚淡；

translations.literal: the Shu guest Jiang Fa had taught him "Autumn Thoughts"; the sound was very subdued;
translations.idiomatic: the Shu visitor Jiang Fa had taught him "Autumn Thoughts," its sound very subdued;

sentences.zh: 弘農楊貞一與青石三，方長平滑，可以坐臥。

translations.literal: Yang Zhenyi of Hongnong had given him three blue stones, square, long, and smooth, on which one could sit or lie.
translations.idiomatic: and Yang Zhenyi of Hongnong had given him three blue stones, square, long, and smooth enough to sit or lie upon.

sentences.zh: 太和三年夏，樂天始得請為太子賓客，分秩於洛下，息躬於池上。

translations.literal: In summer of the third year of Taihe, Juyi first obtained permission to serve as guest of the heir apparent, took up his stipend at Luoyang, and rested his person at the pool.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Taihe 3, Juyi was at last permitted to serve as guest of the heir apparent, drew his stipend at Luoyang, and rested at his poolside estate.

sentences.zh: 凡三任所得，四人所與，洎吾不才身，今率為池中物。

translations.literal: Everything gained from three offices, given by four men, and extending to my unworthy person—all are now entirely possessions of the pool.
translations.idiomatic: Everything accumulated across three offices, bestowed by four friends, together with my own unworthy self—all are now part of the pool estate.

sentences.zh: 每至池風春，池月秋，水香蓮開之旦，露清鶴唳之夕，拂楊石，舉陳酒，援崔琴，彈《秋思》，頹然自適，不知其他。

translations.literal: Whenever it was spring breezes over the pool, autumn moon on the pool, the morning of fragrant water and opening lotuses, or the evening of clear dew and crane cries, he would brush the Yang stones, raise Chen's wine, take up Cui's zither, play "Autumn Thoughts," and lapse contentedly into self-sufficiency, unaware of anything else.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever spring breezes stirred over the pool or autumn moonlight bathed it—on mornings when the water smelled sweet and lotuses opened, or evenings when dew lay clear and cranes called—he would brush the Yang stones, pour Chen's wine, take up Cui's zither, and play "Autumn Thoughts," sinking into contentment and forgetting everything else.

sentences.zh: 酒酣琴罷，又命樂童登中島亭，含奏《霓裳散序》，聲隨風飄，或凝或散，悠揚於竹煙波月之際者久之。

translations.literal: When the wine was deep and the zither done, he would also command music youths to ascend Middle Island Pavilion and perform in ensemble the "Prelude to Rainbow Skirts"; the sound drifted with the wind, now gathering, now dispersing, lingering long amid bamboo, mist, waves, and moon.
translations.idiomatic: When wine ran deep and the zither fell silent, he would have young musicians climb Middle Island Pavilion to perform the "Prelude to Rainbow Skirts"; the sound drifted on the wind, now lingering, now scattering, rising and falling long among bamboo, mist, waves, and moonlight.

sentences.zh: 曲未竟，而樂天陶然石上矣。

translations.literal: Before the piece was finished, Juyi was already blissfully drowsing on the stones.
translations.idiomatic: Before the piece ended, Juyi had already drifted contentedly asleep on the stones.

sentences.zh: 睡起偶詠，非詩非賦，阿龜握筆，因題石間。

translations.literal: Waking from sleep he chanted casually; it was neither poem nor fu; A'gui took the brush and inscribed it among the stones.
